jobs.title: Support Group Lead
jobs.description:
Our mission

We're making Africa the first cashless continent.

In 2017, over half the population in Sub-Saharan Africa had no bank account. That's for good reason—the fees are too high, the closest branch can be miles away, and nobody takes cards. Without access to financial institutions, people are forced to keep their savings under the mattress. Small business owners rely on lenders who charge extortionate rates. Parents spend hours waiting in line to pay school fees in cash.

We're solving this by building financial services that just work: no account fees, instantly available, and accepted everywhere. In places where electricity, water and roads don't always work, you can still send money with Wave. In 2017, we launched a mobile app in Senegal for cash deposit, withdrawal, and peer-to-peer and business payments. Now, we have millions of users across 9 countries and are growing fast.

Our goal is to make Africa the first cashless continent and that's where you come in...

How you'll help us achieve it

As Support Group lead, you will manage and lead a team of customer support representatives. You will set goals and targets for your team, monitor team performance, and ensure that the team provides excellent customer service and addresses customer issues promptly and efficiently.

In this role, you'll:

• Manage the customer support day-to-day functions of your team.

• Respond and escalate customer support issues.

• Implement customer support processes to enhance customer satisfaction.

• Formulate and revise customer support policies and promote their implementation.

• Inform the team of all new information related to products, procedures, and trends.

• Assess support statistics and prepare detailed reports on the findings.

• Delivering performance evaluations and following the disciplinary process according to company policy.

• Have 1-on-1s every month with the customer support representatives assigned to you.

• Report relevant information to support team leads to ensure the service functions effectively.

• Assess Support representatives monthly.

• Listen to phone calls and improve quality.

Key details

• Location: Kotu, The Gambia

• Work authorisation in The Gambia is required.

• This is a permanent position.

• Our salaries are competitive and calculated using a transparent formula.

• We offer generous health insurance for yourself and your dependents.

• We support working parents - we offer generous parental leave policies (26 weeks for mothers and 4 weeks for fathers) and subsidized childcare when you return to work.

• We help you live your fullest life now! We subsidize gym memberships and fitness classes.

• Airtime reimbursement.

• Free food and a beautiful office space.

Requirements

• Fluency in English and local languages.

• At least one year of experience as a customer support representative (call center, customer service).

• One year of experience as a Customer Service Manager.

• Ability to work flexible hours.

You might be a good fit if you

• Demonstrate tenacity and a willingness to go the distance to get something done: work flexible hours.

• Can think strategically and lead.

• Are comfortable defaulting to over-communication and overreaching in coordination.

• Are excessively detail-oriented and seek to achieve excellence in everything you do.

• Are client-oriented and have strong interpersonal skills.

• Are a diplomatic speaker.

• Have a teamwork spirit.

• Are available every day of the week, including weekends, if necessary.

• You have significant experience managing a large team of Support Representatives.

Our team

• We have a rapidly growing in-country team in Senegal, Côte d'Ivoire, Mali, Burkina Faso, The Gambia, Uganda, Niger, Sierra Leone, and Cameroon plus remote team members spread across the world.

• We're deeply passionate about our mission of bringing radically affordable financial services to the people who need them most.

• We foster autonomy for our employees. You'll own your projects at every stage, from understanding the problem to monitoring your solution in production.

• We raised the largest Series A in Africa in 2021. Our world-class investors, include Founders Fund, Sequoia Heritage, Stripe, Ribbit Capital, Y Combinator, and Partech Africa.

• We are on Y Combinator's top companies by revenue.

How to apply

Fill out the form below, and upload a resume in English and a cover letter describing your interest in Wave and the role.

We review applications frequently and recommend that you apply to the role that most closely aligns with your skills, experience and career goals.

Wave is an equal-opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

jobs.title: Medical Assistant - Urology Full time Days
jobs.description:
Monday - Friday: must be flexible with work hours and available to work between the hours of 7am - 7pm

The Medical Assistant reflects the mission, vision, and values of Northwestern Medicine, adheres to the organization’s Code of Ethics and Corporate Compliance Program, and complies with all relevant policies, procedures, guidelines and all other regulatory and accreditation standards.

The Medical Assistant is a member of the health care team primarily responsible for providing support to physicians, nurses, and other licensed medical staff by facilitating efficient patient flow, assisting with various patient care activities, and performing related administrative functions. The Medical Assistant is responsible for ensuring efficient patient flow through the clinic; maintaining neat, clean and safe patient care areas; promoting patient satisfaction by interacting with patients in a professional, friendly manner; safeguarding patient confidentiality.

Responsibilities:

• Assures efficient patient flow through the site: Escorts patient to exam room, identifies patient with 2 identifiers and prepares patient for examination. Obtains accurate vital signs, per organization standards. Documents reason for visit and updates/confirms, allergies, smoking history and pharmacy information. Promptly informs the provider and registered nurse of any significant change in vital signs or acute symptoms. Anticipates/sets up equipment or supplies needed for visit. Cleans and prepares exam room for next patient. Responds to needs to expedite visits and maintain flow of patients and prioritize tasks accordingly.

• Assists practitioner with medical and surgical procedures in accordance with established protocols such as: Electrocardiogram (ECG), venipuncture, immunizations, setting up procedure trays, specimen collection and/or Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA) waived testing as directed by Provider.

• Provides high quality care by: Prepares and stocks all exam rooms in treatment area by following established protocols for disinfecting and sterilizing equipment and instruments. Participates in environmental safety rounds. Maintains vaccine/medication inventory. Monitors and maintains equipment and instruments according to clinic guidelines. Assists in ordering supplies and correctly disposes of all expired items. Adheres to office opening and closing procedures.

• Functions as an integral part of the patient care team and promotes patient satisfaction by interacting with patients in a professional, friendly manner: Accepts and performs delegated responsibilities in a positive manner. Offers assistance to others. Attends and participates in staff meetings. Communicates appropriately and effectively with patients and patient care team (in the office and on the phone)

• Performs delegated procedures common to the specialty area in a safe, effective, and efficient manner (see specialty practice addendum)

• Performs all other duties as assigned by the Supervisor or Manager

Required:

• High school diploma or GED.
• Current certification in one of the below or must have written proof of meeting candidate eligibility requirements for writing one of the five eligible certification exams (AAMA, AMT, NCCT, NHA, NRCMA)Accepted documentation:New MA Graduates within six (6) months from date of graduation from an MA Program must submit: a letter from the school or a letter from the certifying bodyNon-Certified MAs or new graduates past six (6) months from date of graduation from an MA program must submit: a letter from the certifying bodyWithin first six months of employment, will complete one of the following certifications after up to two test attempts:Certified Medical Assistant (CMA) through American Association of Medical Assistants (AAMA)Registered Medical Assistant (RMA) through American Medical Technologists (AMT) orNational Certified Medical Assistant (NCMA) through the National Center for Competency Testing (NCCT)Certified Clinical Medical Assistant (CCMA) through the National Healthcareer Association (NHA)Nationally Registered Certified Medical Assistant (NRCMA) through the National Association for Health Professionals (NAHP)Signed acknowledgement during onboarding that certification must be attained within six (6) months, as a condition of employment
• American Heart Association accredited Basic Life Support (BLS/CPR) certification.
• Zero (0) to two (2) years’ experience in a relevant role.
• Strong computer skills.

Preferred:

• Completion of accredited Medical Assistant training program.
• One to two years of ambulatory care experience.
• Experience with electronic medical record.

Northwestern Medicine is an equal opportunity employer (disability, VETS) and does not discriminate in hiring or employment on the basis of age, sex, race, color, religion, national origin, gender identity, veteran status, disability, sexual orientation or any other protected status.

Background Check

Northwestern Medicine conducts a background check that includes criminal history on newly hired team members and, at times, internal transfers. If you are offered a position with us, you will be required to complete an authorization and disclosure form that gives Northwestern Medicine permission to run the background check.  Results are evaluated on a case-by-case basis, and we follow all local, state, and federal laws, including the Illinois Health Care Worker Background Check Act.

Artificial Intelligence Disclosure

Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools may be used in some portions of the candidate review process for this position, however, all employment decisions will be made by a person.

Benefits

We offer a wide range of benefits that provide employees with tools and resources to improve their physical, emotional, and financial well-being while providing protection for unexpected life events.

Click on or copy and paste URL to your browser to view detailed benefits information

NorthwesternMedicine Career Page

https://jobs.nm.org/benefits

Please refer to the Benefits Eligibility by Employment Classification to determine benefits eligibility for job postings.

If sign-on bonus is included in a job posting eligibility is as followed: Internal employees and rehires who left Northwestern Medicine within 1 year are not eligible for the sign-on bonus. Exception: New graduate internal employees seeking their first licensed clinical position as a Registered Nurse at NM may be eligible.

A kifli.hu http://kifli.hu-nál a logisztika és az ellátási lánc nem a háttérben meghúzódó folyamat, hanem a vásárlói élményünk szive

A raktári operációnk gyors, adatalapú és folyamatosan fejlődik. Ebben a környezetben az Area Manager nem egy irodában ülő megfigyelő: te vagy a logisztikai központ egy meghatározott területének igazi gazdája, aki kézben tartja a napi teljesítményt, és motiválja a csapatot a legjobb eredmények elérésére.

Olyan vezetőt keresünk, aki szeret jelen lenni a folyamatok sűrűjében, jól igazodik el a mutatók (KPI-ok) világában, és készen áll arra, hogy a csoportvezetőkből és raktári munkatársakból a legjobbat hozza ki. Ez a pozíció kiváló ugródeszka a további vezetői fejlődéshez a gyorsan növekvő e-kereskedelmi szektorban.

Miért izgalmas ez a pozíció?

 - Valódi felelősség és hatás: Egy teljes operatív terület működéséért, biztonságáért és teljesítményéért felelsz, döntéseid azonnal meglátszanak az eredményekben.

 - Közvetlen csapatépítés: Nemcsak irányítod, hanem fejleszted is a munkatársakat, alakítva a felelősségteljes és elkötelezett kultúrát.

 - Folyamatos fejlődési lehetőség: Egy dinamikusan skálázódó, modern logisztikai környezetben léphetsz előre a vezetői karrierlétrán.

 - Keresztfunkcionális együttműködés: Szorosan együttdolgozol a munkavédelmi, automatizációs, HR, IT és folyamatfejlesztési csapattal.

 - Problémamegoldás élesben: Nem sablonos feladataid lesznek; a napi operatív kihívásokat feltárod, és fenntartható megoldásokat vezetsz be.

 Mi lesz a feladatod

 - Irányítod és biztosítod az adott terület napi operatív működését, elerve a biztonsági, minőségi és termelékenységi mutatókat (KPI-ok).

 - Vezeted, motiválod és fejleszted a területen dolgozó munkatársakat.

 - Támogatod a biztonsági kultúrát: példamutatással, proaktív beavatkozásokkal és rendszeres auditokkal garantálod a munkavédelmi szabályok betartását.

 - Elemzed az operatív problémák kiváltó okait, és hosszú távú, hatékony megoldásokat léptetsz életbe.

 - Aktívan hozzájárulsz a munkaerő-tervezéshez, a folyamatok optimalizálásához és a hatékonyságnövelő kezdeményezésekhez.

 - Szorosan együttműködsz a társfőosztályokkal (automatizáció, karbantartás, operációs kiválóság, pénzügy) a működési akadályok elhárításában.

 - Biztosítod a munkaügyi jogszabályok, a belső működési eljárások és a vállalati előírások teljes körű betartását.

Kit keresünk

 - Tapasztalat: 1–3 év embereket vezetői, logisztikai, gyártási vagy operációs területen szerzett tapasztalat.

 - Vezetői attitűd: Erős határozottság, kiváló kommunikációs készség és képesség a csapatok motiválására dinamikus, gyors tempójú környezetben.

 - Adat- és KPI-szemlélet: Otthonosan mozgsz az adatelemzésben, és tudod, hogyan kell a teljesítménymutatókat a gyakorlati működés szolgálatába állítani.

 - Nyelvtudás: Kommunikációképes angol nyelvtudás.

 - Rugalmasság: A logisztika pörög – nyitottság a több műszakos munkarendre, beleértve a hétvégi és ünnepnapi műszakokat is. (Délelőtt: 04:00-14:15
   Délután: 13:30-23:15)

 - Iskolai végzettség: Legalább középfokú végzettség (felsőfokú tanulmányok vagy diplomás háttér előny).

Előnyt jelent:

 - Felsőfokú végzettség, MBA vagy logisztikai/üzleti képzettség.

 - E-kereskedelmi, raktárirányítási (WMS) vagy ellátási lánc környezetben szerzett tapasztalat.
   
   
   
   Amit kínálunk:
   

 - Versenyképes jövedelem

 - Fiatalos, barátságos és vidám csapat

 - Folyamatos fejlődési lehetőség scale-up környezetben

• Phone and company vehicle for business travel

jobs.title: Forward Deployed Engineer
jobs.description:
ABOUT US

Higharc is a VC-backed startup that is changing how new homes are designed and built. Join a founding team who’ve shipped products for Autodesk, Electronic Arts, Nike, and Apple. We have raised over $175M with support from top-notch venture capital firms and more than 18 strategic investors: industry leaders in construction, building products manufacturing, and distribution.



Higharc is seeking a Forward Deployed Engineer to join as one of the founding roles on our new Forward Deployed team. You'll work embedded alongside a large production homebuilder to turn plans into actionable data.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

A homebuilder's plan library is the product data behind its entire business — and at enterprise scale, that data is almost entirely unstructured. Plans live as drawing sets scattered across semi-autonomous divisions, renamed and re-numbered as they move. Nobody can say with confidence which plans are duplicates, how many versions of a given home exist, or what actually varies between them.

Higharc converts those catalogs into structured, queryable plan data, and builds the analysis on top of it: searchable plan libraries with agent-enabled natural-language search, geometric similarity scoring that surfaces plans which have forked under different names, structured mapping of what varies across a library, and classification that makes consolidation decisions possible. You'll build what gets shipped in the field.

This role is for someone who wants to build against real, messy data in front of the customer, not two abstractions removed from it. 

Expect to:

 - Embed with HQ, regional, and division teams to run technical discovery — profile plan assets, assess data quality, and reverse-engineer how each division's drawing sets encode variation

 - Build and ship the searchable plan library, analytics dashboard, and agent-enabled natural-language search — own the pipeline from raw plan ingestion through structured, queryable output

 - Tune and extend Higharc's Autotranslate AI capabilities to identify, categorize, and translate floorplans into data

 - Work hands-on with the data — write the ETL, build against internal APIs, and ship working capability back to users directly rather than handing off a spec

 - Build geometric similarity scoring and classification models that surface plans which have forked under different names

 - Meet delivery milestones — coverage targets, data-field completeness, QA error thresholds — and flag tradeoffs in real time when schedule pressure argues against them

 - Instrument and quantify results: redundancy across a catalog, dimensional spread on repeated conditions, consolidation candidates, and the purchasing leverage each one represents

 - Partner with the Forward Deployed Product Manager, Technical Lead, QA, Intake Specialists, and Client Strategy, and present technical progress and tradeoffs to executive stakeholders

 - Build the repeatable version — turn one-off scripts and data patterns into reusable tooling that lets the forward deployed model work on the next engagement, not just the current one

 - Travel to client sites and company events up to 30% of the time.
   
   


ABOUT YOU

You're happiest closest to the customer, and you've learned that the fastest path to the right answer is usually to go build it and see. You're comfortable being handed a scope that is 70% specified and a data set nobody has structured before. You can sit with an architect reviewing how a plan set is drawn in the morning and ship the pipeline that tests your hypothesis about it in the afternoon.

You know the difference between a demo and a deliverable, and you build the one the situation actually calls for.

You have:

 - 5+ years of engineering experience, including significant time in customer-facing or deployed settings — forward deployed engineering, solutions engineering, technical consulting, or professional services

 - Strong hands-on data fluency: SQL, scripting against APIs, comfort in notebooks, and a habit of interrogating a data set yourself rather than requesting a pull

 - Experience prototyping to validate ideas quickly using tools like Cursor, Replit, or V0.dev http://V0.dev

 - A track record building structured data models, taxonomies, or classification schemes and getting a system to actually run on them in production

 - Strong judgment about data quality — what level of accuracy a decision requires, and what it costs to get there

 - Excellent written and verbal communication, including with executive stakeholders who have limited time and no patience for status without substance

 - Willingness to travel to client sites and company events up to 30% of the time

A major plus if you also bring:

 - Background in residential construction, homebuilding, architecture, or AEC technology — especially fluency with plan sets, elevations, options, and how builders manage plan variation

 - Experience with agent-based or natural-language search over structured data, RAG systems, or LLM-powered analytics

 - Exposure to geometric or spatial data — CAD/BIM, computer vision on drawings, similarity and clustering methods

 - Experience working with large, messy, enterprise-scale data migrations or ingestion programs

 - Having built a function from zero: first hire into a new team, new practice, or new delivery model
   
   


WORKING AT HIGHARC

Remote work and travel: Our company is entirely remote, and has been since we were founded in 2018. Remote work means more time with family, less time commuting, and the flexibility to blend work and life. We value in-person collaboration and asynchronous deep-work time, which is why we schedule regular team meet-ups in our hubs across the US and, depending on the role, prioritize hiring in those hubs. If your role requires frequent travel beyond pre-scheduled team meet ups, we will represent that to the best of our ability as early as possible in the interview process. 

Compensation and benefits: Higharc offers competitive salaries with significant equity, in a fast-growing, well-funded company. We provide comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage, with flexible PTO, and meaningful maternity/paternity leave to all U.S based employees that are full-time. You'll also have access to other big-company benefits such like short and long-term disability plans and a 401K. We also provide a stipend to create the ideal home office and support ongoing L&D. 

Please note: we are seeing an uptick of fraudulent recruiting activity claiming to be associated with Higharc. All communication and outreach from our in-house team will come from an @higharc.com email address.

jobs.description:
About Inspira Education

Inspira Education Group is one of the fastest-growing edtech startups in the US. We started with a simple mission to democratize access to high-quality coaching so that every student in the world has an equal opportunity to access the best opportunities.

As the world’s leading network of top admissions coaches in medical, legal, business, and college studies, we’re building software and services in one place—disrupting long-entrenched application processes with products and experiences that strive to provide an equal platform for candidates from diverse backgrounds worldwide.

As one of the fastest-growing edtech firms in the world, we are backed by some of the leading venture capital firms and investors in the world, including Zeev Ventures, Quiet Capital, Craft Ventures and Jeff Fluhr (Founder of Stubhub).

The Role

Most companies treat sourcing as a support function: post a job, run some Boolean strings, wait. We're building something different - a sourcing engine that operates like a high-performing sales team, where every search is a targeting problem and every hire teaches us something we systematize for the next one.

The candidates who move the needle for us aren't applying - they're not checking job boards. Finding them takes real search craft. This role is for someone who's already spent years getting good at exactly that, and is ready to own it end-to-end: partnering with hiring managers, running the hardest searches yourself, and building the playbooks that let the function scale beyond you.

This role requires in-office attendance 5 days a week (NYC - Gramercy).

• 3-5 years of recruiting and sourcing experience with deep Boolean/LinkedIn Recruiter expertise

• Track record filling hard or senior roles through proactive sourcing, not just managing inbound

jobs.description:
ON.energy is setting the standard for large load interconnection. ON’s patented AI UPS™ is a medium-voltage UPS that serves as a firewall, protecting the data center from the grid, and the grid from the data center. With multiple gigawatts currently under construction, we are enabling grid-safe data centers.

Principal Battery Systems Engineer

Role Overview

We're looking for a Principal Engineer to set the technical direction for our BESS product line and to own the product roadmap across multiple concurrent development cycles. This is the senior technical voice on the product team: you'll architect new products, resolve the hardest engineering trade-offs, set the engineering standards others work to, and represent ON.energy's product engineering externally — to vendors, customers, certifying bodies, and the broader industry. You should be comfortable operating with minimal direction, holding the bar on technical quality, and moving multiple product cycles forward in parallel without losing the thread on any of them.

What You'll Own

Architecture & Technical Direction

• Set the architecture for the BESS product line and own the technical roadmap across multiple concurrent product cycles.

• Make the hard trade-off calls — cost vs reliability, performance vs lead time, standardization vs customization — and document the reasoning so future decisions inherit context.

• Define the engineering standards, design rules, and review gates that other engineers on the team work to. Own the product-engineering bar.

• Approve major design changes; act as the final technical authority on the change baseline.

Multi-Product Development

• Run multiple product development cycles in parallel — concept through prototype, FAT, field deployment, and revision — without losing depth on any of them.

• Drive cycle cadence: decide what ships when, where the technical risk lives, what gets parallelized vs sequenced.

• Identify and execute the next-generation product moves — higher voltage class, alternate chemistries, new form factors — ahead of customer demand.

Detailed Engineering Depth

• Personally own the hardest pieces of work: novel architectures, first-of-kind designs, advanced component sizing (fuse coordination, busbar thermal optimization, protection coordination across cascaded systems), cabinet thermal modeling, and complex protection schemes.

• Review and approve detailed engineering drawings — SLDs, GAs, schematics, panel layouts — at the level required to sign off, not just consult.

Vendor & Supply Chain Strategy

• Own the strategic relationships with key vendors — battery, PCS, BoP. Decide the architecture of those relationships: sole-source vs dual-source, co-development depth, IP boundaries.

• Set the technical qualification process used by the team and enforce it. Run the highest-stakes design reviews and resolve the highest-stakes vendor escalations personally.

Engineering Leadership & Mentorship

• Mentor and develop other engineers on the team. Build their technical judgment, not just their throughput.

• Run design reviews. Lead post-mortems on field issues and turn them into product changes.

• Set the cadence and quality bar for ECR/ECN, FMEA, design reviews, and product handoff.

External & Cross-Functional Representation

• Represent ON.energy's product engineering externally — customer technical reviews, vendor escalations, industry working groups, certifying bodies, conferences.

• Partner with the commercial team on the most technically complex pursuits and proposals — proposing architectures, defending positions, structuring technical exhibits in LTSAs and supply agreements.

• Brief leadership on technical risk and product roadmap decisions.

Required Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Power Electronics, or a closely related technical field. MS preferred.

• 10+ years of hands-on engineering experience in BESS, power electronics, UPS, or comparable mission-critical industrial power systems, with a demonstrated record of operating with minimal direction in a senior technical role.

• Owned multiple product development cycles end-to-end and independently. You've personally designed and integrated a BESS at the system level, from engineering through commissioning and into live operation, not just handed it off at FAT, and the products are still in the field.

• Architecture-level decision authority on previous BESS equipment. You've made the trade-off calls others built around, not just executed someone else's architecture.

• Deep, demonstrable skill in detailed component sizing — fuse coordination, busbar sizing, protection device selection, thermal sizing for enclosed cabinets — at the level required to sign off on production designs.

• Fluency producing and reviewing SLDs, GAs, schematics, and panel layouts; expert with AutoCAD or equivalent E-CAD; comfortable across mechanical drawings.

• Strong track record running strategic vendor relationships through design, FAT, serial production, and post-deployment escalation.

• Excellent written and verbal communication — specs, technical positions, design review leadership, board-level briefings.

• Willing to travel up to 25–30% for FAT inspections, site commissioning, customer engagements, and vendor reviews.

Preferred

• Direct experience with data center / UPS / mission-critical power or utility-scale BESS at the architecture level.

• Active involvement in standards bodies (UL, IEC, NFPA, IEEE working groups, CSA TC committees) or technical conference contributions.

• Patents, peer-reviewed publications, or other evidence of recognized technical depth in the field.

• PE license.

• Familiarity with UL 9540 / 9540A, NFPA 855, IEC 62619, IEEE 1547, NEC Article 706, plus the relevant codes for target markets.

• Experience standing up or scaling structured PLM, ECR/ECN, and design-review processes.

• Multi-domain depth — BMS / cell engineering, PCS / power electronics, thermal / mechanical — alongside the EE core.

jobs.title: Building Envelope Internship
jobs.description:
SOCOTEC’s Building Envelope team helps clients evaluate, design, construct, maintain, and improve the exterior components of buildings. The building envelope includes systems such as exterior walls, windows, doors, roofs, waterproofing, and other components that protect buildings from weather and the surrounding environment.

Our projects range from new construction to upgrades, repairs, maintenance, and repositioning of existing buildings. As a Building Envelope Intern, you will work alongside experienced engineers, inspectors, and Project Managers to gain exposure to both the technical and practical sides of building envelope consulting.

About SOCOTEC’s Summer Internship Program

SOCOTEC’s summer internship program is designed for college students who are eager to gain hands-on industry experience and learn more about the work we do. Interns receive well-rounded exposure to their field, with opportunities to spend time both on job sites and in the office while working alongside experienced professionals.

As a Building Envelope Intern, you can expect to spend approximately 2–3 days per week in the field, gaining firsthand experience with real-world building projects, construction activities, and site inspections. The remainder of your time will be spent in the office supporting project teams and learning how Building Envelope services are delivered.

What You’ll Do

Depending on the project, you may have the opportunity to:

• Participate in field visits and construction site inspections alongside experienced engineers and inspectors.
• Observe different phases of exterior wall and building envelope construction.
• Learn how building envelope projects progress from design and planning through construction.
• Assist with field reviews and documenting construction progress.
• Learn how to identify and document building envelope conditions and potential issues.
• Assist with reviewing architectural and construction drawings.
• Gain exposure to shop drawings, design development, and construction documents.
• Assist with building envelope research, inspections, and technical evaluations.
• Help prepare clear and detailed project reports, photographs, and other documentation.
• Gain exposure to building codes, construction standards, and industry best practices.
• Work alongside Project Managers and other team members to support project activities and deadlines.
• Learn how engineers and inspectors communicate technical information to clients, contractors, architects, and design teams.
• Attend team meetings, training sessions, and in-house seminars.
• Assist with other project-related assignments as needed.
• Develop your technical, communication, organization, and problem-solving skills.

• Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Architecture, Construction Management, or a related field. Architectural, Civil, or Mechanical Engineering is preferred.
• Interest in building envelope design, construction, inspection, and engineering.
• Basic understanding of building construction, architectural design, or structural concepts is a plus.
• Ability or willingness to learn how to read and interpret architectural and construction drawings.
• Strong written and verbal communication skills.
• Strong attention to detail and problem-solving skills.
• Ability to work collaboratively with engineers, inspectors, Project Managers, and other team members.
• Proficiency in Microsoft Office.
• Familiarity with AutoCAD, Revit, BIM, or other modeling/drafting software is a plus, but not required.
• Comfortable working both in an office and on active construction sites.
• Willingness to learn, ask questions, and take on new challenges.

What You’ll Gain

Through this internship, you will gain:

• Hands-on experience with real-world Building Envelope projects.
• Exposure to exterior wall systems, windows, doors, roofing, waterproofing, and other building envelope components.
• Experience participating in field reviews and construction site inspections.
• An understanding of how building envelope projects move from design through construction.
• Exposure to architectural drawings, shop drawings, construction documents, and building codes.
• Experience working with engineers, inspectors, Project Managers, clients, contractors, architects, and design teams.
• Opportunities to apply your classroom knowledge to practical building and construction challenges.
• Mentorship and professional development from experienced industry professionals.
• A better understanding of career opportunities in Building Envelope Engineering, Inspection, and Consulting.

Work Environment

This is a combination of field and office-based work. Building Envelope interns should expect to spend approximately 2–3 days per week on construction sites or at project locations.

Field work may involve walking active construction sites, climbing stairs or ladders, and working in various weather conditions. Interns will be expected to follow all applicable site safety requirements and will receive guidance from their supervisor and project team.

Potential Career Paths

This internship can provide a strong foundation for future opportunities in Building Envelope Engineering, Inspection, and Consulting, including entry-level roles such as:

• Building Envelope Engineer
• Engineer Inspector
• Building Envelope Consultant
• Project Engineer

SOCOTEC offers competitive compensation and benefits, mentorship, training, professional development opportunities, and social activities. SOCOTEC has also been certified as a Great Place to Work®.

Job Type: Internship

Your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

SOCOTEC is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

jobs.description:
At MERGE, we are Built Different. We are a marketing and technology agency purpose-built for the intersection of health and wellness—where human impact matters most. By weaving storytelling through technology, we move beyond traditional engagement to Whole Human Marketing. This approach recognizes that humans are multidimensional and complex, and uses AI to ensure every brand interaction feels natural, contextual, and relevant.

This commitment to human-first innovation is what brings us together and propels us forward. We are united by our North Star: to unite people and brands to empower healthier, happier lives.

Emerge to the Top of Your Career

At MERGE, we strive to create a superior work experience where talented and ambitious people grow. An experience that encourages people to think higher and feel deeper. An experience where people engage their minds and hearts to do the best work of their careers.

As our Director, Talent- Talent Management, you will…

Own the execution and continuous improvement of MERGE’s core Talent Management programs while overseeing the operating discipline behind the broader Talent roadmap. This is a hands-on role for an experienced operator who creates structure, anticipates risks, establishes accountability and drives work through completion. You will lead the day-to-day delivery of performance management, talent reviews, employee relations and employee programs, while ensuring broader Talent initiatives have clear owners, milestones and visibility. You will also develop sufficient familiarity with payroll to provide continuity support during planned leaves, unexpected absences and other coverage periods.

What You’ll Do

Talent Management & Employee Experience

• Own the end-to-end execution of performance management cycles, including planning, goal setting, talent reviews, assessments, systems, communications, training and follow-through.

• Develop clear project plans, establish ownership and proactively manage timelines, dependencies and risks.

• Ensure leaders and employees understand Talent processes, expectations and required actions.

• Maintain and continuously improve Talent Management toolkits, workflows, templates and process documentation.

• Monitor completion, exceptions and recurring challenges, providing Talent leadership with concise reporting and recommendations.

• Own offboarding processes, including exit interviews, documentation, reporting and identification of recurring themes.

• Partner with Talent leadership to operationalize new or updated programs across the agency.

Employee Relations & Risk Management

• Serve as a primary resource to managers and employees on employee relations and performance matters.

• Independently manage routine and moderately complex matters, escalating sensitive or high-risk issues appropriately.

• Guide managers through employee concerns, documentation, coaching and performance development plans.

• Ensure matters are addressed promptly, consistently and in accordance with company practices and applicable employment requirements.

• Support workforce changes, organizational restructurings and other employee actions by coordinating required processes, documentation, communications and follow-through.

• Maintain complete, accurate and appropriately confidential employee relations records.

• Identify recurring themes, organizational risks and gaps in manager practice, and recommend appropriate action.

Talent Roadmap & Program Management

• Own the integrated Talent roadmap, operating calendar and portfolio-management cadence across Talent functions.

• Translate priorities into clear project plans with defined owners, milestones, dependencies, decisions and deadlines.

• Hold initiative owners accountable for timely execution while ensuring functional leaders retain ownership of their deliverables and outcomes.

• Proactively identify risks, resource constraints and competing priorities, escalating issues that require leadership decisions.

• Directly project-manage priority cross-functional initiatives as assigned.

• Provide Talent leadership with concise, regular reporting on progress, risks, decisions and next steps.

• Ensure completed initiatives are documented and effectively transitioned into ongoing operations.

Operational Continuity & Team Leadership

• Cross-train on payroll processes and serve as designated continuity support during planned or unexpected gaps in primary payroll coverage.

• Maintain sufficient working knowledge of payroll timelines, controls and ADP processes to provide hands-on support when needed.

• Partner with the primary payroll owner and other internal stakeholders to ensure payroll remains accurate and on schedule during coverage periods.

• Create and maintain SOPs, controls and cross-training plans that reduce key-person dependency across critical Talent processes.

• Mentor junior Talent team members and reinforce a culture of accountability, accuracy, responsiveness and open communication.

• Support recurring compliance requirements, audits and reporting by maintaining documentation, tracking deadlines and driving follow-through.

• Partner effectively across Talent, Finance, Legal, Operations and agency leadership to resolve issues and move work forward.

What Success Looks Like

• Talent programs are completed accurately, consistently and on schedule, with minimal last-minute escalation.

• The Talent roadmap has clear priorities, owners, milestones and visibility.

• Initiative owners are held accountable, and risks or stalled decisions are surfaced early.

• Leaders receive timely, practical guidance and understand their responsibilities.

• Employee relations and performance matters are addressed early, documented appropriately and brought to resolution.

• Critical processes have current documentation, cross-training and dependable continuity coverage.

• Payroll continues accurately and on schedule during planned or unexpected coverage gaps.

• Talent leadership has reliable visibility into progress, trends and decisions requiring attention.

What You’ll Bring

• 10+ years of progressive HR experience, ideally within an agency, technology company or fast-paced professional services environment.

• Significant hands-on experience executing and operationalizing performance management, talent reviews and employee programs.

• Demonstrated experience managing complex, cross-functional projects and organizational roadmaps.

• Ability to work independently, make sound decisions and distinguish between matters to resolve directly and those requiring escalation.

jobs.title: Director of Special Projects - Finance
jobs.description:
About the role

This role sits in the Office of the CFO, and it is not a conventional finance role. Finance holds much of what IFS knows about itself: cost structure, unit economics, how the plan was built and where it has drifted. Most of the decisions that evidence should shape sit somewhere else, in Sales, Services, R&D and Operations. Connecting the two is the job.

You will lead a small number of substantial cross-functional projects each year and advise on several more. The work moves between transformation and analysis: redesigning how we plan and allocate, building the models and reporting leadership needs to see the business clearly, designing operating models and governance that hold up in practice, and working out where AI genuinely changes how finance and its partner functions work.

The portfolio changes with what the company needs. What stays constant is the shape of the problem. It crosses functions, nobody owns it yet, and the people involved do not start out

agreeing. A meaningful part of the work runs through external consulting partners, so you will be directing teams you do not employ about as often as teams you do.

Why this role?

Many roles at this level are either functional ownership or advice. This is neither. You take a problem from framing through analysis, decision and implementation, and you stay with it long enough to find out whether it worked.

You get direct access to the CFO and the executive team, a small team on your projects, and responsibility for outcomes rather than documents. IFS has grown quickly, organically and through acquisition, so there is real work to do on how the company plans, allocates and decides. This is not a tidy system to maintain.

What you'll do

Your responsibilities will include:

• Lead initiatives end to end. Frame the problem, build the workplan, run the analysis, drive to a decision with senior stakeholders and stay through implementation. You will not hand over a deck and move on.

• Diagnose how the business actually runs. Through interviews, workshops and time in the data, establish how a process really works rather than how it is documented, where cost and effort sit, and which decisions are being made on weak evidence or not being made at all.

• Design the future state. Process, structure, roles, governance and a transition plan someone can follow, built with the teams who have to live with it rather than presented to them.

• Connect finance, data and operations. Translate across financial logic, the data that describes the business and operational reality: cost structure to process design, forecast variance to capacity decisions, margin pressure to where the work actually happens. Work with Data and Technology teams so the numbers behind those links can be trusted.

• Improve the evidence behind decisions. Define the metrics, models and reporting leadership needs, retire what it does not, and make sure assumptions can be inspected and argued with.

• Scope and manage external consulting partners. Write the brief and scope of work, evaluate proposals, direct day-to-day delivery, hold external teams to a standard, integrate their output with internal work, control spend against the value delivered, and bring the knowledge back in house when the engagement ends.

• Lead blended teams. Run internal, cross-functional and third-party teams without formal authority over most of them. The role may carry direct reports over time.

• Shape where AI belongs in this work. Finance and its partner functions have no shortage of candidate use cases across planning, forecasting, close, procurement and workforce processes. The useful contribution is judgment: what is worth building, in what order, who owns it afterward, and where a human check has to stay. IFS holds its internal AI adoption to the same standard as the software it sells.

In your first six months: take one significant cross-functional problem from framing to a decision the executive team has signed off, with an implementation plan and a named owner. Alongside it, produce a clear read on how one core planning or allocation process works today and what should change.

What you'll bring

You are comfortable being handed a broad question and a group of stakeholders who do not agree, and turning that into a recommendation people act on. You care as much about whether the change held as about whether the analysis was right.

We are not looking for a controller, an FP&A manager or an accountant. You do need to be fluent enough in financial logic to hold your own in the CFO organization.

• Six or more years in management consulting, corporate strategy, finance transformation or business operations, with substantial cross-functional exposure. A consulting background fits well, and so does someone who has already left consulting for industry and wants a broader remit than a single function.

• Ownership of complex, multi-stakeholder work from diagnosis through implementation. Not analysis on its own, and not project administration.

• Strong quantitative skills and financial literacy. You can build a model or take one apart, work with messy enterprise data, connect operational drivers to financial results, and say plainly what the numbers do and do not support.

• Experience designing operating models, processes or organizational structures, and seeing them through to implementation.

• Experience working with or inside professional services. You know how an engagement is scoped, priced and staffed, what good delivery looks like, how to get value out of a partner firm and when bringing one in is the wrong answer.

• Executive communication. You can write a one-page recommendation and defend it in front of people who disagree with each other, and run a workshop that ends in a decision rather than another meeting.

Nice to have

• An MBA or comparable advanced degree, or an equivalent record of progression.

• Experience with planning, forecasting or resource allocation processes: how they work, where they break and what it takes to redesign one. Deep FP&A ownership is welcome but not expected.

• Hands-on work on AI strategy or delivery, such as use case prioritization, build, buy or partner decisions, or getting an AI-enabled product into real use. Technical depth is welcome; judgment about what is realistic matters more.

• Working knowledge of SQL, Python or R, and of modern business intelligence and planning tools. You do not need to build the pipeline, but pulling your own data and pressure-testing someone else's analysis will make you faster.

• Enterprise software, or another business with recurring revenue and a substantial services component. Post-acquisition integration or carve-out experience.

• Shared services or center of excellence design, or work in regulated and high-consequence environments where a decision also has to be defensible.

If you have led cross-functional work that ended in a decision someone had to make, and you want a broader problem set than any one function can offer, we would like to hear from you.

What We’re Offering

• Salary Range: $175,000 - $190,000 plus bonus
• Flexible paid time off, including sick and holiday
• Medical, dental, & vision insurance
• 401K with Company contribution
• Flexible spending accounts
• Life insurance and disability benefits
• Tuition assistance
• Community involvement and volunteering events

We embrace flexibility and hybrid work opportunities to support diverse needs and lifestyles, while also valuing inclusive workplace experiences. By fostering a sense of community, we drive innovation, strengthen connections, and nurture belonging. Our commitment ensures you can work in a way that suits you best, while also engaging with colleagues to share ideas and build meaningful relationships.

jobs.description:
Reimagine the infrastructure of cancer care within a community that values integrity, inspires growth, and is uniquely positioned to create a more modern, connected oncology ecosystem. We’re looking for a Communications Coordinator to help us accomplish our mission to improve and extend lives by learning from the experience of every person with cancer. Are you ready to be the next changemaker in cancer care?

What You’ll Do

We’re seeking an organized, collaborative, and strong writer to support Flatiron’s internal and external communications. This entry-level role will help coordinate content, campaigns, events, and day-to-day communications operations that keep employees informed and strengthen Flatiron’s visibility in the market. In addition you will:

Internal Communications

• Draft and edit internal announcements, newsletters, Slack posts, event invitations, and other employee communications

• Support company-wide meetings, leadership events, and employee engagement initiatives by coordinating content, speakers, timelines, and logistics

• Maintain internal communications calendars and company intranet to help ensure employees receive clear, timely, and consistent information

• Gather updates and stories from teams across Flatiron for use across internal channels

• Track employee engagement and feedback to help the team improve internal communications

External Communications and Content

• Support the development of press releases, blog posts, executive communications, award submissions, media materials, and other external content

• Draft and coordinate social media content across Flatiron’s corporate channels

• Assist with communications campaigns tied to company news, product launches, research publications, partnerships, and industry conferences

• Help translate scientific, technical, and business information into clear and engaging content for different audiences

• Coordinate reviews and approvals with internal stakeholders to ensure content is accurate, timely, and aligned with Flatiron’s voice

• Research relevant industry trends, competitor activity, and potential storytelling opportunities

Media Relations and Monitoring

• Conduct daily media and industry monitoring and share relevant coverage with internal stakeholders

• Maintain media lists, coverage trackers, briefing materials, and other communications resources

• Support proactive and reactive media opportunities by coordinating interview logistics and preparing background materials

• Assist with tracking earned media coverage, share of voice, and campaign results

• Support the Corporate Communications team and external agency partners with media outreach and follow-up

Social Media and Digital Communications

• Help maintain the corporate social media editorial calendar

• Draft, schedule, and publish approved content using social media management tools

• Coordinate basic graphics and visual assets in partnership with Brand and Marketing

• Monitor social engagement and compile regular performance reports

• Identify relevant company, employee, and industry content that Flatiron may want to amplify

Communications Operations

• Maintain project trackers, editorial calendars, distribution lists, and shared documentation

• Coordinate meetings, deadlines, reviews, and approvals across multiple communications initiatives

• Organize communications assets and templates across shared platforms such as Google Drive

• Support vendor onboarding, invoices, contracts, and other administrative processes

• Help maintain communications guidelines, templates, executive biographies, fact sheets, and other core materials

• Provide general coordination support to help the Corporate Communications team operate effectively

Who You Are

You are curious, detail-oriented, and eager to build communications experience within a fast-paced healthcare and technology environment. You will work closely with members of the Corporate Communications team and partners across the business, gaining exposure to internal communications, media relations, social media, executive communications, and scientific storytelling. In addition you have:

• 0–2 years of relevant professional or internship experience in communications, public relations, marketing, journalism, or a related field

• Strong writing, editing, and verbal communication skills

• Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail

• Ability to manage multiple assignments and meet deadlines

• Comfort working collaboratively with colleagues across different functions

• Familiarity with social media platforms, particularly LinkedIn

• Proficiency with Google Workspace or similar productivity tools

• Interest in healthcare, life sciences, technology, or corporate communications

Extra Credit

• Internship or early-career experience in corporate communications, internal communications, public relations, or social media

• Experience drafting content for internal or external audiences

• Familiarity with communications tools such as Sprinklr, Airtable, Canva, or Figma

• Experience supporting events, executive communications, or media monitoring

• Exposure to healthcare, life sciences, oncology, or another complex industry

• Basic understanding of communications measurement and social media analytics

Where You’ll Work

In this hybrid role, you’ll have a defined work location that includes work from home and 3 office days set by you and your team. For more information on our approach to hybrid work, please visit the how we work website.

Life at Flatiron

At Flatiron Health, we offer a full range of benefits to support you and your loved ones so you can focus your working hours on improving cancer care and accelerating cancer research, and your non-working hours on everything else life has to offer:

• Work/life autonomy via flexible work hours and flexible paid time off

• Comprehensive compensation package

• 401(k) contribution to help you reach your retirement planning goals

• Financial health resources including 1:1 financial advice

• Mental well-being tools and services

• Parental benefits and policies including family-building care and generous leave

• Path to parenthood programs supporting fertility, adoption and surrogacy

• Travel support for safe healthcare services

In addition to our robust benefit offerings, visit our Life at Flatiron page to learn how we support continuous learning and celebrate inclusion and belonging in the workplace.

jobs.title: Sheet Metal Mechanic
jobs.description:
COHO Consulting Group is seeking a Sheet Metal Mechanic to join our team in support of a contract at Robins AFB in Warner Robins, GA.  This is a mixed position performing the duties of a sheet metal mechanic and aircraft mechanic. The candidate in this position is required to perform several unrelated aircraft overhaul functions for assigned aircraft.

Responsibilities (include but are not limited to):

• Develop patterns and lay out, cut, form, join, assemble, and install metal parts, items, and assemblies

• Plan and lay out work from blueprints, sketches, drawings, specifications, and work orders in manufacturing aircraft sheet metal structures that have combined straight and curved edges, and irregular angles, planes, and curves

• Evaluate structural damage to aircraft sheet metal systems or items to be manufactured, repaired, or modified, and examine aircraft sheet metal structures to locate cracks, breaks, holes, bulges, dents, and loose or missing rivets

• Determine the type and extent of repairs needed to restore original strength to components such as frames, stringers, bulkheads, spars, ribs, and stiffeners

Requirements:

• Education: High School Diploma or equivalent Airframe Certificate

• Required Knowledge/Experience: 1-3 years civilian or military aircraft sheet metal experience Prior experience planning, laying out work in manufacturing aircraft sheet metal parts and components that have combined straight and curved edges, and irregular angles, planes, and curves. Proven experience using hand and power tools such as hammers, chisels, hand snips, band and circle saws, squaring shears, seamers, bar folders, brakes, and stakes, and operating complex hand and power machines such as slip roll forming machines, box and pan brakes, rotary machines with extra forming rolls, crimpers and beading machines, and soldering and welding equipment. Knowledge of the characteristics and properties of metals used in the trade such as stainless steel, magnesium, and alloys, and of advanced shop mathematics and principles of radial-line development combined with parallel-line development to calculate and scribe patterns involving combined straight and curved edges or irregular curves, angles, and planes. Knowledge of the makeup, operation, installation, and adjustment of a variety of major interrelated and/or integrated aircraft systems, subsystems, and assemblies such as fuel and hydraulic systems, flight control systems, instrumentation systems, engines, landing gear assemblies, airframe, and control surfaces. Using complicated measuring instruments such as protractors, calipers, snap ring, height, depth, dial, and screw pitch gauges, and other hand measurement devices to measure plans and projects. Ability to examine aircraft sheet metal structures to locate cracks, breaks, holes, bulges, dents, and loose or missing rivets and determine the type and extent of repairs needed to restore original strength, and to make repairs by manufacturing and installing new parts and reinforcing, patching, and replacing defective parts.

jobs.title: Senior Project Analyst
jobs.description:
For more than 50 years, ENSCO has been providing leading-edge engineering, science and advanced technology solutions to governments and private industries worldwide.

ENSCO prides itself in creating and applying advanced technologies for mission success. We provide systems engineering, integration, and advanced technology services to transform the future safety, security, and resiliency of critical missions on the ground, in the air, in space, and in the information systems that connect these domains.

Learn more about ENSCO.

Position Description

Job description
ENSCO Inc. is a diverse engineering and technology company that provides engineering, science, and advanced technology solutions supporting mission success, safety, and security for government and commercial customers worldwide.

We are seeking a Project Analyst to work with Government mission leaders, project owners, technical teams, operators, acquisition professionals, cybersecurity stakeholders, test organizations, and industry partners delivering critical space and defense capabilities. The analyst will turn broad mission priorities into visible work, maintain a reliable view of progress and readiness, and ensure decision owners have accurate information when choices must be made.

This role is central to pre-prototype planning and capability maturation. The analyst will connect schedules, work products, risks, actions, stakeholder commitments, and transition needs across concurrent efforts. Success requires disciplined analysis, strong written communication, attention to data quality, and the judgment to surface a weak assumption or missed dependency before it becomes a delivery problem. Government decision owners retain all formal authority.

Primary Responsibilities

• Translate priorities into executable work. Clarify the mission outcome, scope, assumptions, work products, owners, milestones, approval points, and evidence required for the next decision.
• Maintain the integrated project picture. Build and update schedules, milestone networks, action registers, decision logs, deliverable trackers, and readiness views across concurrent projects.
• Manage work product status. Track planned and actual submission dates, review status, acceptance or rejection, Government actions, corrective actions, and the next month's forecast.
• Identify risks and dependencies early. Analyze schedule conflicts, resource constraints, stakeholder commitments, technical handoffs, security activities, test events, training needs, and transition dependencies; elevate consequences with practical response options.
• Coordinate the stakeholder rhythm. Prepare and facilitate project kickoffs, working sessions, status reviews, and decision forums; capture actions, owners, due dates, decisions, and unresolved issues through closure.
• Produce decision-ready products. Develop concise status reports, briefing materials, schedule and dependency views, risk summaries, alternative comparisons, meeting records, and recommendations that allow leaders to act.
• Connect planning to rapid learning. Track the analyses, demonstrations, interface events, prototypes, and user feedback needed to test important assumptions before the Government commits to a larger acquisition or fielding path.
• Build trusted working relationships. Learn what each organization must accomplish, communicate facts clearly, resolve documentation or coordination gaps without blame, and follow through on commitments across organizational boundaries.
• Improve project workflows. Identify recurring delays or quality problems, simplify tracking and review steps, standardize useful templates, and communicate process changes so teams can execute consistently.

Qualifications Required
• Bachelor's degree in business, project or program management, operations, data analytics, public administration, communications, education, a technical field, or a closely related discipline, plus a minimum of 5 years of relevant professional experience. An equivalent combination of education and relevant experience may be considered.
• Experience coordinating projects, programs, operations, training, or other complex work in a Government, defense, intelligence, technology, education, or similarly regulated environment.
• Demonstrated ability to maintain schedules, milestones, action items, decision records, deliverable status, risks, dependencies, and stakeholder commitments across multiple concurrent efforts.
• Experience reviewing records or work products for completeness, accuracy, consistency, and compliance with established requirements before submission or processing.
• Ability to analyze project information, identify missing or conflicting data, determine the operational or schedule consequence, and coordinate corrective action to closure.
• Demonstrated ability to coordinate effectively with Government, military, civilian, contractor, technical, operational, and external partner personnel.
• Clear written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain process or requirement changes and obtain timely responses from multiple stakeholders.
• Experience handling sensitive, controlled, proprietary, or classified information with discretion and in accordance with established policy.
• Ability to work in a hybrid environment in Colorado Springs, Colorado, and support periodic coordination or travel to Albuquerque, New Mexico, as required.
• U.S. citizenship and an active DoD Top Secret security clearance required at time of hire.

Qualifications Desired
• Master's degree in a relevant business, management, analytical, operational, educational, or technical discipline.
• Current Top Secret or TS/SCI eligibility.
• Experience organizing information for acquisition strategy, alternatives, market research, cost estimates, schedules, procurement planning, or future contract and prototype actions.
• Working knowledge of project scheduling, portfolio tracking, risk and issue management, configuration control, records management, and Government work-product review processes.
• Experience with Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, SharePoint, Project, Power BI, Smartsheet, Jira, Confluence, or comparable tools used for analysis, collaboration, scheduling, and status reporting.
• Project management, agile delivery, process improvement, data analytics, records management, or related professional credentials.

Required Certifications: None
U.S. Citizenship Required: Yes
Security Clearance Required: Top Secret
Employment Type: Regular Full-time
Background Check Type: 7 Year Pre-Employment
Drug Screen Required: None
Position Contingent Upon Contract Award: Yes

Salary Range

$91,500—$120,000 USD

REAL ID Requirement

This position may require the ability to access to U.S. federal facilities. In accordance with the Department of Homeland Security’s enforcement of the REAL ID Act, as of May 7, 2025, individuals must present a REAL ID-compliant form of identification or an acceptable alternative to gain entry. For a list of acceptable forms of identification, please click here.

Benefits

At ENSCO, a positive working environment and a competitive salary are only part of the reason for choosing a career here. We offer a comprehensive benefits package that creates a stimulating and supportive environment where you can thrive - visit ensco.com/careers/benefits to learn more.

Export Control and Licensing

This position may involve access to technology or technical data that is controlled under U.S. export control laws and regulations and the release of which to a non US person may require an export license from the U.S. Government.

jobs.title: Provider (Physician Assistant/Nurse Practitioner) - West Region
jobs.description:
Of the 10 million Americans struggling with opioid misuse, only 1 in 10 receive treatment. This is an accessibility crisis, and we are on a mission to solve it by bringing life-saving care to the 89% currently left behind. Through a single app, Bicycle Health combines Medication for Opioid Use Disorder (MOUD) with behavioral healthcare, drug screening, therapy, and peer support.

We’re looking for Nurse Practitioners and Physician Assistants to join us full-time in a 40-hour-per-week, W-2 role with a schedule designed to offer both structure and flexibility.

The Provider position at Bicycle Health is a remote full-time addiction medicine clinical position with responsibility for the continuity care of a panel of adult patients under care primarily for opioid use disorder. The Nurse Practitioner or Physician Assistant will assess new patients presenting for telemedicine-based care of opioid use disorder, determine appropriateness of enrollment in our care setting, and manage their continuity OUD treatment from initial induction through the duration of their care.  The Nurse Practitioner also addresses co-occurring mental health conditions directly when appropriate, and also via referral and care-coordination with outside providers.  The NP/PA participates actively in regular clinical team meetings and quality improvement activities, collaborates with our program physicians and therapists, and reports to the regional medical director.

What You Can Expect:

✅ Stable, full time employment - This is a full-time, W-2 employees. As a a full-time employee you will receive full benefits.
✅ Location Flexibility - Work from home and work from anywhere in your state (subject to change depending on regulations).
✅ Limited Call - there are on-call responsibilities but most providers are on-call once every 2-3 months on average. Call is one week at a time (Monday to Monday).
✅ Start times vary by region - See below to see more detail on available shifts by region

Target Pay Range: $120,000-$135,000 + Bonus Eligible -  Salary to be determined by the education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities of the applicant, internal equity, and alignment with market data.

• Safely and effectively start treatment with buprenorphine-naloxone for OUD, manage the early induction and stabilization phase of care with close follow-up

• Telehealth experience a big plus!

This is a full-time (40hrs per week) remote position.

Bicycle Health is a telemedicine group that specializes in the evidence-based treatment of individuals with Opioid Use Disorder using buprenorphine. We believe addiction treatment should be available to everyone who needs it. And with our technology-driven approach, we work to reach as many people as possible. Our innovative model has achieved clinical outcomes that exceed expectations for standard-of-care in-person treatment nationally. Our mission is to increase access to high quality, affordable, convenient and confidential Opioid Use Disorder treatment for all.

jobs.title: Senior Manufacturing Engineer
jobs.description:
About Re:Build

At Re:Build, our mission is to ensure the next generation of important products are made, at scale, in America. We are laying the foundation for a better future for our customers, employees, and communities by revitalizing America's manufacturing base and creating meaningful jobs across the country, including in historically deindustrialized regions.

We operate an advanced, end-to-end manufacturing platform that partners with industrial companies and innovators to take products from first concept to full-scale production in critical verticals including aerospace and defense, electrification, medical, energy and environment, and robotics and automation.

The way we operate is as important as the work we do. It's guided by The Re:Build Way, 16 principles that shape how we collaborate with each other, partner with our customers and vendors, and contribute to the communities where we operate. (link to The Re:Build Way principles)

About Re:Build DAPR Engineering

Re:Build DAPR Engineering, LLC (DAPR) is an engineering design and analysis consulting firm in Merrimack, New Hampshire. We work with customers across many industries to develop and deliver turnkey industrial machines to meet their unique requirements. We design and build custom automation solutions, work with OEM’s to develop industrial products, and provide engineering analysis using FEA tools.

Who We Are Looking For

We're looking for an experienced manufacturing engineer who bridges product design and production—whether that means shaping capacity and design requirements early on, or taking a finished design and determining the best way to bring it to production. You bring strong analytical instincts, a hands-on approach, and the ability to solve complex problems without a clear precedent to follow. You communicate clearly, whether documenting a process, leading root cause investigations, or collaborating with multi-functional teams.

This role offers ownership over how products get built—from cell layout and tooling to the documentation that keeps production running at target rates.

What You Get To Do

• Bridge product design and production, ensuring designs can be manufactured efficiently and to spec

• Develop and document manufacturing processes, process flows, and work instructions from prototype through production

• Design cell layouts, fixtures, and tooling using lean principles

• Conduct timing studies to identify bottlenecks and optimize line performance

• Specify and source manufacturing equipment

• Lead troubleshooting and root cause analysis to resolve and prevent issues

• Contribute to Lean 2P/3P events and Value Stream Analyses to reduce waste

• Build preventative maintenance plans and champion a safe manufacturing environment

• Support Design for Manufacturing (DFM) efforts for clients as needed

What You Bring To The Team

• Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience in manufacturing, mechanical, or related engineering field, plus 5+ years of manufacturing experience

• Strong analytical skills (statistics, advanced algebra, geometry, trigonometry)

• Proficiency in CAD/CAE tools (preferably SolidWorks) and strong Excel skills

• Advanced written/verbal communication skills for technical and business documents

• Ability to solve complex, novel problems with creativity and sound judgment

• Willingness to travel domestically 10–20%

• Nice to have: machine design/solving experience; ERP familiarity (e.g., Syteline)

The base salary range for this position is $112,000 – $140,000 per year. This range represents the Company’s good faith estimate of the base compensation for this role at the time of posting.  Actual compensation will be determined based on several factors, including but not limited to relevant experience, skills, qualifications, internal equity, and geographic location. In addition to base salary, this role may be eligible for annual incentive compensation and/or long-term incentives, subject to Company plans. The Company offers a comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental, vision, retirement, paid time off, and other benefits.

The BIG payoff

We are a company who is going to make a difference in the industries and the communities in which we choose to operate.  Every employee of Re:Build will share ownership in the company and will share in the financial rewards of the success we achieve together, at all levels of the company!

We want to work with people that reflect the communities in which we operate

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.



About the Role

You will serve as a front-line manager for a team of Sales Development Representatives, responsible for outbound prospecting and pipeline generation across Ramp’s SMB segment.

You will lead and evolve the SMB sales development motion by providing 1:1 coaching, onboarding, training, and mentorship; setting team strategy; and partnering closely with Sales, Marketing, Product, and Executive Leadership to drive pipeline and business outcomes.

As a member of the Sales Leadership team, you will play a critical role in developing SDR talent, scaling effective outbound practices, and continuously refining Ramp’s SMB go-to-market motion.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

WHAT YOU NEED
