jobs.title: Inventory Control Associate
jobs.description:
WHO WE ARE

Biofire Technologies is on a mission to give gun owners better tools for reducing preventable gun injuries and deaths, especially among children. We believe our technology, combined with a best-in-class customer experience, will define the future of firearms safety for the next generation. Our mission-driven approach has earned support from the firearm community, the tech world, and the media.

Biofire employees encompass a diverse range of talents, including world-class engineers who have designed and tested firearms, medical devices, robots, cars, satellites, rockets, and supersonic jets; expert technicians from aerospace, defense tech, special forces, and gunsmithing; and elite operators from high-tech, advanced manufacturing, and regulated industries. Whether building the product or powering the company behind it, every Biofire team member is united by an obsession with safety, reliability, and operational excellence.




OUR CULTURE

Reducing accidental firearm injuries and deaths requires original thinking and authentic collaboration, so we're deeply invested in building a team and culture that can achieve our mission together. Team members enjoy autonomy and flexibility from day one, so expect to be immediately tasked with solving challenging problems and building new systems that work. We'll hold you accountable for executing audacious goals, giving and receiving honest feedback, and helping your teammates succeed. You'll receive respect, kindness, and support from every direction while you figure out how to get it all done.




ABOUT THE ROLE

As an Inventory Control Associate at Biofire, you will own the physical flow of inventory that keeps our production lines building — receiving incoming shipments, storing materials, picking and kitting components to work orders, keeping lineside inventory stocked, performing cycle counts, and supporting the shipment of finished goods. Every part in our Smart Gun has a story the system must be able to tell, so in this role the scanner is as important as the pallet jack: you'll make sure that what's on the shelf and what's in the system always match, down to the serial, lot, and revision.

We are looking for someone who takes real pride in accuracy — the kind of person who counts twice, flags what doesn't look right, and hands off a warehouse the next shift can trust. You'll work under the direction of our Inventory Manager and alongside production, quality, engineering, and shipping teams in a fast-moving manufacturing environment where your work directly determines whether the line builds on schedule.

To succeed, you will need to move quickly without sacrificing precision, follow procedures built for a regulated product while speaking up the moment reality doesn't match the paperwork, and communicate clearly with everyone who depends on the parts you touch. If you're excited about keeping a mission-driven production floor running with discipline and care, we encourage you to apply.




KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Day-to-day responsibilities of the role will include:

 - Unload, verify, and inspect incoming shipments against packing slips and purchase orders, reporting discrepancies and damage the same day

 - Put away received materials to designated storage locations and record every movement accurately and in real time in our inventory system

 - Pick, kit, and stage components to production work orders according to the bill of materials and specified revisions, delivering materials to points of use across the manufacturing floor

 - Replenish lineside inventory to established min/max and kanban levels through proactive floor walks each shift, and respond promptly to restock requests from production

 - Perform daily and periodic cycle counts, research count variances, and support annual and interim physical inventories

 - Maintain accurate serial-number, lot, and revision records, and handle controlled and regulated components in accordance with all applicable federal, state, and internal chain-of-custody procedures

 - Record and label expiration dates for shelf-life-controlled consumables at receipt, store and rotate materials using FIFO, and flag items approaching expiration for review

 - Prepare finished goods for shipment — pick, pack, label, and stage — and coordinate with the shipping team on outbound readiness

 - Maintain a clean, safe, and well-organized warehouse and staging area, storing materials appropriately by size, weight, hazard class, and turnover

 - Identify and report damaged, obsolete, or non-conforming inventory to Quality, and contribute ideas to process-improvement initiatives

 - Operate pallet jacks, hand trucks, and RF scanners safely as part of daily work, providing backup and cross-coverage for other warehouse and inventory roles as needed




QUALIFICATIONS

We understand that not all applicants will possess skills that perfectly align with our job qualifications. At Biofire, we appreciate diverse experiences from various industries, and we encourage all individuals who meet the necessary qualifications to submit their applications. While having the "desired" qualifications may strengthen a candidate's profile, we also welcome applicants with alternative experiences to apply.

 - 2+ years of material handling, warehouse, or inventory experience in a manufacturing, distribution, or similar environment; a high school diploma or equivalent is required, and prior work in manufacturing industries is a plus

 - Demonstrated accuracy and attention to detail in recording inventory transactions, with comfort using computer-based inventory systems, handheld RF scanners, and basic math (counting, addition, subtraction, unit conversion)

 - Ability to operate standard warehouse equipment (pallet jack, hand truck); forklift certification is a plus

 - Experience with kitting for manufacturing production and with cycle counting and inventory reconciliation is strongly preferred

 - Reliable, punctual, and able to work independently as well as on a team; legally eligible under federal and state law to handle regulated components (background check required)




PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

This is a hands-on warehouse and manufacturing-floor role. You should be able to stand, walk, and move about the floor for the duration of a shift; regularly lift, push, pull, and carry up to 40 lbs and occasionally up to 50 lbs; bend, stoop, kneel, reach overhead, and climb ladders to access storage locations; and handle small parts and hardware with precision. The work environment includes typical manufacturing noise, machinery, and temperature variation. Required PPE (closed-toe safety shoes, safety glasses, and other PPE as directed) is provided.




COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS

In addition to competitive pay, as a full-time employee at Biofire you are eligible for:

 - Stock Options in Biofire, 401(k), HSA - and other financial benefits

 - Medical Insurance - including plan options with $0 payroll deduction

 - Dental, Vision and Life Insurance Plans - with $0 payroll deduction

 - 3 Weeks Vacation and Sick time (Flex Time for salary positions), and 13 Paid Holidays

 - Parental Leave - and other family-building, adoption and surrogacy benefits

The compensation range for this role is $25.00 – $30.00 /hour + stock options + benefits.

Pay offered may vary depending on multiple individualized factors, including market location, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. The total compensation package for this position may also include other elements dependent on the position offered. Details of participation in these benefit plans will be provided if an employee receives an offer of employment.




LOCATION

This is a full-time, hourly, on-site role. Our dog-friendly, state-of-the-art headquarters is located in beautiful Broomfield, Colorado, between Boulder and Denver.

We expect you to bring your very best, and in return, we will provide the support necessary for you to excel. You'll collaborate with colleagues you appreciate, respect, and find inspiration from, and have access to all the technical resources needed.




DIVERSITY & INCLUSION

We're bringing innovation to a technological problem that has persisted for decades, so we depend on diverse, inclusive, and collaborative teams to break new ground and do great work. We welcome people from all qualified backgrounds, and we don't discriminate based on race, religion, color, political affiliation, national origin, gender (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, or other applicable legally protected characteristics.




ELIGIBILITY

This role handles information subject to US Export Control Regulations. Applicants must be (a) a citizen of the United States; (b) a lawful permanent resident of the United States ("Green Card" holder); or (c) a person admitted into the United States as an asylee or refugee to be considered for the position.

jobs.title: Lab Operations and Research Associate I (SINGAPORE)
jobs.description:
About Antheia:
Antheia is the advanced biosynthesis company transforming pharmaceutical manufacturing and innovation for the 21st century. Antheia’s commercially proven technology platform produces high-value pharmaceutical ingredients in a fraction of the time compared to legacy approaches while significantly reducing supply chain risk. The company provides its global pharmaceutical customers with a resilient, efficient supply of critical ingredients at scale, while expanding the innovation frontier for new therapeutic development. Backed by leading investors and recognized by the U.S. government as a priority technology for public health and national and economic security, Antheia is manufacturing the medicines the world needs today while enabling tomorrow’s breakthrough therapeutics.

Working at Antheia:
Our cross-functional team shares a vision for the future: improved pharmaceutical supply chains that can end drug shortages and drive equitable access to essential medicines. As a team, we aim to embody a culture that celebrates diversity, prioritizes knowledge sharing, encourages exploration and ideation, challenges constructively, and supports individuals in their professional and personal journeys. At Antheia, you can expect to be inspired by the science, by your teammates, and by the opportunity we have to bring about change in the pharmaceutical industry.

PLEASE NOTE THAT THIS POSITION IS BASED IN OUR SINGAPORE OFFICE.  Our Singapore-based employees receive a competitive benefits and time-off package designed to reflect local market practices and comply with all applicable Singapore requirements.

At Antheia Bio Asia, we're reprogramming yeast to biosynthesize complex, high-value compounds using cutting-edge synthetic biology and precision genome engineering tools.

As a Lab Ops and Research Associate, you'll keep the lab running like clockwork — reagent prep, inventory, autoclaving, the operational backbone every good discovery depends on — while also getting hands-on with strain construction and molecular biology alongside senior scientists who are actively pushing the boundaries of what yeast can produce. Think advanced genetic engineering techniques, plasmid builds, and watching your work move from a digital design straight into a living cell.

This is a new subsidiary in Singapore, so you'll wear a lot of hats — and that's exactly the appeal. If you're organized, resourceful, genuinely curious about biology, and want a front-row seat (and a working role) in a fast-moving metabolic engineering team building toward real therapeutic impact, we want to hear from you.

RESPONSIBILITIES

• Lab Operations & Infrastructure: Manage daily lab operations, including receiving/logging deliveries, monitoring stock levels, and placing daily orders. Coordinate with accounting for invoices and purchase orders to ensure a steady supply chain. Maintain lab tidiness and safety by cleaning common bench areas and general-use equipment. Manage the sterilization cycle: washing and autoclaving glassware, pipette tips, tubes, and plates. Troubleshoot laboratory equipment and schedule routine maintenance or repairs.

• Reagent & Strain Support: Prepare high-quality liquid media, agar plates, buffers, and stock solutions for molecular biology. Prepare and validate competent yeast and E. coli cells. Assist in the systematic banking and cataloging of engineered strains.

• Technical Research Support: Execute routine molecular biology tasks including PCR, DNA assembly (cloning), and plasmid preparation. Perform yeast transformations and strain verification via colony PCR and gel electrophoresis. Conduct routine laboratory assays and protocols, including spectrophotometry (OD600 measurements), plate-based colorimetric assays, and sample preparation for downstream analysis Document all work accurately in Electronic Lab Notebooks (ELN) and follow established SOPs.

• Perform other duties as assigned[1]

QUALIFICATIONS

• Education: B.S. in Biology, Biotechnology, Molecular Biology, or a related field.

• Experience: 1–2 years of relevant laboratory experience (industry, internship, or intensive academic research).

• Hands-on experience with basic molecular biology techniques (PCR, gel electrophoresis, cloning).

• Familiarity with microbial culture (yeast or bacteria) and aseptic technique.

• Outstanding organizational and time-management skills; ability to prioritize tasks in a dynamic environment.

• Strong communication skills and a collaborative mindset.

• High attention to detail and a commitment to maintaining a safe, clean work environment.

• Physical ability to lift 40 pounds and perform repetitive lab tasks.

• Experience operating analytical equipment such as HPLC systems, and comfort with related workflows is a plus.

• Experience with Benchling or similar digital lab management tools is a plus.

[1] This job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee. Duties, responsibilities and activities may change or new ones may be assigned at any time with or without notice.

Please note that Antheia doesn't discriminate based on age, race, ethnicity, national origin, religion, gender, sexual orientation, disability, medical history, and other non-merit characteristics.

For full-time employees, Antheia offers a comprehensive total rewards package. Part-time (<30 hours per week) and temporary roles are not eligible for Company sponsored benefits.

• Comprehensive compensation package, which includes annual bonus potential and equity opportunities

• Paid time off, in addition to company-observed holidays

jobs.title: Malawi Extension Lead
jobs.description:
About One Acre Fund

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our Why Work Here blog post.

Our Malawi program, founded in 2016, provides more than 670,000 farmers with quality farm supplies and training. Our office in Malawi is located in Zomba, in the country’s south. One Acre Fund works in Malawi’s southern region, which has the highest concentration of smallholder farmers in the country.

About the Role

The Agronomy & Extension Lead will own the implementation of Malawi’s extension strategy, using HCD and SBC approaches to translate agronomic recommendations into simple, practical and adoptable support for farmers. The role will strengthen extension delivery, training and communication content, and use farmer feedback and impact data to continuously improve our approaches. They will work closely with Field Operations and Innovations to turn validated research into scalable farmer-facing solutions.

Responsibilities

The role combines technical agronomy leadership with the design and management of a practical, farmer-centered extension system.

Own Malawi's agronomy and extension strategy

• Co-design and maintain a multi-year strategy aligned with Malawi’s impact priorities and farmers’ needs.

• Turn the strategy into annual OKRs, budgets, seasonal plans and clear ownership across teams.

Embed extension in Field Operations execution

• Build agronomy and extension priorities into the Field Operations seasonal calendar, training cascade, field tools and performance routines.

• Strengthen the technical capability of Field Managers, Field Officers and other delivery partners through training-of-trainers, coaching and practical support.

• Create clear feedback and support channels so field teams receive timely technical answers and can share implementation challenges and farmer responses.

Own the process of qualitative technical agronomic recommendations

• Use Human-Centred Design, farmer feedback and impact data to develop, test and refine agronomic recommendations.

• Work with Innovations, MEL and global technical teams to assess recommendations against local evidence, farmers’ realities and government guidance before they are scaled.

• Conduct formative research to understand farmers’ needs, behaviours and barriers to adoption.

Design farmer-centered extension and behavior-change interventions

• Translate technical recommendations into simple, memorable and actionable guidance for field teams and farmers.

• Develop extension approaches that use the right mix of group training, demonstrations, coaching and digital channels.

• Use the findings to design, test and improve extension approaches and communication content.

• Apply adult-learning, behavior-change and human-centered design approaches to understand barriers to adoption and ensure content works for different farmer profiles.

Monitor adoption, learning and impact

• Analyze results across farmer groups, locations and delivery channels to identify where recommendations or delivery approaches need to change.

• Lead seasonal learning reviews and maintain clear records of lessons and decisions to continue, adapt or stop interventions or crop offerings.

Build and manage a high-performing team

• Set clear goals, roles and decision-making responsibilities, and hold the team accountable for timely, high-quality delivery.

• Coach direct reports, strengthen the team’s technical expertise and support staff to take on greater ownership.

Career Growth and Development

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

Qualifications

Across all roles, these are the general qualifications we look for. For this role specifically, you will have:

Technical Expertise

• A bachelor's degree in Agronomy, Crop Science, Agricultural Systems, Agricultural Extension, Sociology, Anthropology, Design or a related field;

• Experience working in the agricultural sector, ideally with smallholder farmers, is strongly preferred.

• At least 5+ years of relevant professional experience in Agricultural Extension, Human-Centred Design, Social Behaviour Change Campaigns, or Rural Marketing, with experience applying these approaches in the agricultural sector

• Demonstrated experience developing, testing or scaling agronomic recommendations or rural extension interventions.

• Experience using adult-learning, instructional-design, SBCC or human-centered design approaches is strongly preferred

Core skills

• Technical judgment: Able to assess agronomic evidence, identify limitations and translate it into responsible recommendations.

• Farmer-centered design: Able to understand farmer constraints and create practical interventions that improve understanding and adoption.

• Data and learning: Comfortable using qualitative and quantitative evidence to make decisions; strong Excel skills required, with R or Stata as an advantage.

• Strategy and project management: Able to prioritize, build critical paths and keep multiple seasonal workstreams on track.

• Communication: Able to make complex technical information simple and persuasive for field teams, farmers, leaders and external partners.

• Collaboration and influence: Able to work across Field Operations, Innovations, MEL and government-facing teams without relying solely on formal authority.

• People leadership: Able to set high standards, coach others and build a healthy, accountable team culture.

Cultural Fit & Communication

• Value Alignment: Deeply aligned with One Acre Fund values: Farmers First, Work Hard, Grow Through Feedback, and Own Your Results.

• Communication: Clear, compelling written and verbal style with a strong eye for data presentation and visual design (English required).

• Commitment: Willingness to relocate and commit to living in Africa (Malawi) for at least two years for a long-term career track.

Preferred Start Date

As soon as possible

Job Location

Zomba, Malawi

Benefits

Health insurance, housing, and comprehensive benefits

Eligibility

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Kenya, Malawi, Ethiopia, Uganda, Tanzania, Nigeria, Rwanda, Burundi, Zambia and the Democratic Republic of Congo.

Application Deadline

16 December 2026. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @oneacrefund.org address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.

Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization’s mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.

We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.

jobs.description:
Elastic, the Search AI Company, enables everyone to find the answers they need in real time, using all their data, at scale — unleashing the potential of businesses and people. The Elastic Search AI Platform, used by more than 50% of the Fortune 500, brings together the precision of search and the intelligence of AI to enable everyone to accelerate the results that matter. You will understand and tackle our customer’s business issues with the Elastic Stack, engage the regional Elastic community through events and programs, and enable sales through our Partners. jobs.title: Program Manager I, Senior Living
jobs.description:
Program Manager I – Home Health

Location: Falls Church, VA
Coverage Area: Alexandria, Springfield, and Mount Vernon
Schedule: Monday–Friday, 8:30 a.m.–5:00 p.m.
Compensation: up to $90,000–$95,000 annually, plus opportunity for quarterly incentives

Make a meaningful impact in the communities we serve

Our BAYADA Fairfax Senior Living team is seeking a relationship-focused Program Manager I to support our Home Health practice across senior living communities in Alexandria, Springfield, and Mount Vernon. This field-based role is ideal for a clinically licensed professional who is organized, personable, growth-minded, and motivated by the opportunity to strengthen partnerships and improve the experience of the individuals and communities we serve.

As Program Manager I, you will execute our provider-of-choice commitments and serve as a key connection point between the BAYADA Fairfax Senior Living office team, community teams, and clinical teams. You will help grow and maintain the business by building trusted relationships, coordinating priorities, and ensuring our services consistently meet the needs of our senior living partners and their residents.

What you’ll do

• Build and maintain strong, collaborative relationships with senior living community partners, office teams, and clinical teams.

• Execute BAYADA Fairfax Senior Living’s provider-of-choice commitments across the assigned territory.

• Serve as a consistent, responsive partner to community leadership and internal stakeholders.

• Identify opportunities to grow and maintain Home Health and outpatient business within the territory.

• Visit senior living communities regularly—up to five days per week—to understand needs, address concerns, and support service excellence.

• Coordinate communication and follow-through across community, operational, and clinical teams.

• Represent BAYADA professionally and reinforce a culture centered on compassion, excellence, and reliability.

• Organize competing priorities, manage follow-up, and ensure commitments are completed on time.

• Participate in an initial 90-day orientation that includes clinical and senior living orientation.

What you’ll bring

Required

• An active clinical license in good standing.

• Bachelor's degree.

• Strong organizational, communication, and relationship-building skills.

• A reliable, self-directed approach and the ability to manage work across multiple locations.

• A valid driver’s license and ability to travel throughout the assigned territory.

Preferred

• Experience in Home Health, senior living, outpatient care, or a related healthcare environment.

• Professional background as a PT, PTA, OT, COTA, SLP, RN, LPN, or another clinically licensed discipline.

• Experience building partnerships, supporting growth, or coordinating care across teams.

We welcome candidates from a range of clinical disciplines. Compensation will be based on experience, scope, and qualifications.

Work model and schedule

This is a field-based role with regular travel to senior living communities throughout Alexandria, Springfield, and Mount Vernon. The position may also require occasional visits to the Falls Church office. The standard schedule is Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. There is no on-call requirement.

Why join BAYADA?

• Make a visible difference in the lives of clients, residents, families, and community partners.

• Work alongside office, community, and clinical teams committed to dependable, high-quality care.

• Receive a structured 90-day orientation, including clinical and senior living training.

• Build meaningful relationships across an established and growing territory.

• Earn a competitive salary of $90,000–$95,000, with the opportunity for quarterly incentives.

BAYADA is committed to creating a caring, collaborative environment where team members can build trusted relationships and contribute to future excellence in the communities we serve.

As an accredited, regulated, certified, and licensed home health care provider, BAYADA complies with all state/local mandates.

BAYADA is celebrating 50 years of compassion, excellence, and reliability. Learn more about our 50th anniversary celebration and how you can join in here.

jobs.title: Senior Technical Program Manager - AppEx
jobs.description:
At Snowflake, we are powering the era of the agentic enterprise. To usher in this new era, we seek AI-native thinkers across every function who are energized by the opportunity to reinvent how they work. You don’t just use tools; you possess an innate curiosity, treating AI as a high-trust collaborator that is core to how you solve problems and accelerate your impact. We look for low-ego individuals who thrive in dynamic and fast-moving environments and move with an experimental mindset — who rapidly test emerging capabilities to discover simpler, more powerful ways to deliver results. At Snowflake, your role isn't just to execute a function, but to help redefine the future of how work gets done.

Snowflake is about empowering enterprises to achieve their full potential, and people too. With a culture that's all in on impact, innovation, and collaboration, Snowflake is the sweet spot for building big, moving fast, and taking technology and careers to the next level.

We are hiring a Senior /Technical Program Manager for our Application Experience (AppEx) organization. AppEx is the engineering org that builds the surfaces developers and data engineers love — from Streamlit and Notebooks to Native Apps, Cortex Code, Snowpark drivers, and the developer platform that ties it all together. This TPM will drive high-visibility programs that span multiple AppEx teams and define how tens of thousands of developers experience Snowflake's capabilities every day.


AS A SENIOR / STAFF TECHNICAL PROGRAM MANAGER, YOU WILL:

 - Own and drive complex, cross-functional programs across AppEx engineering teams — spanning application surfaces, developer tooling, AI-powered experiences, and the underlying platform — from scoping through delivery

 - Partner with Engineering Managers, Product Managers, and Principal Engineers to define program roadmaps, surface dependencies, and build execution plans that hold up under real-world complexity

 - Serve as the connective tissue across AppEx sub-orgs (Applications, Notebooks, Native Apps, Drivers, AIML, Developer Platform) to keep programs aligned and unblocked

 - Establish and maintain clear reporting cadences — tracking milestones, risks, decisions, and engineering health — and proactively escalate when things need leadership attention

 - Drive cross-org alignment on shared APIs, integration points, and developer-facing feature launches that touch multiple Snowflake product surfaces

 - Identify systemic friction in how AppEx teams plan and deliver; design lightweight processes and tooling-backed workflows to improve engineering velocity and predictability

 - Represent AppEx programs to senior leadership with crisp, data-backed status and recommendations


OUR IDEAL SENIOR / STAFF TECHNICAL PROGRAM MANAGER WILL HAVE:

 - 7+ years of technical program management experience at a cloud software company, with a track record of owning complex, cross-team programs end-to-end

 - Deep familiarity with developer-facing products or platform engineering — you understand what it takes to build great developer experiences and the challenges that come with shipping at scale

 - Demonstrated ability to work directly with engineers and architects, going deep on technical design when needed while keeping program execution on track

 - Strong cross-functional leadership skills: you've driven alignment across Engineering, Product, Design, and Go-to-Market without formal authority

 - Comfort operating in ambiguity — you can define structure where none exists and make progress while not all the answers are clear yet

 - Excellent written and verbal communication; you're effective in front of engineers, executive stakeholders, and everyone in between

 - Experience with modern cloud-native software development lifecycle, including CI/CD, release management, and API-first development

 - Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent experience


BONUS POINTS FOR THE FOLLOWING:

 - Hands-on experience with Snowflake, data platforms, or developer tooling products (Streamlit, Notebooks, Native Apps, Spark, etc.)

 - Prior exposure to AI/ML product development programs or agentic application delivery

 - Experience driving developer ecosystem programs — SDKs, drivers, or developer relations-adjacent work

 - Familiarity with program management tooling (Linear, Jira, Shortcut) and data-driven program health dashboards

 - Prior experience in a high-growth, post-IPO technology company environment


WHY JOIN THE APPEX TEAM AT SNOWFLAKE?

AppEx is one of the most cross-cutting and high-visibility engineering organizations at Snowflake. The team owns the developer-facing surface area — the products developers open every morning to build, analyze, and deploy. From Streamlit's growth as a first-class app framework, to Notebooks as a unified analytics environment, to Native Apps enabling Snowflake's application ecosystem, to Cortex Code bringing AI-native development to the data cloud — AppEx ships the surfaces that define how the world experiences Snowflake.

As the first TPM embedded in AppEx, you'll have a greenfield opportunity to shape what great program management looks like in this org — building the foundations, tools, and operating rhythms that will scale with the team. This isn't a seat at the table; it's an invitation to build the table.

Snowflake is growing fast, and we’re scaling our team to help enable and accelerate our growth. We are looking for people who share our values, challenge ordinary thinking, and push the pace of innovation while building a future for themselves and Snowflake.

How do you want to make your impact?

For jobs located in the United States, please visit the job posting on the Snowflake Careers Site for salary and benefits information: careers.snowflake.com http://careers.snowflake.com

jobs.title: Senior Manager, Finance
jobs.description:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.



We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.



We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.



If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.



About the Role:

Join Crusoe's Finance team as an embedded strategic and operational partner to Manufacturing leadership. This role reports into the Director of Finance, Manufacturing. You will design new processes from the ground up to meet the changing needs of a fast-growing organization, improve existing ones, and bring a financial lens to business decision making. Your work will directly shape the financial trajectory of the business unit and its long-term success.



You will work cross-functionally with the Manufacturing org, R&D, Accounting, Data Center, and Cloud teams, acting as a co-pilot in steering the business toward its financial goals. This is a builder role. We are looking for someone who can operate at the ground level and as a strategic leader across multiple stakeholders to drive decisions.



This role is based in our Denver office, with at least two days per week spent at our manufacturing locations in Arvada and Brighton. Some light travel is required.



What You'll Be Working On:

 - Planning & Forecasting: Own end-to-end financial planning cycles for the manufacturing business line, including the annual budget, long-range plan (LRP), monthly rolling forecasts, and month- and quarter-end close support.

 - Executive Reporting: Build clear, actionable performance narratives for executive, board, and investor materials.

 - Strategic Financial Modeling: Build and scale complex financial models to support the commercialization and roll-out of Crusoe Spark™ modular AI factories.

 - Business Partnership: Act as the primary financial advisor and hands-on "on-the-floor" partner to Manufacturing leadership, providing data-driven insights on strategic and operational decisions, and translating those decisions into near- and long-term financial impact.

 - Scenario Analysis: Deliver robust modeling and scenario analysis for new initiatives, capacity planning, customer profitability, and market expansion.

 - Driver-Based Analysis: Translate operational drivers such as production efficiency, utilization, and operational uptime into P&L impacts and actionable recommendations.

 - Cost Accounting & Product Costing: Partner with corporate accounting to establish standard costing frameworks, manage inventory valuation, track variances, monitor excess and obsolete (E&O) risk, and deliver insights on cost drivers to support margin management and investment decisions.

 - Profitability & Efficiency Initiatives: Proactively identify risks and opportunities to improve margins and operational efficiency, partnering with operational teams to develop improvement plans.

 - Process Improvement: Design new processes required by business growth and improve existing ones in close collaboration with Accounting, Corporate Finance, and Manufacturing teams.

 - Process & Control Integrity: Ensure compliance with corporate policies, internal controls, and audit requirements.



What You'll Bring to the Team:

 - Strong manufacturing finance background with working knowledge of cost accounting.

 - 8+ years of progressive finance experience, including at least 3 years supporting a business unit P&L.

 - Capital budgeting and resource planning experience.

 - Advanced financial modeling skills, with the ability to build driver-based models, sensitivity analyses, and complex operational scenarios from the ground up.

 - Strong business acumen. You connect financial analysis to operational and strategic levers, look around corners, and translate risks and opportunities into financial impact.

 - Demonstrated ability to translate complex operational data into clear financial insights and executive-ready narratives.

 - Proven track record of working with and influencing senior stakeholders across multiple functions.

 - Proactive and self-driven, and comfortable thriving in a fast-paced, high-intensity environment while managing multiple priorities. You don't wait to be asked. You identify problems, instinctively seek solutions, and take ownership of outcomes.

 - Excellent Excel and PowerPoint skills, plus experience with ERP systems (e.g., Acumatica, Oracle, SAP) and financial planning or BI tools.

 - Strong communication skills and the ability to build effective relationships with project management and technical teams, translating project-specific updates into financial impact analysis.

 - Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related analytical field, or equivalent practical experience. MBA, CFA, or CPA a plus.

 - Experience in a high-growth technology, infrastructure, energy, or data center environment strongly preferred.



Benefits:

 - Competitive compensation and equity packages

 - Restricted Stock Units

 - Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

 - Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

 - Employer contributions to HSA account

 - Paid parental leave

 - Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

 - Professional development & tuition reimbursement

 - Mental health & wellness support

 - Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

 - Cell phone stipend

 - 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

 - Volunteer time off

 - Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

 - Daily meals allowance

 - Additional perks & programs specific to location



Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $170,000 to $205,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

jobs.title: Senior Instrumentation & Controls Engineer - Spark
jobs.description:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.



We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.



We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.



If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.




ABOUT THIS ROLE

As a Senior Instrumentation & Controls Engineer supporting Crusoe's modular data center platform, you will own the control system deliverables for major systems inside the modules we manufacture. Modular is how Crusoe compresses the timeline from steel to compute, and that speed only holds when the controls package is repeatable, verified in the factory, and correct the first time it lands in the field. You will independently produce and defend the point lists, instrument schedules, and control system drawings for your assigned systems, then prove them out through factory acceptance testing before a module ships.

This role sits at the point where design intent meets manufactured hardware. You will move between the design desk and the factory floor, adapting standards to non-standard conditions, resolving equipment substitutions and installation deviations without waiting for direction, and making the judgment calls that keep a production line moving. Your deliverables become the reference that construction, commissioning, and operations teams build against, and you will mentor Engineer I and II teammates on the standards behind them. Denver is your home base, with estimated travel at 25% to manufacturing partners and deployment sites. This is a full-time position.




WHAT YOU'LL BE WORKING ON

 - System Design Ownership: Own the I&C design deliverables for assigned building-level or major systems, including point lists, I/O assignments, instrument schedules, and control system drawings from concept through as-built.

 - Factory Acceptance Testing Leadership: Develop and execute FAT protocols on control panels and integrated modules, adjudicate discrepancies against design intent, and hold the release gate before shipment.

 - Non-Standard Condition Resolution: Resolve equipment substitutions requiring control specification updates, field installation deviations, and calibration discrepancies by adapting established procedures with minimal guidance.

 - Platform Standardization: Improve the repeatable design packages, drawing templates, and test procedures that let the modular platform scale across successive builds, feeding lessons from the factory floor back into the standard.

 - Vendor and Integrator Coordination: Lead technical coordination with control panel fabricators, systems integrators, and instrument suppliers on submittal review, specification compliance, and closure of open technical items.

 - Commissioning Readiness: Coordinate control loop checkout, startup support, and field verification activities so modules arrive at deployment sites commissioning-ready with accurate documentation.

 - Mentorship: Coach Instrumentation & Controls Engineer I and II teammates on Crusoe's control platforms, documentation standards, and field verification practices, and review their deliverables before release.

 - Schedule Accountability: Track your I&C deliverable schedule against project milestones and flag risk to design and deployment leadership early enough to act on it.




WHAT YOU'LL BRING TO THE TEAM

 - Instrumentation & Controls Depth: 5 to 8 years of professional experience in industrial instrumentation and controls, with demonstrated independent ownership of design deliverables across the design and commissioning lifecycle.

 - PLC Proficiency: Strong working command of Rockwell and Allen-Bradley platforms, including Studio 5000 and ControlLogix or CompactLogix hardware, and the ability to read, modify, and troubleshoot existing logic.

 - SCADA Capability: Hands-on experience with Ignition SCADA or a comparable platform, including tag architecture, screen development, historian configuration, and troubleshooting integration issues.

 - Testing and Commissioning Rigor: Proven ability to author and execute test procedures, drive discrepancies to closure, and make release decisions on the accuracy of your own verification.

 - Field and Factory Judgment: Comfort operating in active manufacturing and construction environments, with the credibility to work through installation and calibration issues directly with technicians, trades, and vendors.

 - Documentation Discipline: A track record of producing accurate, well-documented deliverables that downstream construction and operations teams can rely on without rework.

 - Mandatory Education: A Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics, Control Systems Engineering, or a related technical discipline.




BONUS POINTS

 - Data Center or Mission-Critical Experience: Prior work on data center mechanical or electrical control systems, or in another high-availability industrial environment.

 - Modular or Prefabricated Delivery: Experience supporting a productized or prefabricated equipment platform where design repeatability and factory verification drive schedule.

 - Protocol Depth: Practical fluency in Modbus TCP, BACnet, or OPC UA within multi-vendor integration environments.

 - Systems Integrator Perspective: Experience on the integrator or EPC side of control system delivery, and an understanding of how scope, submittals, and acceptance criteria are negotiated.

 - OT Cybersecurity Awareness: Working knowledge of industrial network segmentation and OT security practices as applied to control system deployments.

 - Professional Credentials: Relevant certifications such as network certifications, Rockwell or Inductive Automation credentials.

 - Mission Alignment: A genuine interest in energy and AI infrastructure, and in the engineering rigor required to build it at speed.





Benefits:

 - Competitive compensation and equity packages

 - Restricted Stock Units

 - Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

 - Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

 - Employer contributions to HSA account

 - Paid parental leave

 - Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

 - Professional development & tuition reimbursement

 - Mental health & wellness support

 - Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

 - Cell phone stipend

 - 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

 - Volunteer time off

 - Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

 - Daily meals allowance

 - Additional perks & programs specific to location



Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $130,000 -$150,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicants knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

jobs.title: Technical Product Manager - DevEx
jobs.description:
Our mission

We're making Africa the first cashless continent.

In 2017, over half the population in Sub-Saharan Africa had no bank account. That's for good reason—the fees are too high, the closest branch can be miles away, and nobody takes cards. Without access to financial institutions, people are forced to keep their savings under the mattress. Small business owners rely on lenders who charge extortionate rates. Parents spend hours waiting in line to pay school fees in cash.

We're solving this by building financial services that just work: no account fees, instantly available, and accepted everywhere. In places where electricity, water and roads don't always work, you can still send money with Wave. In 2017, we launched a mobile app in Senegal for cash deposit, withdrawal, and peer-to-peer and business payments. Now, we have millions of users across 9 countries and are growing fast.

Our goal is to make Africa the first cashless continent and that's where you come in...

How you'll help us achieve it

Your mission is to make it dramatically easier for our engineers to ship features and learn from them quickly, securely, and reliably. You'll aim for small-startup speed while meeting the quality bar of a large financial institution. Velocity here means removing friction and toil from the path between idea and learning, not asking people to work harder.

AI is a big part of the opportunity, and we're looking for a PM who is optimistic about its possibilities but pragmatic about what actually works. The goal is not to adopt the latest shiny AI tool; it's to deeply understand your internal users, experiment, and honestly evaluate what solves their problems, whether that's AI, process changes, or boring tooling that just works.

The Technical Product Manager - DevEx will:

• Lead a team of engineers with full ownership of how we deliver new features for our users and use AI solutions to remove impactful friction for our engineers and product managers.

• Define product goals, metrics, and roadmaps based on user needs and mission impact.

• Drive user research within our engineering and product teams.

• Write clear, compelling design docs and facilitate async, fast-moving decision-making.

• Over-communicate context, priorities, and decisions to ensure team alignment.

• Adjust priorities quickly based on feedback, experiments, or new learnings.

• Solve problems holistically, whether through product features, ops tooling or process changes.

In this role, you'll...

• Own the developer experience holistically, including any internal or external tooling needed to support it.

• Research and implement solutions for how we can use AI to remove engineering and development friction.

• Build your own prototypes to test ideas where possible.

• Relentlessly gather feedback (by talking to users and looking at data) to deeply understand the problem space and our engineers' and product managers' needs.

• Work from first principles to understand the engineers' and product managers' biggest problems and then figure out how our tooling should work to solve those problems.

• Prioritize the biggest problems blocking the engineers' and product managers' productivity and the impact on delivering value to our users fast and securely.

• Directly manage the DevEx team to help them grow in their careers, partnering with the Tech Lead, who will own the technical bar.

Key Details

• This is a fully remote role. Candidates must be based in one of our talent hub countries (UK, Spain, USA (East Coast), Canada, Kenya and Ghana) or in one of our operating markets in Africa including Senegal, Côte d'Ivoire, or Burkina Faso

• Wave provides a yearly $1,200 stipend to support co-working meetups with teammates.

• Remote team members are expected to travel to our operational markets (e.g. Senegal or Côte d'Ivoire) at least once per year. Exceptions apply, but we’ve found this key to understanding our users and product.

• Our salaries are competitive and are calculated using a transparent formula. For this role, depending on your level and location, we offer a salary up to $237,500 USD, plus a generous equity package.

• Major benefits: Subsidized health insurance for you and your dependents, and retirement contributions (both vary from country to country). 6 months of fully paid parental leave and subsidized fertility assistance. Flexible vacation, with most folks taking between 21-30 days per year. $10,000 annual charitable donation matching.

Requirements

• Have 3+ years of product management experience and hands-on engineering background (you’ve shipped production code) or direct PM ownership of a developer experience, or developer productivity function.

• Proven success in overseeing all elements of the product development lifecycle, such as user research, design, implementation and evaluation.

• Speak fluent English

• Bonus if you: Have proven experience with successfully rolling out AI-based solutions in a larger org Have professional experience in a consumer fintech company

You might be a good fit if you

• Resonate deeply with how we do product and have experience working that way.

• Are continuously iterating on using AI in real workflows with honest evaluation.

• Are a strong communicator who can inspire and lead by influence.

• Are great at coordinating across teams and excel at communicating across multiple cultures.

• Take ownership for outcomes and do whatever you can to make them close to inevitable.

• Have strong instincts for asking questions that could move the needle.

• Have the courage and persistence to replan when feedback or new information arrives.

• Always listen with empathy but ruthlessly prioritize based on impact.

About Product at Wave

Product has always been very important to us at Wave, starting from day one with two very strong product-minded founders. Product Managers play a central role in our organization, impacting large chunks of the company around them, similar to the founders they were shaped after years ago.

Our approach to building products may not be what you’ve seen in other places. Our processes are lightweight, informed by principles instead of methodologies and our PMs don’t just manage backlogs full of polished tickets. Read our write-up on product at Wave!

If you’re excited to own a real problem end-to-end, set your own goals, and guide a team toward outcomes that matter for real people, you’ll feel right at home here.

If that’s you, we’d love to meet you.

Our team

• We have a rapidly growing in-country team in Senegal, Côte d'Ivoire, Mali, Burkina Faso, The Gambia, Uganda, Niger, Sierra Leone, and Cameroon plus remote team members spread across the world.

• We're deeply passionate about our mission of bringing radically affordable financial services to the people who need them most.

• We foster autonomy for our employees. You'll own your projects at every stage, from understanding the problem to monitoring your solution in production.

• We raised the largest Series A in Africa in 2021. Our world-class investors, include Founders Fund, Sequoia Heritage, Stripe, Ribbit Capital, Y Combinator, and Partech Africa.

• We are on Y Combinator's top companies by revenue.

How to apply

Fill out the form below, and upload a resume in English and a cover letter describing your interest in Wave and the role.

We review applications frequently and recommend that you apply to the role that most closely aligns with your skills, experience and career goals.

Wave is an equal-opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

jobs.title: Automation Engineer I
jobs.description:
About Lucid

At Lucid, we are creating exceptional mobility experiences through innovation to drive the world forward. Built on Lucid’s proprietary technology and software-defined vehicle architecture, our award-winning vehicles bring our “Compromise Nothing™” approach to the global automotive market. That means refusing to choose between performance and sustainability, design and engineering, ambition and integrity. In Lucid Air and Lucid Gravity, we have designed and built vehicles that have redefined their segments, combining exceptional range, performance, design, and expansive space in a single experience.

We achieve this through deep vertical integration, with design, engineering, and production happening in-house across our global offices and manufacturing facilities. Our teams come from industries around the world, united by a shared commitment to excellence. By refusing to settle, you can help redefine what’s possible and shape the future of mobility.

The Automation Engineer, Powertrain will be responsible of ensuring new and existing control systems meet throughput, safety, and quality requirements for production, as well as designing and developing continuous improvement projects according to the company's needs.

You Will:

• Have familiarity with equipment control systems, equipment I/Os and basic machine coding logic.

• Work with layout engineering to prepare and optimize Powertrain line layouts

• Experience working with the following equipment: robotics, end of arm tooling, pick and place automation, position sensors, material handling, fluid dispensing, vision systems, conveyor and laser cleaning and welding.

• Develop company level, factory level, and line/machine level controls standards and specification for application by internal equipment development team and external partners

• Create data management and tracking communications network architecture and interface with cross-functional teams for product, processes and quality traceability control implementation

• Architect, write and debug PLC ladder logic with an emphasis on generating code that is organized, structured, documented, maintainable and reusable. PLC code will interact with subsystems such as conveyors, robots, Manufacturing Execution System (MES), LabView, machine vision, and 3rd party equipment

• Implement (ANSI/RIA15.06/OSHA compliant) control reliable safety systems for safeguarding robots, gantries, conveyors, and other high volume manufacturing equipment

• Generate aesthetically simple HMI screens for complex machinery while providing sufficient feedback for troubleshooting

• Enforce application of Lucid Motors standards, Manage external integrators during specification, design review, design approval

• Establish test plans and control test plan execution at Vendor and at Lucid Motors facility during installation and buy-off

• Train Maintenance and Production teams to support automated equipment after deployment into production

• Create machine interactions with plant-wide Manufacturing Execution System (MES) to communicate product acceptability, machine status, and process variables

• Debug and optimize automated processes to maximize cycle time, improve availability and yield

You Bring:

• Bachelor’s Degree in Electrical, Mechanical, Computer engineering or related field is preferred, a combination of years of experience may be considered in lieu of degree

• 0 - 2+ years of experience in an Automation Engineering role in the automotive industry

• Proficiency with process integration and electromechanical / mechatronic systems

• In-depth knowledge of Safety standards (ANSI/RIA15.06, OSHA).

• Advanced proficiency programming industrial equipment:

• Ladder logic PLCs (Allen Bradley ControlLogix, CompactLogix and RSLogix 5000)

• Safety PLCs (Allen Bradley ControlLogix, SmartGuard, etc)

• Human Machine Interface (IGNITION IS A MUST)

• Field bus Networks (Ethernet IP, Safety rated field bus networks)

• Serial communication (RS-232) between PLCs and instruments

• Ethernet communications between machine PLCs and database systems

• Demonstrated excellence in programming PLCs. Must have a well-defined methodology for maintaining code structure and organization. Ability to program state machines for complex processes which involve multi-station parallel processing, pick and place automation, data acquisition, and PID control. Proven ability to design fault-tolerant systems with error handling and recovery

• Proficiency selecting appropriate circuit protectors, wire and cable, sensors, safety hardware, PLC hardware, remote I/O, VFD and servo systems

• Exposure to a wide variety of production machinery, industrial sensors, and equipment (LVDT and pressure transducers, dispense systems, temperature controllers, DC nut runner torque controllers, current and power meters, etc)

• Experience programming Fanuc Robots is a plus

• Experience with Vision systems (Cognex, Keyence, Fanuc) is desired

• Experience creating technical specifications for automated manufacturing equipment is highly desired

• Experience transitioning products and processes from prototype to production desired

• Knowledge of production quality metrics is a plus

• Ability to use 3D CAD packages such as with SolidWorks and CATIA is a plus

Compensation & Benefits: Lucid offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package including medical, dental, and vision insurance; life and disability coverage; paid time off; paid holidays, paid sick leave; and a 401(k) retirement plan. Hourly/non-exempt employees accrue up to 120 hours paid time off, and salaried/exempt employee accrue up to 160 hours paid time off.  Eligible employees may also participate in Lucid’s equity program and/or a discretionary annual cash incentive program. Incentive and equity awards, if applicable, are determined based on individual performance, role scope, market considerations, and overall company results, in accordance with the terms of the applicable plans.

Equal Opportunity: At Lucid, we believe diversity strengthens everything we build. Lucid Motors is proud to be an equal opportunity employer and is committed to providing an inclusive workplace for all. We consider all qualified applicants without regard to race, color, national or ethnic origin, age, religion, disability, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity or expression, marital status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable state or federal laws and regulations.

Accessibility: Lucid Motors is committed to providing reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities. If you need any accommodation to participate in the application process, please contact us at TA-Operations <@> lucidmotors.com. This email address is designated solely for accommodation requests and is not monitored for job applications or resume submissions. To be considered for employment, all applications must be submitted through the Lucid Motors Careers website.

Candidate Data Privacy: By submitting your application, you understand and agree that your personal data will be processed in accordance with our Candidate Privacy Notice.

To all recruitment agencies: Lucid Motors does not accept agency resumes. Please do not forward resumes to Lucid Motors. Lucid Motors is not responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes.

jobs.title: Associate GTM Recruiter
jobs.description:
ABOUT RAMP

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Ramp is scaling the Sales Development org, and we're hiring a Recruiter to help build it. SDR hiring is its own discipline: the bar is high, the volume is real, and the strongest candidates rarely have a track record long enough to read. 

You'll work with our Sales Development recruiter, owning full-cycle SDR hiring: sourcing, screening, scheduling, and offer close. It's a foundational seat with real autonomy. You'll work as a team to build the playbook. The SD team you're hiring for moves fast, with consistent quota beats and frequent promotions.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own pipeline hygiene in Ashby, moving candidates through stages, keeping data clean, and flagging what's stuck.

 - Schedule and coordinate interviews across hiring managers, panelists, and candidates.

 - Run clear, timely candidate communication and a consistently good candidate experience, even at high volume.

 - Keep scorecards and business case materials up to date and consistently applied, so hiring managers test the same way every time.

 - Flag process friction early instead of waiting for someone else to catch it.

 - Use AI daily for drafting outreach, summarizing notes, and speeding up research.

WHAT YOU NEED

 - 0 to 2 years in recruiting, sales, or a candidate/client-facing role. SDR/BDR experience is a strong plus.

 - A track record of overachieving against a goal or quota, in any context.

 - Genuinely good at multitasking, with many candidates and stakeholders in motion at once and nothing slipping.

 - High emotional intelligence: reads a room accurately, adapts on the fly, and knows when to push and when to hold back.

 - Trustworthy with sensitive comp and candidate information.

 - Highly organized, catching what's off before it becomes a problem.

 - Strong written communication.

 - Low ego, high curiosity, comfortable learning the craft rather than just executing a checklist.

 - Genuine interest in using AI as part of daily workflow.




BENEFITS AVAILABLE TO ALL FULL-TIME RAMP EMPLOYEES (GLOBAL)

jobs.title: Staff Software Architect
jobs.description:
About Taskrabbit:

Taskrabbit is a marketplace platform that conveniently connects people with Taskers to handle everyday home to-do’s, such as furniture assembly, handyman work, moving help, and much more.

At Taskrabbit, we want to transform lives one task at a time. As a company we celebrate innovation, inclusion and hard work. Our culture is collaborative, pragmatic, and fast-paced. We’re looking for talented, entrepreneurially minded and data-driven people who also have a passion for helping people do what they love. Together with IKEA, we’re creating more opportunities for people to earn a consistent, meaningful income on their own terms by building lasting relationships with clients in communities around the world.

Taskrabbit is a hybrid company with employees distributed across the US and EU and a Built In — Best Places to Work (2022, 2023, 2024, 2025) continually ranked across multiple national and regional categories. Join us at Taskrabbit, where your work will be meaningful, your ideas valued, and your potential unleashed!

Prior to applying please note:

• This role is hybrid requiring 2 days in office at our San Francisco hub every Tuesday & Wednesday (located at 130 Sutter St, San Francisco, CA).

About the Role:

The Architecture Team drives Taskrabbit's Platform Modernization efforts, guiding engineering teams toward our Target State Architecture (TSA). As a Staff Software Architect, you'll serve as an embedded representative of the Architecture team, partnering with engineering teams across the platform to accelerate their modernization work.

You'll operate as a subject matter expert on platform modernization within a small team of architects, applying AI-assisted and Spec-Driven Development (SDD) practices to help teams build new components using our Target State Architecture stack of technologies. This role is hands-on and results-oriented: pairing directly with engineers and technical leads, not just advising from the sidelines.

You will be:

• Acting as the Architecture team's representative to assigned engineering teams, driving platform modernization projects in accordance with the TSA.

• Applying AI tooling and Spec-Driven Development practices to help teams modernize the parts of the platform they own.

• Pairing with engineers and technical leadership to unblock modernization work and transfer architectural patterns directly into team practice.

• Serving as a subject matter expert on platform modernization, advising on migration approach, sequencing, and risk.

• Advocating for TSA-aligned solutions in technical discussions, including working through design discussions with engineering leads and other stakeholders.

• Collaborating with a small team of architects to maintain consistency across modernization efforts platform-wide.

• Writing and reviewing Technical Design Documents (TDDs) and RFCs, and coaching authors to strengthen their proposals.

• Defining standards for tooling, coding, processes, AI usage, and documentation strategies that make modernization repeatable across teams.

This is not a purely consultative role. You're expected to engage directly with projects and drive results forward — TDDs, code, and outcomes.

You should have:

• 8+ years of professional experience in software development, with a primary focus on building and scaling backend systems.

• Demonstrated experience with distributed systems and event-driven architecture.

• TypeScript/Node.js experience preferred; candidates with a background in another strongly typed language (e.g., Java, .NET) will also be considered.

• Experience with containerization and containerized application deployment.

• An enthusiast for AI tooling and AI-assisted development practices, with a proven track record of applying them professionally.

• Excellent communication skills, with the ability to build consensus and keep technical design discussions professional and productive, even when opinions differ strongly.

• Willingness to lead, speak up, and be visible and vocal in Architecture and team design meetings.

• Comfort pairing directly with engineers and technical leadership, not just producing documentation or recommendations.

Bonus Criteria:

• Experience with Kubernetes (K8s).

• Experience with the NestJS framework.

• Experience designing or using Helm charts.

• Experience with Spec-Driven Development tools such as SpecKit, OpenSpec, Intent, Kiro, or similar.

• Experience with ArgoCD.

• Experience with Datadog.

• Experience with contract-first design using OpenAPI and AsyncAPI.

Compensation & Benefits:

At Taskrabbit, our approach to compensation is designed to be competitive, transparent, and equitable. Total compensation consists of base pay + bonus + benefits + perks. The base pay range for this position is $150,000 - $200,000. This range is representative of base pay only, and does not include any other total cash compensation amounts, such as company bonus or benefits. Final offer amounts may vary from the amounts listed above and will be determined by factors including, but not limited to, relevant experience, qualifications, geography, and level.

You’ll love working here because:

• Taskrabbit is a Hybrid Company. We value flexibility and choice but also stay committed to regular in-person connection.

jobs.title: Outreach Leader
jobs.description:
About Hopscotch Primary Care

At Hopscotch Primary Care, we believe great healthcare should be accessible to all people across all communities.  Today, almost 20% of Americans live in a rural community, yet only 11% of physicians practice in those same communities.  We are on a mission to transform healthcare in rural America.  We provide high-quality primary care tailored to meet the needs of our patients through our robust care model and comprehensive care team, delivering care in our clinics, and across settings, and wrapping resources around the patients who need them most.

Our patients and the care teams who serve them sit at the center of everything we do at Hopscotch.  Hopscotch Primary Care takes a team approach to serve patient needs and provide the best care possible.  Our goal is to provide the care each of us would want for ourselves or for our family members, in the right setting, and at the right time.

Today, we are serving thousands of patients in our value-based care model and the number is growing every day.  If you want to bring your experience, skill and passion to make a lasting impact in healthcare, we’d like to meet you.

About the Role

This is a field-based sales role focused on growing our patient population.

As an Outreach Leader, you'll be responsible for identifying, developing, and managing relationships that generate new patients for Hopscotch Primary Care. You'll spend your time in the community meeting with prospective patients, local organizations, referral partners, businesses, senior groups, and community leaders to educate them about Hopscotch and help eligible individuals enroll as patients.

Success in this role comes from building trust, creating new opportunities, developing a strong sales pipeline, and consistently achieving patient growth goals.

You'll have significant autonomy to build your territory, execute your outreach strategy, and drive measurable results.

This position is home-based in the greater Asheville, NC area and requires daily local travel throughout Buncombe County.

What You'll Do

Drive Patient Growth

• Own patient acquisition goals within your assigned territory

• Build and execute a territory sales plan to achieve monthly and quarterly enrollment targets

• Prospect for new opportunities through networking, cold outreach, community engagement, and referrals

• Identify, qualify, and convert prospective patients into active Hopscotch patients

• Develop and maintain a healthy pipeline of leads and manage opportunities through every stage of the enrollment process

• Track sales activity, conversion metrics, and pipeline performance using CRM tools

Build Community Partnerships

• Develop strong relationships with community organizations, senior centers, churches, employers, healthcare providers, pharmacies, and other referral sources

• Identify new partnership opportunities that increase awareness and patient referrals

• Serve as the face of Hopscotch Primary Care throughout your territory

• Represent Hopscotch at community events, health fairs, educational programs, and networking opportunities

Relationship Management

• Build lasting relationships with patients, caregivers, and community partners

• Follow up with new patients to ensure a positive onboarding experience

• Collect market intelligence and community feedback to improve outreach efforts

• Collaborate closely with Marketing, Clinic Operations, and Care Teams to maximize growth opportunities

Sales Planning & Performance

• Develop territory growth strategies and action plans

• Monitor key sales metrics including leads, conversions, enrollments, and partnerships

• Maintain accurate CRM documentation and activity reporting

• Continuously evaluate outreach efforts and adjust strategies to improve results

About You

This role is ideal for someone who loves meeting new people, enjoys building relationships, and is motivated by achieving goals. We're looking for someone with the drive, resilience, and relationship-building skills that make great sales professionals successful.

A great candidate for the role:

• Is ambitious, organized, and energetic

• Is empathetic and an active listener

• Is a self-starter who is resourceful and doesn’t need a lot of direction to succeed

• Has a drive to succeed and want to control their own income

• Has an ability to quickly connect and influence the right people

• Builds trust quickly and can handle tough conversations

• Is collaborative and contributes to the effectiveness to the overall team

• Demonstrates good judgement professionally and ethically at all times

• Enjoys talking with seniors

• Is comfortable using email, Microsoft Office applications, and computer reporting tools; CRM experience preferred

Qualifications

Required

• High school diploma or equivalent

• 2+ years of sales, business development, account management, or customer-facing experience

• Valid driver's license and reliable transportation

• Ability to travel locally throughout the assigned territory

• U.S. work authorization

Preferred

• Bachelor's degree

• Healthcare, Medicare, insurance, or value-based care experience

• Experience using a CRM (Salesforce or similar)

• Experience working with older adults or community organizations

At Hopscotch Primary Care, we embrace diversity, invest in a culture of inclusion and positivity and encourage all to apply to join our team.  You will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status.
