jobs.title: Procurement Specialist II
jobs.description:
The field of gene therapy is growing rapidly and Genezen is here to meet the exacting needs of our clients. We provide process development, produce GMP viral vectors, and provide cell transduction for gene and cell therapy clinical trials and are proud to be a part of the process that leads to new cures.

WORKING AT GENEZEN

Many people have worked in environments where you feel like just another nameless part of an enormous machine. Genezen is different. We want our employees to be innovative, collaborative problem solvers who are dedicated to meeting the challenges of working at a fast-growing company. We are dedicated to empowering our employees to be their best and making Genezen a rewarding place to work. Every employee contributes to the success of the company and you can be part of that team.

JOB SUMMARY

The Procurement Specialist II role is integral to the on-time delivery of compliant materials for Operations. This role supports the day-to-day purchasing of materials and management of vendors by working with internal stakeholders and managing external relationships. These activities are performed in accordance with cGMP guidelines and departmental and inter-departmental policies and standard operating procedures.

JOB RESPONSIBILITIES

• Assist in the procurement of GMP materials in compliance with company policies and procedures.

• Monitor inventory levels and support analysis of historical trends to help prevent stockouts.

• Support the tracking and reporting of supplier freight and expedite costs.

• Coordinate with vendors to gather quotes, confirm lead times, and process purchase orders.

• Assist in managing supplier documentation, including Vendor Change Notifications and Corrective Action Requests, under the guidance of senior staff.

• Maintain and update item master data in the ERP system as directed.

• Support internal teams by gathering information and helping assess material needs.

• Learn and apply GMP and procurement best practices through daily activities and team training.

• Meet with internal customers to assess needs and create forecasts.

• Work effectively with cross-functional teams including but not limited to Finance, Manufacturing, Quality Assurance, Quality Control, Planning/Scheduling and Warehouse.

SPECIAL JOB REQUIREMENTS

• Adaptability required as work schedule may change based on business needs.

• Criminal background check required.

• Other duties as assigned.

EDUCATION / CERTIFICATIONS / LICENSES

• BS/MS degree in business or related field (e.g., Business Management, Supply Chain, or Finance)

• APICS Certification

ON-THE-JOB EXPERIENCE

• 2-4 years of relevant GMP experience in pharma/biotech company, working within a quality system and regulated GMP environment

• 1-2 years experience working with ERP systems

• Well versed in cGMP/ICH/FDA/EU regulations and guidelines

SKILLS / ABILITIES

• Supplier/Vendor Management

• Inventory Management & Analysis

• Excellent computer, verbal, and written communication skills

• Ability to work independently with minimal supervision, as well as working effectively as part of a team

• Ability to adapt quickly to change, such as but not limited to ideas, responsibilities, and strategies

• Analytical problem solving

COMPENSATION RANGE

The annual salary range for this position is $80,000-$95,000.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is required to meet the following physical demands:

Work Environment

• Regularly sit for long periods of time.

Movement

• Frequently required to stand; sit; walk; balance; stoop; kneel; crouch; use hands to finger, handle, or feel; reach with hands and arms

• Occasionally required to walk; climb or balance; and stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl

Lifting

• Frequently lift and/or move up to 10 pounds.

• Frequently lift and/or move up to 25 pounds

Vision

• Frequently utilize close vision and the ability to adjust focus

Communication

• Frequently required to communicate by talking, hearing, using telephone and e-mail

GENEZEN'S CURES VALUE-BASED COMPETENCIES

Committed to Science
We are committed to scientific excellence, staying current with industry developments, making data-driven decisions, and pursuing innovation to advance healthcare.

Urgency in action for the patients
We operate with urgency and a commitment to delivering timely treatments to patients by accelerating our partners' programs.

Resilience & Grit in operations
We are committed to overcoming challenges, learning from failures, and persistently striving for success.

Execute with Excellence & Integrity
We are dedicated to delivering quality results and upholding ethical principals.

Solutions driven for our partners
We are committed to being a proactive, collaborative, creative and open-minded partner.

GENEZEN'S BENEFITS

• Paid vacation days, amount based on tenure

• Paid sick time

• 10 observed holidays + 2 floating holiday + 1 volunteer day

• 401(k) plan with company match up to 6% of salary

• Share Appreciation Rights

• Choice of several healthcare plans

• FSA and HSA programs

• Dental & vision care

• Employer-paid basic term life/personal accident insurance

• Voluntary disability, universal life/personal accident insurance

• Accidental Death & Dismemberment (AD&D) Insurance

ADDITIONAL DETAILS

• Nothing in the job description for this role restricts management’s right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time.

• This position requires a criminal background check.

• Genezen is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

• Genezen participates in EVerify.

• Genezen is interested in every qualified candidate who is eligible to work in the United States; however, we are not able to sponsor visas.

Genezen has operates two locations: one in Fishers, Indiana and the second in Lexington, Massachusetts.

Fishers is a suburb of Indianapolis. Fishers was named the #1 place to live in the US by Money Magazine in 2017 for its livability, safety and entrepreneurship. Fishers is one of the fastest growing communities in Indiana and is dedicated to supporting a high quality of life for all its residents. Nearby Indianapolis is home to professional and college sports teams, the Indy 500, a growing art community and the world’s largest children’s museum--to name just a few reasons why this area is a great place to live.

Lexington, Massachusetts, located just northwest of Boston, is renowned as a historic suburb with a rich cultural heritage. It boasts picturesque New England charm, tree-lined streets, and a vibrant community. Known for its pivotal role in the American Revolution, Lexington offers visitors and residents alike a blend of historical landmarks, modern amenities, and a strong sense of community pride.

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager, Ad Monetization
jobs.description:
RevenueCat gives app businesses the infrastructure and tools to build, run, and improve their monetization. Since graduating from YC's S18 batch, we've grown into the default monetization platform for mobile. 

We're in 50%+ of newly shipped subscription apps, we process $16B+ in annual purchase volume, and we help everyone from a solo developer to the OpenAI mobile team understand and grow their revenue.

We're a remote-first team of 150+ people across 25+ countries, guided by values we actually practice: Customer Obsession, Always Be Shipping, Own It, and Balance. 

This isn't the right fit for everyone. The systems you’ll build here manage billions of dollars and touch hundreds of millions of end users, and we don’t take that lightly. You'll be expected to work hard and hold a high bar for what you ship, alongside some of the sharpest, most driven people you've worked with. If that sounds energizing rather than exhausting, keep reading.


THE ROLE

As Senior Product Manager, Ad Monetization, you'll join a small product and engineering team building RevenueCat's next generation of monetization products for app developers.

Ads at RevenueCat are early, but we're no longer starting from zero. Ad revenue tracking is live, along with rewarded-ad infrastructure including in-app currency, entitlement grants, and server-side reward validation. We've seen strong early adoption and are entering the next phase of investment in the space.

You'll report to our product lead for Ads and become the primary IC product owner for ad monetization. You'll own significant parts of the roadmap end-to-end: understanding customer problems, identifying opportunities, forming hypotheses, working closely with engineering and design, shipping quickly, and using what we learn to determine what comes next.

This is still a fast-moving initiative with significant strategic latitude. We're specifically looking for someone who has built ad monetization products for mobile apps, ideally at a mediation platform, ad network, SSP, or similar company serving app publishers. You should already understand the ecosystem well enough to contribute a strong point of view while remaining willing to challenge your assumptions as we learn.




ABOUT YOU:

 - You have 5+ years of experience owning product decisions end-to-end. Your title may have been Product Manager, founder, or something else — what's important is that you've been accountable for deciding what to build and whether it worked.

 - You've built and shipped publisher-facing ad monetization products for mobile apps, and have firsthand experience solving the product, technical, and business problems involved in helping developers monetize ad inventory.

 - You deeply understand the mechanics of mobile ad monetization, including how publisher inventory, demand sources, auctions, pricing, mediation, and measurement interact.

 - You understand the incentives of the different participants in the ad ecosystem and can reason about both the technical and commercial implications of product decisions.

 - You are excited about RevenueCat's mission to help developers make more money and about expanding that mission beyond subscriptions.

 - You have an entrepreneurial mindset and are excited to take an initiative with early traction and help turn it into a significant product area.

 - You are sufficiently technical to work closely with engineering on SDKs, APIs, integrations, data flows, and other technical product decisions.

 - You have demonstrated the ability to ship and learn quickly, including finding pragmatic solutions to hard problems with many constraints.

 - You are comfortable operating with ambiguity, making decisions under uncertainty, and taking responsibility for the outcomes of those decisions.

 - You communicate clearly across different audiences and media, particularly in writing.


IN THE FIRST MONTH, YOU'LL:

 - Build a deep understanding of what's live today, including ad revenue tracking, rewarded-ad infrastructure, and virtual currency and entitlement flows.

 - Spend significant time talking with customers using these products to understand what's working, what isn't, and where the biggest opportunities may be.

 - Build strong working relationships with your engineering, product, design, data, and go-to-market counterparts.

 - Develop context on our existing strategy, customer research, technical architecture and the hypotheses behind our current roadmap.

 - Begin contributing your own perspective on where RevenueCat should invest next.


WITHIN THE FIRST 3 MONTHS, YOU'LL:

 - Take ownership of a meaningful portion of the ad monetization roadmap.

 - Work closely with engineering to identify the fastest and most effective ways to validate our next set of product hypotheses.

 - Ship or meaningfully advance your first product bets.

 - Establish a strong understanding of the opportunities, constraints, and tradeoffs that should shape our roadmap.

 - Effectively collaborate with senior stakeholders on priorities for the area.


WITHIN THE FIRST 6 MONTHS, YOU'LL:

 - Independently drive product discovery, prioritization, and execution across your areas of the ad monetization roadmap.

 - Have shipped meaningful improvements for customers and developed clear signals about what we should invest in next.

 - Have a documented point of view on where RevenueCat should be headed in ad monetization over the longer term and what capabilities we'll need to get there.

 - Have materially improved RevenueCat's understanding of the ad monetization vendor ecosystem, customer needs, competitive landscape, and relevant industry trends.

 - Be recognized internally as a domain expert who can help the broader company reason about advertising and monetization.


WITHIN THE FIRST 12 MONTHS, YOU'LL:

 - Be the primary IC product owner for RevenueCat's ad monetization products.

 - Have shipped products that create measurable monetization value for our customers and establish a meaningful new growth opportunity for RevenueCat.

 - Have a credible, evidence-backed view of RevenueCat's longer-term opportunity in ad monetization and a roadmap for pursuing it.

 - Have shipped enough meaningful bets that you've also stopped, changed, or deprioritized something when the evidence showed it wasn't delivering the value we expected.


WHAT WE OFFER:

 - Competitive equity in a fast-growing, Series C startup backed by top-tier investors, including Y Combinator

 - 10-year window to exercise vested equity options

 - A fully remote environment designed around autonomy and flexibility.

 - 4-5 weeks of flexible time off annually

 - Paid desk at a co-working space

 - Workspace budget and continuous learning stipend


INTERVIEWING AT REVENUECAT

Our interview process is rigorous on purpose. We want to be sure that everyone we bring on is genuinely excited about this work, aligned with how we operate, and ready to meet our high bar for performance. Curious what that actually looks like? Read more in our blog post on how we hire at RevenueCat https://www.revenuecat.com/blog/company/how-we-hire-at-revenuecat/, including tips to help you succeed.


MORE ON HOW WE WORK:

jobs.title: Office Administrator
jobs.description:
OUR MISSION  


SPAN IS ENABLING ELECTRIFICATION FOR ALL ⚡

 


WE ARE A MISSION-DRIVEN COMPANY DESIGNING, BUILDING, AND DEPLOYING PRODUCTS THAT ELECTRIFY THE BUILT ENVIRONMENT, REDUCE CARBON EMISSIONS, AND SLOW THE EFFECTS OF CLIMATE CHANGE.

 - Making electrification upgrades possible

This is an onsite role, in our San Francisco office five days a week and supporting events at our South San Francisco office or other offsite events. We're looking for someone with 2+ years of administrative, executive or office management experience, sound judgment handling confidential information, strong communication skills, and genuine curiosity to learn about other areas of the business (ie: executive support, HR, recruiting, and workplace operations).

ABOUT YOU

LIFE AT SPAN

Headquartered in San Francisco’s vibrant SoMa neighborhood, we are an eclectic group of creative thinkers who value open communication, teamwork, and a ‘make it happen’ approach to addressing complex challenges. 

SPAN embraces diversity and equal opportunity in a serious way. We are committed to building a team that represents a variety of backgrounds, perspectives, and skills. 

We’re hiring talented individuals who are driven by success and are passionate about shaping the future of renewable energy. If that sounds like you, we’d love for you to consider joining the rapidly growing team at SPAN.

 


THE PERKS:

⚡ Competitive compensation + equity grants at a well-funded, venture-backed company

⚡ Comprehensive benefits: 100% employee premiums for base plans on medical, dental, vision with options for additional coverage.  Parental leave up to twenty four (24)  weeks depending on eligibility

CONDICIONES LABORALES

Exposición a:

Condiciones climáticas variables y, en ocasiones, adversas al retirar la basura y realizar otras tareas en el exterior.

Las temperaturas dentro de la tienda oscilan entre 36 grados en la nevera y 90 grados o más en algunas áreas de trabajo.

Cambios repentinos de temperatura en el área de trabajo y en el exterior. Vapores de olores de alimentos.

Exposición al polvo de harina de maíz.

Espacios reducidos, incluyendo cámaras frigoríficas.

Superficies/herramientas calientes del horno a temperaturas de hasta 260 °C o superiores.

Bordes afilados y piezas mecánicas móviles.

SENSORÍA

Hablar y oír por teléfono.

Visión de cerca y media distancia para la mayoría de las tareas en la tienda.

Percepción de profundidad.

Capacidad para diferenciar entre superficies calientes y frías.

TEMPERAMENTOS

Capacidad para dirigir actividades, realizar tareas repetitivas, trabajar solo y en equipo, trabajar bajo estrés, cumplir con estrictos estándares de control de calidad, tratar con personas, analizar y recopilar datos, y tomar decisiones.

Detalles adicionales del puesto: REQUISITOS FÍSICOS, incluyendo, entre otros:

De pie

La mayoría de las tareas se realizan de pie.

Caminando

Para distancias cortas y periodos cortos.

Las superficies incluyen ladrillos de cerámica con linóleo en algunas áreas de procesamiento de alimentos. La altura de las superficies de trabajo es de entre 36 y 48 pulgadas.

Sentado

El papeleo se realiza normalmente en una oficina, en un escritorio o mesa.

Levantar

Las entregas de productos a granel se realizan dos veces por semana o más, y el miembro del equipo las descarga utilizando una carretilla.

Las entregas pueden incluir cajas de ingredientes y suministros con un peso de hasta 50 libras y dimensiones de hasta 3' x 1.5'.

Las cajas generalmente se levantan del suelo y se apilan en estantes de hasta 72 pulgadas de altura.

Cargar

Las latas grandes, con un peso de 3 libras y 7 onzas, se transportan desde la estación de trabajo hasta los estantes de almacenamiento. Ocasionalmente, se transporta salsa de pizza de 13.6 kg desde el almacén hasta la entrada de la tienda.

Las bandejas de masa de pizza se transportan de tres en tres, recorriendo distancias cortas, y cada una pesa aproximadamente 5.4 kg.

Empujar

Mover bandejas colocadas en plataformas rodantes. Una pila de bandejas en una plataforma rodante pesa aproximadamente 10-13 kg y requiere una fuerza de hasta 3.4 kg para empujarlas.

También se pueden jalar las bandejas.

Escalar

Los miembros del equipo rara vez deben subir escaleras o usar una escalera para cambiar precios en los letreros, limpiar paredes o realizar tareas de mantenimiento.

Agacharse/Doblarse

Es necesario inclinarse hacia adelante en la estación de montaje de pizzas.

Hay espacio para los dedos de los pies, pero los trabajadores no pueden flexionar las rodillas mientras están de pie en esta estación.

La duración de esta posición es de aproximadamente 30 a 45 segundos, y se repite continuamente durante el día.

También se inclinan hacia adelante en el mostrador y al almacenar ingredientes.

Agacharse/En cuclillas

Se realiza ocasionalmente para reponer los estantes y limpiar las zonas bajas.

Estiramiento

Se realiza continuamente: arriba, abajo y hacia adelante.

Los trabajadores se estiran por encima de 72 pies ocasionalmente para encender/apagar los controles del horno, cambiar los precios en los letreros y subir y bajar objetos de los estantes.

Los trabajadores se estiran para realizar tareas como sacar harina de maíz de un barril de plástico o lavar platos.

Los trabajadores se estiran hacia adelante para obtener ingredientes, limpiar superficies de trabajo o contestar el teléfono.

Tareas manuales

La coordinación ojo-mano es esencial. El uso de las manos es continuo durante la jornada.

Con frecuencia, las actividades requieren el uso de una o ambas manos.

Dar forma a la masa de pizza requiere el uso frecuente y enérgico de los antebrazos y las muñecas.

Los trabajadores deben manipular una pala para pizza al sacar la pizza del horno y al usar el cortador.

Se requiere pinzar con frecuencia o con fuerza para ensamblar cajas de pizza de cartón. Los miembros del equipo deben poder agarrar latas, el teléfono, el cortador de pizza, la pala y las cajas de pizza.

Máquinas, herramientas, equipos, ayudas de trabajo

Los miembros del equipo podrían necesitar usar lápices/bolígrafos, computadoras, teléfonos, calculadoras, equipo TDD, cortador de pizza y pala.

jobs.title: Maintenance Technician - Twin Farms
jobs.description:
The Maintenance Technician supports the day-to-day maintenance, repair, safety, and overall care of Twin Farms’ buildings, equipment, grounds, and guest-facing spaces. This role is responsible for performing preventive and corrective maintenance, troubleshooting facility issues, completing repairs, assisting with renovations and light construction, and helping ensure the property remains safe, functional, and beautifully maintained for guests and team members.

This position requires strong technical ability, sound judgment, flexibility, and a service-minded approach. The Maintenance Technician should be comfortable working independently, responding to changing operational needs, and maintaining a professional and discreet presence in a luxury hospitality environment.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

• Perform preventive and corrective maintenance on buildings, equipment, guest rooms, public areas, back-of-house spaces, and property systems.
• Troubleshoot and repair maintenance issues related to plumbing, electrical, HVAC, painting, carpentry, small appliances, and general building systems.
• Complete light-duty construction, renovation, repair, and installation projects as assigned.
• Inspect buildings, mechanical systems, equipment, and property areas to identify repair needs, safety concerns, or preventive maintenance opportunities.
• Accurately read, interpret, sketch, and update water, gas, electric, plumbing, building, and property as-built drawings as needed.
• Perform basic electrical troubleshooting and repairs within the scope of experience, training, and applicable regulations.
• Perform basic soldering and plumbing repairs.
• Run tests, document findings, complete reports, and follow technical procedures and manufacturer specifications.
• Respond to maintenance requests in a timely, professional, and guest-sensitive manner.
• Prioritize work orders while remaining flexible to urgent guest, operational, or safety-related needs.
• Work with contracted tradespeople, vendors, and service providers to support repairs, inspections, projects, and preventive maintenance.
• Assist in monitoring supplies, tools, materials, and equipment needed for maintenance operations.
• Follow all safety procedures, including proper use of tools, equipment, PPE, and safe work practices.
• Maintain familiarity with OSHA general industry safety expectations, including confined space awareness.
• Communicate clearly with supervisors, team members, vendors, contractors, and other departments.
• Maintain a clean, organized, and safe work area, including maintenance shops, vehicles, and storage areas.
• Support snow removal, seasonal property needs, event support, and emergency maintenance response as needed.
• Maintain confidentiality and professionalism when working in guest rooms, private areas, and staff spaces.
• Perform other duties as assigned.

• Knowledge of materials, practices, tools, and safe work methods used in preventive and corrective maintenance of buildings and equipment.
• Familiarity with HVAC, painting, electrical, plumbing, general repair, renovation, and light construction.
• Basic understanding of electrical principles and theories.
• Ability to inspect, troubleshoot, repair, and maintain building systems and equipment.
• Ability to read and update water, gas, electric, plumbing, building, and property as-builts.
• Basic soldering skills.
• Ability to use experience and judgment to plan and complete a broad range of maintenance tasks with competing priorities.
• Ability to analyze and solve complex maintenance problems independently or in partnership with contracted tradespeople.
• Ability to run tests, document results, complete reports, and follow technical procedures.
• Strong organizational and prioritization skills, with the flexibility to adjust quickly to operational needs.
• Familiarity with OSHA general industry safety practices; confined space awareness preferred.
• Strong verbal communication skills, including the ability to provide and obtain clear information.
• Ability to communicate professionally with contractors, vendors, managers, team members, and guests.
• Strong interpersonal skills and a customer-oriented approach.
• Professional, positive, proactive, and discreet demeanor.
• Ability to maintain confidentiality and represent Twin Farms with professionalism.

Required Education, Experience, and Training

• High school diploma, equivalent, or vocational/technical degree required.
• Valid driver’s license with an acceptable driving record required.
• Minimum of three years of general maintenance experience in building, mechanical, HVAC, electrical, plumbing, and/or small appliance repair preferred.
• General maintenance experience in a hotel, resort, luxury property, or hospitality environment preferred.
• Familiarity with applicable local, state, and federal codes preferred.
• OSHA General Industry certification preferred.
• Water or wastewater operation training/certification a plus.

Physical Requirements

• Ability to stand, walk, bend, kneel, crouch, climb, reach, and work with hands for extended periods.
• Ability to lift, carry, push, or pull equipment, tools, and materials as needed.
• Ability to climb ladders and work in mechanical spaces, utility areas, and outdoor environments.
• Ability to work indoors and outdoors in varying weather conditions.
• Ability to respond to urgent maintenance needs and changing operational demands.
• Ability to safely operate tools, equipment, and company vehicles.

Work Environment

This position works throughout the Twin Farms property, including guest rooms, public areas, back-of-house spaces, mechanical areas, outdoor areas, and maintenance facilities. The role may require interaction with guests and must be performed with professionalism, discretion, and attention to the standards of a luxury hospitality environment.

Schedule

Schedule may vary based on business needs, seasonal demands, emergencies, and property coverage requirements. Weekends, holidays, evenings, on-call support, and weather-related response may be required.

At Twin Farms, we believe that when our team members are genuinely cared for, they are empowered to deliver extraordinary hospitality. Our benefits are thoughtfully designed to support well-being, provide stability, and encourage long-term professional growth.

Compensation: $24–$30 per hour, based on experience, certifications, and qualifications.

Our benefits include:

• Health, dental, and vision insurance with employer contributions
• Complimentary life insurance
• 401(k) retirement plan with employer match
• Paid vacation, holidays, and sick time
• Employee Assistance Program (EAP) with confidential support and resources
• Relocation and travel assistance for select roles
• Daily staff meal
• Training, professional development, and tuition assistance
• Employee referral bonuses
• Exclusive dining and lodging privileges

Because taking care of our people isn’t a perk, it’s a tradition.

jobs.title: Senior Domain Expert, Total Rewards
jobs.description:
Do you want to empower organizations to build smarter compensation strategies while ensuring fair pay for all employees?

Syndio is the leading pay governance and compensation intelligence platform. We help organizations make better pay decisions at every stage of the compensation lifecycle, from leveling and offers to promotions and merit. Our platform gives HR, compensation, and finance leaders the data and decision support they need to govern pay fairly, compliantly, and with confidence. We partner with many of the world’s most recognized and respected enterprises, helping them implement leading-edge compensation solutions with expert guidance and analyzing pay for over 10 million employees across the world.

Join us in our mission to help companies make smarter pay decisions they can trust!

About the role

Syndio is the leader in compensation equity and pay decision intelligence, helping the world's largest employers make fair, defensible, and transparent pay decisions at scale. As Decisions expands across the compensation lifecycle — from leveling and offers to promotions and merit — the compensation practice depth behind our recommendations has to keep pace.

The Senior Domain Expert (Total Rewards) is a hands-on compensation practitioner on the Applied Pay Intelligence team. Draw on your past experience in total rewards strategy as well as Syndio-provided training on pay equity best practices to provide expert advice on advanced pay equity topics to customers, fellow employees, and external audiences. This is a senior individual contributor role. You are the person our customers, our product, and the rest of the team turn to when the question is how pay should actually be structured — job architecture, market data, pay ranges, offer construction, geographic differentials — and how it should hold up in front of a CHRO, a comp committee, or a works council.

You own an area of Syndio's compensation content and product surface, build the 1:many resources that scale your expertise across the customer base, partner directly with Product to embed compensation practice into Decisions and Essentials, and show up in the customer conversations where the design choices have to hold. You will translate custom analytics into product requirements and support product and development teams as needed on design and implementation plans, partner with the data science and development teams to ensure the product helps advance the outcomes of our total rewards customers.

Why this job is exciting

• Lead a squad. You will be an individual contributor but you will own an area of Syndio's compensation content and product surface — job architecture, market data integration, pay range design, offer intelligence, or a related domain. Guide the squad's roadmap, prioritize what gets built on the Applied Expertise team, and hold the practitioner bar for the work that ships.

• Apply total rewards expertise in complex customer situations. Work through the design questions customers can't resolve inside the product: architecture redesigns, market data conflicts, range strategy, offer logic, geographic differentials. Bring the practice, explain the tradeoffs, defend the approach.

• Build 1:many resources. Turn recurring compensation questions into durable content — customer briefings, design guides, model communication templates, worked examples — so recurring questions do not require a recurring meeting.

• Partner with Product. Work directly with Product and AI teams to embed compensation practice into Decisions and Essentials. Shape offer recommendation logic, range and structure inputs, market data workflows. Catch the practitioner-level edge cases before customers do.

• Show up for the moments that matter. Anchor customer QBRs, offer strategy conversations, and architecture reviews where the design has to hold up under CHRO or board scrutiny. Not every meeting — the ones where getting the structure and the framing right changes the outcome.

• Feed the frameworks upward. Surface what current frameworks don't yet cover. Bring specific customer patterns and design gaps to the Principal-level colleagues and to Product so the platform's intelligence keeps compounding.

About you

• 5+ years of hands-on total rewards, compensation, or organizational design work, ideally with meaningful time in job architecture, market data, pay range design, or org design projects at enterprise scale.

• Deep facility with compensation practice: leveling frameworks, benchmarking methodology, salary structure design, offer construction, geographic differentials, incentive design.

• Experience translating compensation practice into something a broader team can execute — a playbook, a tool, a product, a set of standards — not just doing the work yourself.

• Demonstrated ability to hold a credible conversation with a CHRO, a comp committee, or an HRBP leadership team about design tradeoffs, and to write for those audiences.

• Strong judgment on the difference between presenting design options and prescribing outcomes, and comfort holding that line.

• Track record of building content, documentation, or enablement materials that reduce reliance on your calendar over time.

• Comfort thinking about how compensation expertise translates into AI-mediated product capability, particularly for offer recommendation and structure design in Decisions.

• Experience in HR tech, compensation SaaS, or a related enterprise domain is a strong plus.

Why you'll love it here:

• 💰 Competitive Compensation. For this role our salary is targeted at $142,000 -$167,000 per year. Final offer amounts are determined by factors such as experience and expertise. jobs.title: Customer Service Representative (6181) - Brownsville, TN
jobs.description:
IMMEDIATE HIRE! Short or Long shifts - YOUR CHOICE!

Flexible Scheduling! Part time and Full-time hours available – Work the shifts that work for you!

JOB REQUIREMENTS:

Must be 16 years of age or older. Must be able to pass a background check. Ability to add, subtract, multiply, and divide accurately and quickly (may use calculator). Must be able to make correct monetary change. Verbal, writing, and telephone skills to take and process orders. The ability to follow directives, perform repetitive tasks, work alone and well with others, work well under stress, meet strict quality control standards, provide excellent customer service, analyze and compile data, make good judgements and decisions.

WORK CONDITIONS

Exposure to:

• Varying and sometimes adverse weather conditions when removing trash and performing other outside tasks

• Sudden changes in temperature in work area and while outside - In-store temperatures range from 36 degrees in cooler to 90 degrees and above in some work areas

• Fumes from food odors

• Exposure to cornmeal dust

• Compact work areas including walk-in cooler

• Hot surfaces/tools including oven reaching 500 degrees or higher

• Sharp edges and moving mechanical parts

PHYSICAL DUTIES & REQUIREMENTS

Including but not limited to:

Lifting

Bulk product deliveries are made twice a week or more and are unloaded by the team member using a hand truck. Deliveries may include cases of ingredients and supplies weighing up to 50 pounds with dimensions of up to 3' x 1.5'. Cases are usually lifted from floor and stacked onto shelves up to 72" high.

Climbing

Team members must infrequently navigate stairs or climb a ladder to change prices on signs, wash walls, and perform maintenance.

Stooping/Bending

Forward bending at the waist is necessary at the pizza assembly station. Toe room is present, but workers are unable to flex their knees while standing at this station. Duration of this position is approximately 30 - 45 seconds at one time, repeated continuously during the day. Forward bending is also present at the front counter and when stocking ingredients. Crouching and bending peformed occasionally to stock shelves and clean low areas.

Reaching

Reaching is performed continuously; up, down and forward. Workers reach above 72" occasionally to turn on/off oven controls, change prices on sign, and lift and lower objects to and from shelves. Workers reaching down to perform such tasks as scooping cornmeal from a plastic barrel, or washing dishes. Workers reach forward when obtaining topping ingredients, cleaning work surfaces, or answering phones.

Hand Tasks

Eye-hand coordination is essential. Use of hands is continuous during the day. Frequent activities require use of one or both hands. Shaping pizza dough requires frequent and forceful use of forearms and wrists. Workers must manipulate a pizza peel when removing pizza from the oven, and when using the rolling cutter. Frequent and/or forceful pinching is required in the assembly of cardboard pizza boxes. Team Members must be able to grasp cans, the pizza cutter and pizza peel, and pizza boxes.

Sensing

Talking and hearing on telephone. Depth perception as well as Near and mid-range vision required for most in-store tasks. Ability to differentiate between hot and cold surfaces. Far and night vision required for driving

What makes driving for Domino's different than our competition?

OPPORTUNITY! Our Customer Service Representatives have the opportunity to work a schedule that works with their lives with flexible full-time and part-time shifts. Domino’s also offers a variety of promotional opportunities such as Shift Lead, Assistant Manager, General Manager and beyond! In fact, 90% of Domino's franchise owners started out as delivery drivers for Domino's!

DIVERSITY

Our mission is to recognize, appreciate, value and utilize the unique talents and contributions of all individuals. To create an environment where all team members, because of their differences, can reach their highest potential

Ready to join our team? Submit your application today!

This job posting is for a position in a store owned and operated by an independent franchisee, not Domino’s Pizza LLC, Domino’s Pizza Franchising LLC, or Domino’s Pizza, Inc. (“Domino’s Corporate”). This means, among other things, that the independent franchisee is alone responsible for and will independently make all decisions concerning employment matters for the store, including those relating to hiring, firing, discipline, supervision, compensation and benefits, staffing, and scheduling. Domino’s will not receive a copy of any application you submit for this job posting and will not have any control over whether you receive an interview and/or are ultimately hired. Further, Domino’s does not control and is not responsible for the employment policies and practices of independent franchisees. If you are hired for this job posting, the independent franchisee will be your only employer, and you will not be an employee of Domino’s.

jobs.title: Delivery Expert(02589)- 1004 E 4th Street
jobs.description:
ABOUT THE JOB

Do you know why Domino's Pizza hires so many drivers? Well, aside from the fact that our delicious pizza is the perfect solution for dinner for families all across the nation - we do it because we can. What do we mean by that, you ask? We mean that we offer a great flexible schedule that offers the hours you're looking for. That means you're free when you need to be. You'll have plenty of time left over for school, to hang with your friends, or whatever. Even if you need a second job for some extra cash, Domino's Pizza is the perfect place for you.

Right now Domino's is looking for qualified drivers to staff stores in your area. We're growing so fast it's hard to keep up, and that means Domino's has lots of ways for you to grow (if that's what you want), perhaps to management, perhaps beyond. Whether it's your hobby, main-gig, or supplemental job, apply online. We're bound to have just the thing for you.

JOB REQUIREMENTS AND DUTIES

You must be 18 years of age and have a valid driver's license with a safe driving record meeting company standards as well as access to an insured vehicle which can be used for delivery. You should possess navigational skills to read a map, locate addresses within designated delivery area and must be able to navigate adverse terrain including multi-story buildings.

ADVANCEMENT

Many of our team members began their careers as delivery drivers and today are successful Domino's franchise owners. From delivery driver to management, general manager to franchisee or Manager Corporate Operations, our stores offer a world of opportunity.

DIVERSITY

Our mission is to recognize, appreciate, value and utilize the unique talents and contributions of all individuals. To create an environment where all team members, because of their differences, can reach their highest potential.

SUMMARY STATEMENT

We take pride in our team members and our team members take pride in Domino's Pizza! Being the best pizza delivery company in the world requires exceptional team members working together. At Domino's Pizza, our people come first!

General Job Duties For All Store Team Members

· Operate all equipment.

· Stock ingredients from delivery area to storage, work area, walk-in cooler.

· Prepare product.

· Receive and process telephone orders.

· Take inventory and complete associated paperwork.

· Clean equipment and facility approximately daily.

Training

Orientation and training provided on the job.

Communication Skills

· Ability to comprehend and give correct written instructions.

· Ability to communicate verbally with customers and co-workers to process orders both over the phone and in person.

Essential Functions/Skills

· Ability to add, subtract, multiply, and divide accurately and quickly (may use calculator).

· Must be able to make correct monetary change.

· Verbal, writing, and telephone skills to take and process orders. Motor coordination between eyes and hands/fingers to rapidly and accurately make precise movements with speed.

· Ability to enter orders using a computer keyboard or touch screen.

· Navigational skills to read a map, locate addresses within designated delivery area.

· Must navigate adverse terrain including multi-story buildings, private homes, and other delivery sites while carrying product.

Work Conditions

EXPOSURE TO

· Varying and sometimes adverse weather conditions when removing trash and performing other outside tasks.

· In-store temperatures range from 36 degrees in cooler to 90 degrees and above in some work areas.

· Sudden changes in temperature in work area and while outside.

· Fumes from food odors.

· Exposure to cornmeal dust.

· Cramped quarters including walk-in cooler.

· Hot surfaces/tools from oven up to 500 degrees or higher.

· Sharp edges and moving mechanical parts.

· Varying and sometimes adverse weather conditions when delivering product, driving and couponing.

SENSING

· Talking and hearing on telephone. Near and mid-range vision for most in-store tasks.

· Depth perception.

· Ability to differentiate between hot and cold surfaces.

· Far vision and night vision for driving.

TEMPERAMENTS

The ability to direct activities, perform repetitive tasks, work alone and with others, work under stress, meet strict quality control standards, deal with people, analyze and compile data, make judgements and decisions.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS, including, but not limited to the following:

Standing

Most tasks are performed from a standing position. Walking surfaces include ceramic tile "bricks" with linoleum in some food process areas. Height of work surfaces is between 36" and 48".

Walking

For short distances for short durations

Delivery personnel must travel between the store and delivery vehicle and from the delivery vehicle to the customer's location.

Sitting

Paperwork is normally completed in an office at a desk or table

Lifting

Bulk product deliveries are made twice a week or more and are unloaded by the team member using a hand truck.

Deliveries may include cases of ingredients and supplies weighing up to 50 pounds with dimensions of up to 3' x 1.5'.

Cases are usually lifted from floor and stacked onto shelves up to 72" high.

Carrying

Large cans, weighing 3 pounds, 7 ounces, are carried from the workstation to storage shelves.

Occasionally, pizza sauce weighing 30 pounds is carried from the storage room to the front of the store.

Trays of pizza dough are carried three at a time over short distances, and weigh approximately 12 pounds per tray.

During delivery, carry pizzas and beverages while performing "walking" and "climbing" duties.

Pushing

To move trays which are placed on dollies.

A stack of trays on a dolly is approximately 24" - 30" and requires a force of up to 7.5 pounds to push.

Trays may also be pulled.

Climbing

Team members must infrequently navigate stairs or climb a ladder to change prices on signs, wash walls, perform maintenance.

During delivery of product, navigation of five or more flights of stairs may be required.

Stooping/Bending

Forward bending at the waist is necessary at the pizza assembly station.

Toe room is present, but workers are unable to flex their knees while standing at this station.

Duration of this position is approximately 30 - 45 seconds at one time, repeated continuously during the day.

Forward bending is also present at the front counter and when stocking ingredients.

Crouching/Squatting

Performed occasionally to stock shelves and to clean low areas.

Reaching

Reaching is performed continuously; up, down and forward.

Workers reach above 72" occasionally to turn on/off oven controls, change prices on sign, and lift and lower objects to and from shelves.

Workers reaching down to perform such tasks as scooping cornmeal from a plastic barrel, or washing dishes.

Workers reach forward when obtaining topping ingredients, cleaning work surfaces, or answering phones.

Driving

Deliver pizzas within a designated delivery area. A Team Member may make several deliveries per shift.

Machines, Tools, Equipment, Work Aids

Team Members may be required to utilize pencils/pens, computers, telephones, calculators, TDD equipment, pizza cutter and pizza peel.

Driving Specific Job Duties

Deliver product by car and then to door of customer.

Deliver flyers and door hangers.

Requires

Valid driver's license with safe driving record meeting company standards.

Access to insured vehicle which can be used for delivery.

General Job Duties For All Store Team Members

· Operate all equipment.

· Stock ingredients from delivery area to storage, work area, walk-in cooler.

· Prepare product.

· Receive and process telephone orders.

· Take inventory and complete associated paperwork.

· Clean equipment and facility approximately daily.

Training

Orientation and training provided on the job.

Communication Skills

· Ability to comprehend and give correct written instructions.

· Ability to communicate verbally with customers and co-workers to process orders both over the phone and in person.

Essential Functions/Skills

· Ability to add, subtract, multiply, and divide accurately and quickly (may use calculator).

· Must be able to make correct monetary change.

· Verbal, writing, and telephone skills to take and process orders. Motor coordination between eyes and hands/fingers to rapidly and accurately make precise movements with speed.

· Ability to enter orders using a computer keyboard or touch screen.

· Navigational skills to read a map, locate addresses within designated delivery area.

· Must navigate adverse terrain including multi-story buildings, private homes, and other delivery sites while carrying product.

Work Conditions

EXPOSURE TO

· Varying and sometimes adverse weather conditions when removing trash and performing other outside tasks.

· In-store temperatures range from 36 degrees in cooler to 90 degrees and above in some work areas.

· Sudden changes in temperature in work area and while outside.

· Fumes from food odors.

· Exposure to cornmeal dust.

· Cramped quarters including walk-in cooler.

· Hot surfaces/tools from oven up to 500 degrees or higher.

· Sharp edges and moving mechanical parts.

· Varying and sometimes adverse weather conditions when delivering product, driving and couponing.

SENSING

· Talking and hearing on telephone. Near and mid-range vision for most in-store tasks.

· Depth perception.

· Ability to differentiate between hot and cold surfaces.

· Far vision and night vision for driving.

TEMPERAMENTS

The ability to direct activities, perform repetitive tasks, work alone and with others, work under stress, meet strict quality control standards, deal with people, analyze and compile data, make judgements and decisions.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS, including, but not limited to the following:

Standing

Most tasks are performed from a standing position. Walking surfaces include ceramic tile "bricks" with linoleum in some food process areas. Height of work surfaces is between 36" and 48".

Walking

For short distances for short durations

Delivery personnel must travel between the store and delivery vehicle and from the delivery vehicle to the customer's location.

Sitting

Paperwork is normally completed in an office at a desk or table

Lifting

Bulk product deliveries are made twice a week or more and are unloaded by the team member using a hand truck.

Deliveries may include cases of ingredients and supplies weighing up to 50 pounds with dimensions of up to 3' x 1.5'.

Cases are usually lifted from floor and stacked onto shelves up to 72" high.

Carrying

Large cans, weighing 3 pounds, 7 ounces, are carried from the workstation to storage shelves.

Occasionally, pizza sauce weighing 30 pounds is carried from the storage room to the front of the store.

Trays of pizza dough are carried three at a time over short distances, and weigh approximately 12 pounds per tray.

During delivery, carry pizzas and beverages while performing "walking" and "climbing" duties.

Pushing

To move trays which are placed on dollies.

A stack of trays on a dolly is approximately 24" - 30" and requires a force of up to 7.5 pounds to push.

Trays may also be pulled.

Climbing

Team members must infrequently navigate stairs or climb a ladder to change prices on signs, wash walls, perform maintenance.

During delivery of product, navigation of five or more flights of stairs may be required.Stooping/Bending

Forward bending at the waist is necessary at the pizza assembly station.

Toe room is present, but workers are unable to flex their knees while standing at this station.

Duration of this position is approximately 30 - 45 seconds at one time, repeated continuously during the day.

Forward bending is also present at the front counter and when stocking ingredients.

Crouching/Squatting

Performed occasionally to stock shelves and to clean low areas.

Reaching

Reaching is performed continuously; up, down and forward.

Workers reach above 72" occasionally to turn on/off oven controls, change prices on sign, and lift and lower objects to and from shelves.

Workers reaching down to perform such tasks as scooping cornmeal from a plastic barrel, or washing dishes.

Workers reach forward when obtaining topping ingredients, cleaning work surfaces, or answering phones.

Driving

Deliver pizzas within a designated delivery area. A Team Member may make several deliveries per shift.

Machines, Tools, Equipment, Work Aids

Team Members may be required to utilize pencils/pens, computers, telephones, calculators, TDD equipment, pizza cutter and pizza peel.

Driving Specific Job Duties

Deliver product by car and then to door of customer.

Deliver flyers and door hangers.

Requires

Valid driver's license with safe driving record meeting company standards.

Access to insured vehicle which can be used for delivery.

jobs.description:
ABOUT THE JOB

You were born to be the boss. We know. You get up in the morning and you make sure everyone else in the house is doing what they need to do. Then you go to work and you make sure that everyone there is doing what they need to do, even your boss. You just do that because you've always done it. Well maybe it's time you moved up. You want to be the boss? Well now's your chance - Domino's Pizza is hiring bosses - more specifically assistant managers. It's a tough job, one that needs a natural like you. Of course, you'll need some skills - judgment, math and the ability to multitask.

You'll be working for a company that's fun and flexible. Not to mention, it's work experience you're going to use for a long time to come. You've had our pizza delivered to you, now help us be the best in pizza delivery. Go on, boss, show us what you've got. Apply now!

JOB REQUIREMENTS AND DUTIES

You are responsible for everything that happens during your shift. This includes all cost controls, inventory control, cash control and Customer relations. You must set the example. You must follow ALL policy and procedures 100% of the time and expect the same from your crew.

In addition: Staffing, Paperwork, Cost Controls, Cash control, Food management, Work to a Schedule, Perfect Image and adherence to standards, Great Customer Service, Attendance & punctuality, Transportation to/from work, Store cleanliness, Marketing, Profitability.

ADVANCEMENT

Many of our team members began their careers as delivery drivers and today are successful Domino's franchise owners. From delivery driver to management, general manager to franchisee or Manager Corporate Operations, our stores offer a world of opportunity.

DIVERSITY

Our mission is to recognize, appreciate, value and utilize the unique talents and contributions of all individuals. To create an environment where all team members, because of their differences, can reach their highest potential.

SUMMARY STATEMENT

We take pride in our team members and our team members take pride in Domino's Pizza! Being the best pizza delivery company in the world requires exceptional team members working together. At Domino's Pizza, our people come first!

QUALIFICATIONS

General job duties for all store team members

Operate all equipment.
Stock ingredients from delivery area to storage, work area, walk-in cooler.
Prepare product.
Receive and process telephone orders.
Take inventory and complete associated paperwork.
Clean equipment and facility approximately daily.

Training

Orientation and training provided on the job.

Communication Skills

Ability to comprehend and give correct written instructions.
Ability to communicate verbally with customers and co-workers to process orders both over the phone and in person.

Essential Functions/Skills

Ability to add, subtract, multiply, and divide accurately and quickly (may use calculator).
Must be able to make correct monetary change.
Verbal, writing, and telephone skills to take and process orders.
Motor coordination between eyes and hands/fingers to rapidly and accurately make precise movements with speed.
Ability to enter orders using a computer keyboard or touch screen.

WORK CONDITIONS

Exposure to

Varying and sometimes adverse weather conditions when removing trash and performing other outside tasks.
In-store temperatures range from 36 degrees in cooler to 90 degrees and above in some work areas.
Sudden changes in temperature in work area and while outside.
Fumes from food odors.
Exposure to cornmeal dust.
Cramped quarters including walk-in cooler.
Hot surfaces/tools from oven up to 500 degrees or higher.
Sharp edges and moving mechanical parts.

SENSING

Talking and hearing on telephone.
Near and mid-range vision for most in-store tasks.
Depth perception.
Ability to differentiate between hot and cold surfaces.

TEMPERAMENTS

The ability to direct activities, perform repetitive tasks, work alone and with others, work under stress, meet strict quality control standards, deal with people, analyze and compile data, make judgments and decisions.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS including, but not limited to the following:

Standing

Most tasks are performed from a standing position.

Walking

For short distances for short durations.
Surfaces include ceramic tile "bricks" with linoleum in some food process areas. Height of work surfaces is between 36" and 48".

Sitting

Paperwork is normally completed in an office at a desk or table.

Lifting

Bulk product deliveries are made twice a week or more and are unloaded by the team member using a hand truck.
Deliveries may include cases of ingredients and supplies weighing up to 50 pounds with dimensions of up to 3' x 1.5'.
Cases are usually lifted from floor and stacked onto shelves up to 72" high.

Carrying

Large cans, weighing 3 pounds, 7 ounces, are carried from the workstation to storage shelves.
Occasionally, pizza sauce weighing 30 pounds is carried from the storage room to the front of the store.
Trays of pizza dough are carried three at a time over short distances, and weigh approximately 12 pounds per tray.

Pushing

To move trays which are placed on dollies. A stack of trays on a dolly is approximately 24" - 30" and requires a force of up to 7.5 pounds to push.
Trays may also be pulled.

Climbing

Team members must infrequently navigate stairs or climb a ladder to change prices on signs, wash walls, perform maintenance.

Stooping/Bending

Forward bending at the waist is necessary at the pizza assembly station.
Toe room is present, but workers are unable to flex their knees while standing at this station.
Duration of this position is approximately 30 - 45 seconds at one time, repeated continuously during the day.
Forward bending is also present at the front counter and when stocking ingredients.

Crouching/Squatting

Performed occasionally to stock shelves and to clean low areas.

Reaching

Reaching is performed continuously; up, down and forward.
Workers reach above 72" occasionally to turn on/off oven controls, change prices on sign, and lift and lower objects to and from shelves.
Workers reaching down to perform such tasks as scooping cornmeal from a plastic barrel, or washing dishes.
Workers reach forward when obtaining topping ingredients, cleaning work surfaces, or answering phones.

Hand Tasks

Eye-hand coordination is essential. Use of hands is continuous during the day.
Frequently activities require use of one or both hands.
Shaping pizza dough requires frequent and forceful use of forearms and wrists.
Workers must manipulate a pizza peel when removing pizza from the oven, and when using the rolling cutter.
Frequent and/or forceful pinching is required in the assembly of cardboard pizza boxes.
Team Members must be able to grasp cans, the phone, the pizza cutter and pizza peel, and pizza boxes.

Machines, Tools, Equipment, Work Aids

Team Members may be required to utilize pencils/pens, computers, telephones, calculators, TDD equipment, pizza cutter and pizza peel.

DRIVING SPECIFIC JOB DUTIES

Deliver product by car and then to door of customer.
Deliver flyers and door hangers.

REQUIRES

Valid driver's license with safe driving record meeting company standards.
Access to an insured vehicle which can be used for delivery.

ESSENTIAL SKILLS

Navigational skills to read a map, locate addresses within designated delivery area.
Must navigate adverse terrain including multi-story buildings, private homes, and other delivery sites while carrying product.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS

Carrying

During delivery, carry pizzas and beverages while performing "walking" and "climbing" duties.

Driving

Deliver pizzas within a designated delivery area. A Team Member may make several deliveries per shift.

Walking

Delivery personnel must travel between the store and delivery vehicle and from the delivery vehicle to the customer's location.

Climbing

During delivery of product, navigation of five or more flights of stairs may be required.

WORK CONDITIONS

Exposure To

Varying and sometimes adverse weather conditions when delivering product, driving and couponing.

SENSING

Far vision and night vision for driving.

JOB REQUIREMENTS AND DUTIES

You are responsible for everything that happens during your shift. This includes all cost controls, inventory control, cash control and Customer relations. You must set the example. You must follow ALL policy and procedures 100% of the time and expect the same from your crew.

In addition: Staffing, Paperwork, Cost Controls, Cash control, Food management, Work to a Schedule, Perfect Image and adherence to standards, Great Customer Service, Attendance & punctuality, Transportation to/from work, Store cleanliness, Marketing, Profitability.

ADVANCEMENT

Many of our team members began their careers as delivery drivers and today are successful Domino's franchise owners. From assistant manager to general manager, general manager to franchisee or Manager Corporate Operations, our stores offer a world of opportunity.

DIVERSITY

Our mission is to recognize, appreciate, value and utilize the unique talents and contributions of all individuals. To create an environment where all team members, because of their differences, can reach their highest potential.

SUMMARY STATEMENT

We take pride in our team members and our team members take pride in Domino's Pizza! Being the best pizza delivery company in the world requires exceptional team members working together. At Domino's Pizza, our people come first!

General Job Duties For All Store Team Members

· Operate all equipment.

· Stock ingredients from delivery area to storage, work area, walk-in cooler.

· Prepare product.

· Receive and process telephone orders.

· Take inventory and complete associated paperwork.

· Clean equipment and facility approximately daily.

Training

Orientation and training provided on the job.

Communication Skills

· Ability to comprehend and give correct written instructions.

· Ability to communicate verbally with customers and co-workers to process orders both over the phone and in person.

Essential Functions/Skills

· Ability to add, subtract, multiply, and divide accurately and quickly (may use calculator).

· Must be able to make correct monetary change.

· Verbal, writing, and telephone skills to take and process orders. Motor coordination between eyes and hands/fingers to rapidly and accurately make precise movements with speed.

· Ability to enter orders using a computer keyboard or touch screen.

· Navigational skills to read a map, locate addresses within designated delivery area.

· Must navigate adverse terrain including multi-story buildings, private homes, and other delivery sites while carrying product.

Work Conditions

EXPOSURE TO

· Varying and sometimes adverse weather conditions when removing trash and performing other outside tasks.

· In-store temperatures range from 36 degrees in cooler to 90 degrees and above in some work areas.

· Sudden changes in temperature in work area and while outside.

· Fumes from food odors.

· Exposure to cornmeal dust.

· Cramped quarters including walk-in cooler.

· Hot surfaces/tools from oven up to 500 degrees or higher.

· Sharp edges and moving mechanical parts.

· Varying and sometimes adverse weather conditions when delivering product, driving and couponing.

SENSING

· Talking and hearing on telephone. Near and mid-range vision for most in-store tasks.

· Depth perception.

· Ability to differentiate between hot and cold surfaces.

· Far vision and night vision for driving.

TEMPERAMENTS

The ability to direct activities, perform repetitive tasks, work alone and with others, work under stress, meet strict quality control standards, deal with people, analyze and compile data, make judgments and decisions.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS, including, but not limited to the following:

Standing

Most tasks are performed from a standing position. Walking surfaces include ceramic tile "bricks" with linoleum in some food process areas. Height of work surfaces is between 36" and 48".

Walking

· For short distances for short durations

· Delivery personnel must travel between the store and delivery vehicle and from the delivery vehicle to the customer's location.

Sitting

Paperwork is normally completed in an office at a desk or table

Lifting

· Bulk product deliveries are made twice a week or more and are unloaded by the team member using a hand truck.

· Deliveries may include cases of ingredients and supplies weighing up to 50 pounds with dimensions of up to 3' x 1.5'.

· Cases are usually lifted from floor and stacked onto shelves up to 72" high.

Carrying

· Large cans, weighing 3 pounds, 7 ounces, are carried from the workstation to storage shelves.

· Occasionally, pizza sauce weighing 30 pounds is carried from the storage room to the front of the store.

· Trays of pizza dough are carried three at a time over short distances, and weigh approximately 12 pounds per tray.

· During delivery, carry pizzas and beverages while performing "walking" and "climbing" duties.

Pushing

· To move trays which are placed on dollies.

· A stack of trays on a dolly is approximately 24" - 30" and requires a force of up to 7.5 pounds to push.

· Trays may also be pulled.

Climbing

· Team members must infrequently navigate stairs or climb a ladder to change prices on signs, wash walls, perform maintenance.

· During delivery of product, navigation of five or more flights of stairs may be required.

Stooping/Bending

· Forward bending at the waist is necessary at the pizza assembly station.

· Toe room is present, but workers are unable to flex their knees while standing at this station.

· Duration of this position is approximately 30 - 45 seconds at one time, repeated continuously during the day.

· Forward bending is also present at the front counter and when stocking ingredients.

Crouching/Squatting

Performed occasionally to stock shelves and to clean low areas.

Reaching

· Reaching is performed continuously; up, down and forward.

· Workers reach above 72" occasionally to turn on/off oven controls, change prices on sign, and lift and lower objects to and from shelves.

· Workers reaching down to perform such tasks as scooping cornmeal from a plastic barrel, or washing dishes.

· Workers reach forward when obtaining topping ingredients, cleaning work surfaces, or answering phones.

Driving

· Deliver pizzas within a designated delivery area. A Team Member may make several deliveries per shift.

Hand Tasks

· Eye-hand coordination is essential. Use of hands is continuous during the day.

· Frequently activities require use of one or both hands. Shaping pizza dough requires frequent and forceful use of forearms and wrists.

· Workers must manipulate a pizza peel when removing pizza from the oven, and when using the rolling cutter.

· Frequent and/or forceful pinching is required in the assembly of cardboard pizza boxes.

· Team Members must be able to grasp cans, the phone, the pizza cutter and pizza peel, and pizza boxes.

Machines, Tools, Equipment, Work Aids

Team Members may be required to utilize pencils/pens, computers, telephones, calculators, TDD equipment, pizza cutter and pizza peel.

Driving Specific Job Duties

· Deliver product by car and then to door of customer.

· Deliver flyers and door hangers.

Requires

· Valid driver's license with safe driving record meeting company standards.

· Access to insured vehicle which can be used for delivery.

Whether it's your hobby, main-gig, or supplemental job, apply online. We're bound to have just the thing for you.

JOB REQUIREMENTS AND DUTIES

You must be 18 years of age and have a valid driver's license with a safe driving record meeting company standards as well as access to an insured vehicle which can be used for delivery. You should possess navigational skills to read a map, locate addresses within designated delivery area and must be able to navigate adverse terrain including multi-story buildings.

General Job Duties For All Store Team Members

· Operate all equipment.

· Stock ingredients from delivery area to storage, work area, walk-in cooler.

· Prepare product.

· Receive and process telephone orders.

· Take inventory and complete associated paperwork.

· Clean equipment and facility approximately daily.

Training

Orientation and training provided on the job.

All driver positions are paid hourly at minimum wage Washington $16.66 and maxiumum $16.66. Credit card tips, cash tips and a partial mileage reimbursement are paid at the end of each shift. Hourly is paid via check or direct deposit bi monthly.

Medical, Dental and Vision insurance are available to employees who have worked at least a year and who average at least 32 hours per week. If you have any questions about Benefits Qualifications, please contact HR@hamiltonholdings.net.

We abide by OR/WA State requirements for sick pay.

HOURS: All scheduled hours are based off what employee is available for and what the store needs. All positions are part time unless otherwise stated. Every employee has the opportunity to work into full time as long as the store has the hours to accommodate by completing training, being reliable for shifts and communicating full time needs with manager.

Communication Skills

· Ability to comprehend and give correct written instructions.

· Ability to communicate verbally with customers and co-workers to process orders both over the phone and in person.

· Ability to communicate and interact respectfully and effectively with people across cultures, abilities, genders, ethnicities, and races.

Essential Functions/Skills

· Ability to add, subtract, multiply, and divide accurately and quickly (may use calculator).

· Must be able to make correct monetary change.

· Verbal, writing, and telephone skills to take and process orders. Motor coordination between eyes and hands/fingers to rapidly and accurately make precise movements with speed.

· Ability to enter orders using a computer keyboard or touch screen.

· Navigational skills to read a map, locate addresses within designated delivery area.

· Must navigate adverse terrain including multi-story buildings, private homes, and other delivery sites while carrying product.

Work Conditions

EXPOSURE TO

· Varying and sometimes adverse weather conditions when removing trash and performing other outside tasks.

· In-store temperatures range from 36 degrees in cooler to 90 degrees and above in some work areas.

· Sudden changes in temperature in work area and while outside.

· Fumes from food odors.

· Exposure to cornmeal dust.

· Cramped quarters including walk-in cooler.

· Hot surfaces/tools from oven up to 500 degrees or higher.

· Sharp edges and moving mechanical parts.

· Varying and sometimes adverse weather conditions when delivering product, driving and couponing.

SENSING

· Talking and hearing on telephone. Near and mid-range vision for most in-store tasks.

· Depth perception.

· Ability to differentiate between hot and cold surfaces.

· Far vision and night vision for driving.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS, including, but not limited to the following:

Standing

Most tasks are performed from a standing position. Walking surfaces include ceramic tile "bricks" with linoleum in some food process areas. Height of work surfaces is between 36" and 48".

Walking

· For short distances for short durations

· Delivery personnel must travel between the store and delivery vehicle and from the delivery vehicle to the customer's location.

Sitting

Paperwork is normally completed in an office at a desk or table

Lifting

· Bulk product deliveries are made twice a week or more and are unloaded by the team member using a hand truck.

· Deliveries may include cases of ingredients and supplies weighing up to 50 pounds with dimensions of up to 3' x 1.5'.

· Cases are usually lifted from floor and stacked onto shelves up to 72" high.

Carrying

· Large cans, weighing 3 pounds, 7 ounces, are carried from the workstation to storage shelves.

· Occasionally, pizza sauce weighing 30 pounds is carried from the storage room to the front of the store.

· Trays of pizza dough are carried three at a time over short distances, and weigh approximately 12 pounds per tray.

· During delivery, carry pizzas and beverages while performing "walking" and "climbing" duties.

Pushing

· To move trays which are placed on dollies.

· A stack of trays on a dolly is approximately 24" - 30" and requires a force of up to 7.5 pounds to push.

· Trays may also be pulled.

Climbing

· Team members must infrequently navigate stairs or climb a ladder to change prices on signs, wash walls, perform maintenance.

· During delivery of product, navigation of five or more flights of stairs may be required.

Stooping/Bending

· Forward bending at the waist is necessary at the pizza assembly station.

· Toe room is present, but workers are unable to flex their knees while standing at this station.

· Duration of this position is approximately 30 - 45 seconds at one time, repeated continuously during the day.

· Forward bending is also present at the front counter and when stocking ingredients.

Crouching/Squatting

Performed occasionally to stock shelves and to clean low areas.

Reaching

· Reaching is performed continuously; up, down and forward.

· Workers reach above 72" occasionally to turn on/off oven controls, change prices on sign, and lift and lower objects to and from shelves.

· Workers reaching down to perform such tasks as scooping cornmeal from a plastic barrel, or washing dishes.

· Workers reach forward when obtaining topping ingredients, cleaning work surfaces, or answering phones.

Driving

· Deliver pizzas within a designated delivery area. A Team Member may make several deliveries per shift.

Hand Tasks

· Eye-hand coordination is essential. Use of hands is continuous during the day.

· Frequently activities require use of one or both hands. Shaping pizza dough requires frequent and forceful use of forearms and wrists.

· Workers must manipulate a pizza peel when removing pizza from the oven, and when using the rolling cutter.

· Frequent and/or forceful pinching is required in the assembly of cardboard pizza boxes.

· Team Members must be able to grasp cans, the phone, the pizza cutter and pizza peel, and pizza boxes.

Machines, Tools, Equipment, Work Aids

Team Members may be required to utilize pencils/pens, computers, telephones, calculators, TDD equipment, pizza cutter and pizza peel.

Driving Specific Job Duties

· Deliver product by car and then to door of customer.

· Deliver flyers and door hangers.

Requires

· Valid driver's license with safe driving record meeting company standards.

· Access to insured vehicle which can be used for delivery

We are currently looking for a driver who can work 20-30 hours a week. 2+ shifts would be closing shifts typically 5pm-1:30am/2am and the other 2-3 shifts would be evening shifts ranging in hours.

we are looking for a part time opener as well. Shifts are typically 10am-6pm. off time can vary.
