jobs.title: Senior Account Manager – North America
jobs.location: New York, NY or Chicago, IL
jobs.description:
InMobi Advertising is a global technology leader helping marketers win the moments that matter. Our advertising platform reaches over 2 billion people across 150+ countries and turns real-time context into business outcomes, delivering results grounded in privacy-first principles. Trusted by 30,000+ brands and leading publishers, InMobi is where intelligence, creativity, and accountability converge. By combining lock screens, apps, TVs, and the open web with AI and machine learning, we deliver receptive attention, precise personalization, and measurable impact.

Through Glance AI, we are shaping AI Commerce, reimagining the future of e-commerce with inspiration-led discovery and shopping. Designed to seamlessly integrate into everyday consumer technology, Glance AI transforms every screen into a gateway for instant, personal, and joyful discovery.  Spanning diverse categories such as fashion, beauty, travel, accessories, home décor, pets, and beyond, Glance AI delivers deeply personalized shopping experiences. With rich first-party data and unparalleled consumer access, it harnesses InMobi’s global scale, insights, and targeting capabilities to create high impact, performance driven shopping journeys for brands worldwide.

Recognized as a Great Place to Work, and by MIT Technology Review, Fast Company’s Top 10 Innovators, and more, InMobi is a workplace where bold ideas create global impact. Backed by investors including SoftBank, Kleiner Perkins, and Sherpalo Ventures, InMobi has offices across San Mateo, New York, London, Singapore, Tokyo, Seoul, Jakarta, Bengaluru and beyond.

At InMobi Advertising, you’ll have the opportunity to shape how billions of users connect with content, commerce, and brands worldwide. To learn more, visit www.inmobi.com

Overview of the Role:

The Senior Account Manager is part of the Direct & Programmatic Demand team, embedded within a revenue pod alongside a dedicated Sales Manager, and working closely with agencies and advertisers across the Americas. Reporting to the VP, Ad Sales, this role will own new customer onboarding, delivering success for their campaigns and new upsell/cross-sell opportunities — while leading internal coordination with sales planning, operations, creative solutions, insights, measurement partnerships, supply partnerships, and tech teams.

Client-facing and regionally embedded, the Lead AM is a primary point of contact for the agency, owns the health of the account post-sale, and is directly responsible for identifying and closing upsell opportunities — that build on the success of the campaigns they run.

Location: This role is open to candidates based in New York, NY or Chicago, IL. Some travel may be required for client meetings and events as needed.

The Impact You'll Make:

• Onboard new advertiser customers in your Revenue pod onto InMobi and Glance ad systems and infrastructure

• Own the end-to-end delivery and KPI optimization of every deal sold by Sales Manager partners — coordinating research, creative, attribution, ad operations, and any other specialist teams required to execute what was sold.

• Act as the client's day-to-day point of contact post-sale, managing quarterly account retention and growth plans, revenue and margin management, and overall account health.

• Own upsell and cross-sell goals for your managed accounts — and track all upsell activities in Salesforce.

• Partner with your Sales Managers to co-own the account's long-term strategy, bringing proactive, data-driven recommendations and account intelligence that support the pod's overall revenue growth targets.

• Lead campaign analysis and reviews; provide consultative guidance to clients in weekly or bi-weekly check-ins and quarterly business reviews (QBRs).

• Manage the full solution lifecycle for campaigns individually and across partner teams — pre-sale media planning support, client onboarding, campaign delivery, in-flight optimization, and post-campaign reporting and deliverables.

• Collaborate cross-functionally with product, revenue strategy, technical account management (TAM), product marketing, ad operations, creative, insights, agency development, and demand partner teams to ensure successful execution and fast resolution of client issues.

• Work with Technical Account Management and Ops teams to troubleshoot campaign issues, and liaise directly with third-party partners such as DSPs, DMPs, and measurement vendors.

• Escalate at-risk accounts early — pacing issues, unresolved service problems, or stakeholder changes at the client

• Prioritize your week around what each account in your book needs — a renewal conversation, a QBR, resolving a client issue

• Surface marketplace feedback and client insights to inform InMobi's broader product and go-to-market strategy

How You're Measured:

This role is goaled on two connected outcomes:

• Pod revenue growth — shared accountability with your Sales Manager partners for the overall revenue performance of the accounts in your pod

• Individual revenue contribution — a dedicated, separately tracked upsell target generated from the deals you manage, logged and measured in Salesforce

The Experience We Need:

• 8+ years of overall client success or account management experience, including at least 4 years in digital and/or programmatic advertising.

• A proven track record of owning post-sale account health and driving measurable retention and growth within existing client accounts, including experience carrying or contributing to an upsell/renewal target.

• Strong ownership instincts and proactive communication — comfortable operating as one half of a tight, paired pod (AM + Seller) rather than managing an undifferentiated account list.

• Strong account management and client success experience, including managing complex agency and brand relationships and co-owning account strategy with a sales partner

• Hands-on experience with major DSPs and platforms such as The Trade Desk (TTD), DV360, and Amazon DSP is a strong plus

• Demonstrated success partnering with cross-functional teams (Sales, Ad Ops, Creative, Insights, Product) and building trusted relationships internally

• Proficiency with Salesforce, Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, and analytics/BI tools

• Strong analytical skills — comfortable interpreting campaign data to identify performance trends, risks, and upsell opportunities, and translating them into clear client recommendations

• Excellent organizational and time-management skills, with the ability to manage multiple clients, campaigns, and stakeholders simultaneously, and to reprioritize quickly as account needs shift

• Willingness and flexibility to work with global teams across several time zones

• Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience

Why InMobi?

You'll be part of a global team shaping the future of the open internet's advertising ecosystem — with visible impact, a supportive and ambitious peer group, and continuous investment in your growth. InMobi offers competitive compensation, comprehensive benefits, and a culture built on ownership, curiosity, and results.

At InMobi, you’ll be surrounded by people who…

• Think big and act fast: We’re entrepreneurial, thrive in ambiguity, and love solving high-impact problems

• Are passionate, fanatically driven, and take immense pride in their work: We care deeply about the impact we create and continuously push our potential

• Own their outcomes: We take responsibility, make bold decisions, and execute with confidence

• Embrace freedom with accountability: We value autonomy and understand that trust comes with responsibility

• Believe in lifelong learning: We welcome feedback, challenge ourselves to grow, and aren’t afraid to take smart risks

jobs.title: QA Analyst
jobs.description:
Ingram Marine Group is looking for a QA Analyst to join our team. This role independently performs software quality assurance activities for application development projects, system enhancements, integrations, and production releases. This position develops and executes comprehensive testing, manages defects, identifies quality risks, and contributes to test automation efforts that improve coverage, efficiency, repeatability, and release confidence. The role collaborates with Business Analysts, Application Developers, Product Owners, Project Managers, and business stakeholders to verify that technology solutions meet business and technical requirements. The role would encompass the below responsibilities.

• Independently plan and execute functional, integration, system, regression, user acceptance, API, performance, and post-deployment testing as appropriate.

• Develop and maintain comprehensive test plans, test cases, test scripts, test data, expected results, traceability, and supporting QA documentation.

• Analyze business requirements, technical specifications, user stories, process flows, and acceptance criteria for clarity, completeness, and testability.

• Identify, document, prioritize, track, and communicate software defects, testing issues, dependencies, and quality risks.

• Participate in or facilitate defect triage and collaborate with technical and business resources to support timely resolution.

• Coordinate test environments, test data, schedules, dependencies, and business participation for assigned efforts.

• Communicate testing status, results, unresolved defects, risks, and release-readiness observations to project stakeholders.

• Support release validation, production implementation, and post-deployment verification activities.

• Apply and promote established QA standards, processes, procedures, documentation templates, and best practices.

• Identify functional, integration, regression, API, and other repeatable tests that are appropriate candidates for automation.

• Design, implement, execute, and maintain automated tests using approved tools, frameworks, and standards.

• Partner with Application Developers and other technology resources to troubleshoot automated test failures and improve automation reliability and coverage.

• Incorporate automated tests into application delivery and continuous integration processes where appropriate.

• Monitor defect trends and testing results to identify opportunities for process and quality improvement.

• Participate in root-cause analysis of production defects and recommend preventive or corrective actions.

• Provide guidance and knowledge transfer to less experienced QA resources when requested.

• Serve as a knowledgeable QA resource for assigned applications, projects, or business processes.

Degree Required:

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Information Technology, Business, or a related field. An equivalent combination of relevant education and experience may be considered.

Years of Experience Required:

Three or more years of progressive experience in software quality assurance, software testing, business application testing, or a related technology role.

Certification Required:

Quality assurance, software testing, Agile, or test automation certifications are preferred but not required.

• Solid knowledge of software quality assurance principles, testing methodologies, processes, and best practices.

• Proficiency developing and executing test plans, test cases, test scripts, test data, traceability documentation, and testing reports.

• Experience performing functional, integration, system, regression, user acceptance, API, performance, and post-deployment testing as appropriate.

• Experience identifying automation candidates and developing, executing, and maintaining automated tests.

• Knowledge of automated testing tools, frameworks, scripting approaches, and continuous integration practices.

• Experience with defect tracking, test management, work management, and software development collaboration tools.

• Ability to analyze business and technical requirements and translate them into effective test scenarios.

• Ability to identify quality risks, dependencies, coverage gaps, and process improvement opportunities.

• Working knowledge of relational databases and queries used for data validation and testing.

• Working knowledge of application integrations, APIs, batch processes, interfaces, and data flows.

• Strong analytical, troubleshooting, critical-thinking, organizational, and problem-solving skills.

• Ability to independently manage multiple assignments, priorities, and deadlines.

• Strong written, verbal, interpersonal, documentation, and collaboration skills.

• Ability to communicate defects, risks, status, and recommendations to technical and business audiences.

Working environment:

• • Standard office environment with the ability to sit at a workstation for extended periods. • Regular use of computers, software applications, testing tools, communication platforms, and other office technology. • May require extended or nonstandard working hours to support significant application releases, production implementations, or critical issue resolution. • May require coordination with technical teams, business stakeholders, vendors, or resources working in different locations or schedules. • Must be able to manage multiple priorities and deadlines in a collaborative, deadline-oriented environment.

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

jobs.title: Corporate Controller
jobs.description:
ABOUT WORKWHILE

WorkWhile is on a mission to help workers earn a better living and live better lives. More than 80 million Americans work hourly jobs - often with unpredictable schedules, near-minimum wages, and few benefits - leading to real financial instability. We're fixing that by matching enterprise customers across logistics, food production, retail, hospitality, events, and managed services with a quality hourly workforce, while giving workers stable income and unmatched benefits like next-day pay, free telehealth, and financial services.

WorkWhile is evolving from a high-growth temporary labor marketplace into a comprehensive workforce platform for enterprises with fintech offerings workers. The result is a multi-business-model company with a genuinely complex, interesting financial landscape.

Backed by Khosla Ventures and recognized by the Inc. 5000 for 10x growth, WorkWhile is reshaping the future of work.




THE OPPORTUNITY

This is not a "maintain the books" Controller role. This is a build-it role.

As Corporate Controller, you'll serve as the CFO's right hand in architecting a world-class accounting function from the ground up - one capable of supporting high-volume transaction processing, multi-stream revenue recognition (Marketplace + SaaS + Fintech), and banking-level treasury operations. You'll lead an ERP migration, deploy AI-driven automation, and own the technical accounting for business models that most Controllers never get to work across simultaneously.

If you're a technically deep CPA who wants to do more than close the books - someone who wants to shape financial infrastructure at a venture-backed, mission-driven company - this role is built for you.




WHAT YOU'LL OWN


1. CORE ACCOUNTING OPERATIONS

 - Full-cycle accounting ownership: General Ledger (GL), Payroll, Procure-to-Pay (P2P), Order-to-Cash (O2C), and Record-to-Report (R2R)

 - Data integrity: Partner with Data Science to ensure financial data in the ERP (NetSuite/Intacct) aligns precisely with operational data sources (BigQuery, Metabase)

 - High-volume payroll: Manage complex weekly and daily payroll runs for a nationally dispersed workforce, with distinct treatment for W2 employees (taxes, benefits, withholdings) and 1099 independent contractors

 - Month-end & year-end close: Own the close calendar, drive down close cycle times, and ensure a clean, audit-ready general ledger at all times


2. TECHNICAL ACCOUNTING & COMPLIANCE

 - Revenue Recognition (ASC 606): Author technical accounting memos and policy for multiple evolving revenue streams - including "Principal vs. Agent" gross-to-net calculations for marketplace revenue and subscription revenue recognition for the Newday SaaS product

 - Fintech & Treasury Accounting: Build accounting workflows for WorkWhile Wallet and W2 Early Pay -  including daily liquidity management for payroll funding, high-volume card transaction reconciliation (Marqeta, Stripe), and accounting for potential credit losses on worker advances

 - Equity & Stock-Based Compensation: Manage equity plan administration and ASC 718 accounting

 - Multi-jurisdiction Tax Compliance: Oversee federal, state, and local tax filings; manage payroll tax nexus across all states where W2 workers operate; address sales tax implications for SaaS products


3. AUDIT & EXTERNAL REPORTING

 - Audit leadership: Own the external audit relationship end-to-end - drive the first company financial audit, prepare PBC schedules, manage fieldwork, and deliver audited financial statements on time

 - Investor & lender reporting: Prepare accurate, well-documented financials for board reporting, debt covenant compliance, and future fundraising due diligence


4. SYSTEMS, AUTOMATION & TEAM LEADERSHIP

 - ERP migration: Lead the evaluation and implementation of a scalable ERP upgrade, including integration with billing, payroll, and payments systems

 - AI & automation: Proactively identify and deploy AI agents for reconciliation, invoice processing, and anomaly detection - reducing manual workload and improving accuracy

 - Collections & DSO optimization: Strengthen billing and collections processes, managing invoicing nuances across Enterprise and SMB client segments

 - Team development: Manage and mentor the internal accounting team and oversee the offshore BPO team, ensuring seamless collaboration across time zones




WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR


Required Qualifications

 - Active CPA license - non-negotiable

 - Big 4 accounting firm experience: Minimum 4-6 years in audit at a Big 4 firm (Deloitte, PwC, EY, or KPMG), serving public company or high-growth technology clients

 - 10+ years of progressive accounting experience, with at least 3 years as a Controller or Assistant Controller at a venture-backed technology company

 - Deep technical accounting expertise in ASC 606 revenue recognition, including multi-element arrangements and gross vs. net revenue treatment

 - Proven track record of ERP implementation - specifically migrating from QuickBooks to NetSuite, Sage Intacct, or equivalent

 - Experience managing multi-state payroll tax compliance and nexus analysis for a company with a distributed workforcePreferred / Bonus Qualifications

Preferred / Bonus Qualifications

 - Industry experience in Marketplace, Fintech (lending, ledgering, prepaid cards), or SaaS business models

 - Hands-on experience with Stripe, Marqeta, or similar payment processors from an accounting and reconciliation standpoint

 - Experience managing hybrid onshore/offshore accounting teams or BPO relationships

 - Exposure to SQL, BigQuery, or BI tools (Looker, Metabase) for financial data analysis

You'll Thrive Here If You:

 - Are the kind of person who investigates a variance until it's fully explained - not just deemed immaterial

 - Can translate complex accounting positions (like Gross vs. Net revenue) clearly for non-finance stakeholders, investors, and lenders

 - Are energized by ambiguity and want to build, not just maintain

 - Have a strong bias for action and take pride in operational excellence




COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

 - Competitive base salary + equity in a high-growth, venture-backed company

 - Hybrid work culture with office in SF

 - In-person company off-sites

 - Medical, dental & vision coverage

 - Unlimited PTO

 - 401(k)

 - WFH stipend to support your home office setup

WorkWhile has a diverse, mission-driven, and supportive culture—we look for people who want to take ownership, are energized by ambiguity, and strive to make a lasting impact. If this resonates with you, we’d love to chat!

jobs.description:
Are you ready to build America’s energy future? Form Energy is an American manufacturing and energy technology company. We’re revolutionizing energy storage with cost-effective, multi-day technology designed to keep the electric grid secure and reliable, even during extended periods of stress. By strengthening the electric system and reimagining what’s possible, we’re giving clean energy a whole new form! 



In recent years, Form Energy has earned a number of accolades, including being named by TIME as a “Best Invention”, MIT Technology Review as a “Top Climate Tech Company To Watch”, and Fast Company as “One of the Next Big Things In Tech”. We are making rapid progress on our mission of delivering energy storage for a better world, and our team is growing just as rapidly to meet demand. We have signed contracts with leading electric utilities across the United States and production of our iron-air batteries is underway at our first high-volume manufacturing facility in West Virginia. 



Working for Form Energy is more than just a job, it’s a chance to be part of something extraordinary. And now - right as we significantly scale up battery manufacturing -  might be the most exciting moment in the company’s history to join. We are assembling a team of highly talented and driven individuals across the country. Driven by our core values of humanity, excellence, and creativity, our team is determined to deliver on our mission and transform the energy landscape for the better.



Feeling energized to make a meaningful impact on the world? Then keep reading - you’ve come to the right place.




ROLE DESCRIPTION

Form Energy is seeking a Quality Controls Test Engineer who will support the development and deployment of analytical methods, leverage large electrochemical and manufacturing datasets to generate actionable improvements, and build data visualization tools that improve process understanding and product quality. Working closely with senior engineers and cross-functional teams, this individual will contribute to method implementation, root-cause investigations, reporting automation, and continuous improvement initiatives across Form Factory 1. The successful candidate will combine strong analytical thinking, technical curiosity, and a desire to grow their expertise in electrochemistry, data analytics, and factory-scale process control.  




WHAT YOU'LL DO:

 - Analyze electrochemical test data and large time-series datasets to identify trends, investigate anomalies, and support engineering decisions related to product performance and process control.

 - Develop dashboards and data visualization tools connecting electrochemical testing results with quality and manufacturing data to improve visibility into process performance and product quality.

 - Support the adaptation, documentation, and deployment of analytical and validation test methods from existing Form Energy sites for implementation at Form Factory 1.

 - Create and maintain clear work instructions, training materials, and method documentation to promote consistent test execution across technicians, engineers, and sites.

 - Assist with root-cause investigations and corrective-action activities by collecting, analyzing, and interpreting analytical and process data.

 - Collaborate with senior engineers to evaluate and improve test methods, data analysis workflows, and reporting tools.

 - Contribute to the development of automated data analysis and reporting solutions that improve efficiency and accelerate engineering insights.




WHAT YOU'LL BRING:

 - 1 to 3 years of experience supporting engineering, quality, or laboratory operations.

 - Experience analyzing experimental, manufacturing, or time-series datasets to identify trends and draw technical conclusions.

jobs.description:
Starling Oncology (NASDAQ: STLN) is advancing oncology by delivering highly specialized, value-based cancer care in the community setting. Formerly known as The Oncology Institute, Starling Oncology offers cutting-edge, evidence-based cancer care to a population of approximately 2.1 million patients, including clinical trials, transfusions, and other care delivery models traditionally associated with the most advanced care delivery organizations. With more than 400 employed and network clinicians and over 100 clinics and network locations of care across five states and growing, Starling Oncology is changing oncology for the better. For more information, visit www.starlingoncology.com.

SAME DAY INTERVIEWS: Meet our AI Recruiting Assistant and complete a same-day interview—quick, easy, and on your schedule. Within minutes of applying, you’ll receive a text message to schedule your interview.

Explore our Medical Assistant careers across the San Fernando Valley.

Mission Hills, Northridge, Burbank, Glendale, Valencia, Van Nuys, and Palmdale

At Starling Oncology, our Medical Assistants play a vital role in transforming the patient experience. You’ll be part of a compassionate care team that helps patients navigate one of the most important journeys of their lives—with dignity, empathy, and hope.

JOB PURPOSE AND SUMMARY:

The Medical Assistant is adaptable, dependable, and eager to advance their clinical careers. As an essential member of the patient care team, the Medical Assistant will provide both administrative and clinical support to ensure the smooth operation of the clinic. The MA should deliver high-quality, compassionate patient care, enhancing clinic efficiency, and contributing to an outstanding patient experience. This position also offers the opportunity to be cross trained in patient registration and medical records support, as needed.

Teammates must be willing and able to work assigned shifts at multiple clinic locations and drive between clinics as needed to support patient care and business operations. Mileage will be reimbursed.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Live and exemplify Starling Oncology core values, providing outstanding customer service and promoting a positive experience for patients and staff members.

• Participate in company initiatives and team activities

• Responsible for documentation in electronic medical record (EMR) system(s)

• Requesting external medical records and preparing patient charts prior to patient appointments

• Performing and documenting patient vital signs

• Completing review of systems and intake documentation

• Preparing patients for physician care

• Administering basic first aid

• Performing venipunctures and non-intravenous injections

• Performing basic laboratory procedures

• Observing and reporting patients’ signs or symptoms

• Able to serve as a chaperone in patient examinations as needed

• Assisting with patient examinations, procedures, or treatments

• Administering certain medications as directed by the physician

• Other duties as assigned

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES:

• Proficiency in electronic medical record (EMR) systems.

• Excellent interpersonal and communication skills.

• Strong organizational and multitasking abilities.

• Detail-oriented with a high level of accuracy.

• Compassionate and patient-focused attitude.

• Ability to work effectively in a team environment.

• Proficiency in completing blood draws and processing labs

EXPERIENCE, EDUCATION AND/OR TRAINING:

• High school graduate or GED

• Completion of a Medical Assistant Diploma program from an accredited educational institute. Medical Assistant Certificate preferred, not required.

• 2 years of experience working as a Medical Assistant or related role in an outpatient clinic/medical office setting is preferred.

• BLS and CPR certification preferred.

• Bilingual in Spanish and English preferred.

PHYSICAL WORKING REQUIREMENTS:

This position involves prolonged periods of standing and walking, performance of precise tasks like drawing blood and administering medications, and occasionally, lifting of up to 50 pounds. Clear vision and acute hearing are essential for reading charts and monitoring patients. Strong communication skills and attention to detail are critical, especially under stress. Frequent bending, stooping, reaching, and repetitive tasks are also required, along with sensitivity to patient needs and environmental changes.

The physical demands described above are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

AI Recruiter Assistant:

To help make our interview process more efficient and respectful of your time, we use interview technology that records your responses and may use automated tools to support the review of job-related skills. These tools do not make final hiring decisions. All hiring decisions are made by our Talent Acquisition and hiring teams. If you need an accommodation or would prefer to complete this step with a recruiter instead, please contact us at careers@theoncologyinstitute.com

Pay Transparency for hourly teammates

jobs.title: Director, Commercial Project Management
jobs.description:
Revolution Medicines is a global, commercial-state oncology company dedicated to discovering, developing and delivering innovative medicines for patients with RAS-addicted cancers. Leveraging its differentiated RAS(ON) tri-complex inhibitor platform, the company is advancing a broad, integrated portfolio of oral RAS(ON) inhibitors designed to directly target the active, cancer-driving state of RAS. Founded on rigorous scientific inquiry and a willingness to challenge long-held assumptions, Revolution Medicines is committed to changing the trajectory of disease for patients with RAS-addicted cancers worldwide.

Our people are united by a shared way of working: follow the science, challenge assumptions, act with urgency and hold ourselves to a high standard of rigor—all in service of patients.

The Opportunity:

This is a unique opportunity to play a critical role in advancing Revolution Medicines' commercialization strategy during a period of significant growth. We are seeking an experienced and highly collaborative Director, Commercial Project Management to lead in one of the company's key Disease Areas by driving cross-functional planning, alignment, and execution across global commercialization priorities.

This role sits within the Commercialization Effectiveness & Operations (CE&O) function and reports to the Executive Director, Global Commercialization Effectiveness.

In partnership with Global Commercial, Medical, Market Access, and cross-functional leaders, you will serve as the primary project management partner to the Global Commercialization Team, the Global Commercial Team and other cross-functional teams in your assigned Disease Area.

Operating in a build-while-scaling environment, you will bring clarity, structure, and execution discipline to complex cross-functional initiatives while helping strengthen commercialization ways of working. As the capability matures, this role may expand to include people leadership responsibilities.

What You’ll Do

• Lead project management support for Global Commercialization Teams and Global Commercial Teams within an assigned Disease Area, driving alignment, accountability, and execution across strategic priorities.

• Drive execution of global commercial and commercialization initiatives, ensuring milestones, risks, dependencies, and key decisions are effectively managed.

• Coordinate and integrate inputs across Commercial, Medical, Market Access, Regulatory, Supply, Legal, Finance, and regional stakeholders into cohesive commercialization plans.

• Facilitate planning, governance, and decision-making processes, ensuring effective follow-through on actions and commitments.

• Identify and proactively manage risks, dependencies, and execution challenges, escalating issues as appropriate.

• Develop and maintain project plans, dashboards, timelines, and reporting tools that provide visibility into progress and priorities.

• to ensure alignment between execution needs, planning processes, and organizational priorities.

• Support launch readiness and other key commercialization initiatives within the Disease Area.

• Partner closely with Project Management colleagues across the organization to ensure alignment between development, life cycle, medical, market access and commercial plans and deliverables.

• Contribute to the development of Commercial Project Management capabilities, including tools, templates, best practices, and ways of working.

Required Skills, Experience and Education:

• Bachelor’s degree, with 10+ years of relevant experience in biotech/pharma/healthcare.

• Significant experience leading complex, cross‑functional projects or commercialization initiatives.

• Experience supporting global commercial organizations, including launch readiness, lifecycle management, or major commercialization initiatives.

• Experience working across global and regional operating models.

• Strong project management skills, including planning, dependency management, risk management, stakeholder leadership, and executive communication.

• Proven ability to influence without authority and drive alignment across diverse stakeholder groups.

• Experience partnering with senior commercial, medical affairs, market access, and cross-functional leaders.

• Track record of thriving in fast-paced, evolving environments with a proactive, solutions-oriented mindset.

• Excellent communication, facilitation, and interpersonal skills, with the ability to translate complexity into clarity for diverse audiences.

• Strong judgment, organizational skills, and attention to detail.

Preferred Skills:

• Advanced degree (MBA/MS/PhD).

• Oncology / specialty pharma commercialization experience.

• Formal Project Management training or certification (e.g., PMP).

• Experience supporting multiple concurrent programs or portfolios.

• Early people leadership experience or readiness to step into people leadership as the capability scales.

jobs.title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer - AI Foundation
jobs.description:
XPENG is a leading smart technology company at the forefront of innovation, integrating advanced AI and autonomous driving technologies into its vehicles, including electric vehicles (EVs), electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) aircraft, and robotics. With a strong focus on intelligent mobility, XPENG is dedicated to reshaping the future of transportation through cutting-edge R&D in AI, machine learning, and smart connectivity.

We are looking for a full-time Machine Learning Engineer - AI Foundation, with deep knowledge and strong enthusiasm towards establishing a state-of-art ML infrastructure for training very large foundation model and accelerating model training/inference.

Our mission is to solve the autonomous driving problem. You will work with a team of talented software engineers, machine learning engineers and research scientists to push the boundary of state-of-art machine learning models which will enable the next-generation E2E solution of autonomous driving.

Job Responsibilities:

• Design and implement training data pipeline that streams data from hundreds of petabytes of labeled and unlabeled data from a fleet of over a million vehicles.

• Implement training framework for all physical AI foundation models in XPeng, including VLA 2.0, XWorld, Robotics.

• Accelerate training with state of the art parallelisms, e.g., FSDP, Expert Parallel, Context Parallel, and data types.

• Accelerate model inference on the cloud for closed-loop simulation, reinforcement learning, and enterprise LLM/VLM applications.

Minimum Skill Requirements:

• Master's Degree in CS/CE/EE, or equivalent, in industry experience.

• Deep knowledge of PyTorch.

• Knowledge of model inference framework (e.g. vLLM, SGLang)

• In-depth knowledge of transformer architecture and ways to accelerate the training and inference of transformer models.

• Experience of performing large scale distributed training of models.

• A track record of profiling model and doing detective work to improve model training and inference speed.

Preferred Skill Requirements:

• Previous experience in the autonomous driving industry.

• Experience with CUDA language for writing custom ops.

• Experience with edge computing systems.

• Knowledge of disributed computing frameworks, such as Ray.

• A track record of efficiently solving complex problems collaboratively on larger teams

What do we provide:

• A fun, supportive and engaging environment.

• Infrastructures and computational resources to support your work.

• Opportunity to work on cutting edge technologies with the top talents in the field.

• Opportunity to make a significant impact on the transportation revolution by the means of advancing autonomous driving.

• Competitive compensation package.

• Snacks, lunches, dinners, and fun activities.

The base salary range for this full-time position is $174,720-$295,680, in addition to bonus, equity and benefits. Our salary ranges are determined by role, level, and location. jobs.title: Materials & Processes Engineer, Metallics
jobs.description:
Vast is developing next-generation space stations and space infrastructure using an incremental, hardware-rich, and low-cost approach. Vast is rapidly developing its multi-module Haven Station to ensure a continuous human presence in space for America and its allies, enabling advanced microgravity research and manufacturing, and unlocking a new space economy for government, corporate, and private customers. Haven Demo’s 2025 success made Vast the only operational commercial space station company to fly and operate its own spacecraft. Next, Haven-1 is expected to become the world’s first commercial space station when it launches in 2027, followed by additional Haven modules. Additionally, the company recently announced Vast Satellite, a high-power satellite product line leveraging its space station components and the heritage of Haven Demo.

Headquartered in Long Beach, California, and with more than 1,000 employees and over a billion dollars in private capital, Vast has built the facilities required to manufacture and operate America’s next space station. The company plans to develop future habitats and systems for the Moon and Mars, dedicated space stations for government partners, and other crewed systems that will unlock the expanding long-term space economy.

Vast is looking for a Materials & Processes Engineer – Metallics, reporting to the Materials & Processes Lead, to support the development of the systems that will be required for the design and build of human-rated space stations.

This will be a full-time, exempt position located in our Long Beach location.

Responsibilities:

• Provide Materials & Processes engineering expertise for metallic materials used across spacecraft structures, mechanisms, pressure systems, propulsion systems, and other flight hardware

• Support material selection and qualification for metals including aluminum, stainless steels, titanium, nickel-based alloys, copper alloys, and other aerospace materials

• Develop, review, and maintain material and process specifications, engineering standards, and acceptance criteria.

• Provide technical guidance for manufacturing processes including machining, forging, casting, heat treatment, welding, brazing, additive manufacturing, and surface treatments

• Evaluate material properties and manufacturing processes against structural, thermal, environmental, fatigue, fracture, corrosion, and life requirements

• Develop and execute material and process qualification test plans, including characterization of mechanical and physical properties. Develop and maintain material allowables and process controls

• Perform and support failure analysis and root cause investigations involving metallic flight hardware and manufacturing processes. Support nonconformance investigations, MRB activities, corrective actions, and disposition

• Work closely with Supplier Quality Engineering and Supply Chain to evaluate supplier capabilities, resolve technical issues, and develop critical suppliers

• Serve as highest technical authority on selected processes, alloy classes, or advanced testing techniques

• Mentor and raise the technical level of more junior M&P engineers across the team

• Represent M&P organization in program-level reviews and lead cross-functional initiatives

Minimum Qualifications:

• Bachelor’s degree in Materials Science, Materials Engineering, Metallurgical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related technical field

• Lvl. I M&P Engineer: 0 years of experience in materials engineering, metallurgy, or manufacturing engineering

• Lvl. II M&P Engineer: 2+ years of experience in materials engineering, metallurgy, or manufacturing engineering

• Senior M&P Engineer: 5+ years of the above, with demonstrated technical leadership across a subsystem, program, or team

Preferred Skills & Experience:

• Master’s degree or PhD in Materials Science, Materials Engineering, Metallurgical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field

• 5+ years of experience supporting metallic materials and processes for spacecraft, launch vehicles, aircraft, pressure vessels, propulsion systems, or other high-reliability hardware

• Deep expertise in one or more areas including welding and joining, heat treatment, fatigue and fracture mechanics

• Fundamental understanding of metallic materials including aluminum, steel, titanium, nickel-based alloys, or other aerospace metals

• Experience with metallic manufacturing processes such as casting, forging, machining, heat treatment, welding, brazing, additive manufacturing, or surface treatments

• Experience interpreting material specifications, engineering drawings, test data, and technical requirements

• Experience supporting material characterization, process qualification, failure analysis, or root cause investigations

• Strong communication skills and demonstrated ability to work cross-functionally with Design, Manufacturing, Quality, and Supply Chain teams

• Demonstrated ability to solve complex technical problems using a first-principles approach

• Extensive, hands-on experience with metallography, microscopy (optical, SEM, EDS), mechanical testing (hardness, tensile, fatigue), fracture analysis or other material characterization methods

• Experience developing or qualifying special processes and working with NADCAP or similarly controlled aerospace processes

• Familiarity with aerospace material and testing standards such as NASA, AMS, ASTM, AWS, MIL, or equivalent industry standards

• Knowledge of material allowables, fatigue and fracture behavior, corrosion prevention, and environmental compatibility

• Experience performing hands-on failure analysis and supporting RCCA investigations on flight or production hardware

• Experience working in a fast-paced, hardware-first aerospace environment

• Ability to work autonomously and take extreme ownership of assigned technical areas

Additional Requirements:

• Ability to travel up to 30% of the time

• Willingness to work overtime or weekends to support critical mission milestones

• Ability to lift up to 25 lbs. Unassisted

Pay Range:

• Materials and Processes Engineer I: $86,100 - $122,220

• Materials and Processes Engineer II: $112,340 - $159,468

• Senior Materials and Processes Engineer: $137,760 - $195,552

Pay Range: California

$86,100—$195,552 USD

Full-time employees also receive company equity, as well as access to a full suite of compelling benefits and perks, including: medical, dental, and vision coverage for employees and dependents, generous paid time off; up to 20+ days of vacation for exempt staff and up to 10+ days of vacation for non-exempt staff with the ability to cash-out unused vacation annually, paid parental leave, short and long-term disability insurance, life insurance, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, ClassPass credits, personalized mental healthcare through Spring Health, and other discounts and perks. jobs.description:
About the Team

Design Program Managers make DoorDash's Design Studio run better. As owner of the Logistics pillar within Design Operations, you're accountable for one of our most important operating outcomes: maximizing the bandwidth of the team.

About the Role

You'll find where ICs and managers lose time, fragmented workflows, manual processes, meeting overload, unclear rhythms, and you'll define and build the tools and systems that fix it. That might mean shipping a new internal tool, automating a recurring workflow, redesigning how scheduling or reviews work, or establishing a better operating cadence. You own the full loop: diagnose the problem, design the system, build the tool, measure whether it worked.

You're excited about this opportunity because you will…

• Own the Logistics outcome, maximize the bandwidth of the team. ICs and managers have more usable time. Meeting load decreases. The team can focus on high-value work.

• Identify the biggest sources of operational drag across the Studio and turn them into a prioritized roadmap of tools and process fixes.

• Define and build the tools, automations, and workflows that reduce manual coordination, including for scheduling, budgets, vendor management, and event logistics.

• Redesign how the Studio operates: reviews, planning cadences, rhythms for both ICs and managers, information flows, whatever determines how fast teams can move.

• Measure whether your systems work, usable time for ICs and managers, meeting load, adoption, hours of manual work eliminated, and iterate.

• Turn recurring requests into scalable solutions. The second time a problem shows up, build the thing that stops a third.

• Own scheduling, budget, vendor, and logistics programs as a builder, not a permanent executor, your job is to make them need less manual effort every quarter.

• Partner with (and, as scope grows, help develop) other DPMs on the Logistics pod.

We're excited about you because you have…

• 5+ years in operations, program management, or business operations, building systems and tools that made a complex org run better. Design/product/creative org experience is a plus; EA or Chief of Staff backgrounds are welcome if you've built beyond pure execution.

• A builder mindset: you've created tools, workflows, or automations that replaced manual work — not just performed manual work well.

• Product-manager instincts applied to operations: find the real pain point, diagnose root cause, prototype, ship, measure, iterate.

• The ability to own an outcome independently at L4/L5 scope — you don't need the problem pre-scoped for you.

• Comfort with AI and no-code tooling (Claude, Cursor, Figma, or similar) to prototype and ship internal tools without needing an engineer.

• Strong written/verbal communication and the judgment to handle sensitive leadership and operational info with discretion.

What success looks like

Maximize the bandwidth of the team. ICs and managers have more usable time. Meeting load decreases. Team can focus on high-value work. Manual workflows become automated. Recurring problems become systems that scale. Your job is to create capacity — not just manage it.

jobs.title: Senior High-Speed Photonic Design Engineer
jobs.description:
About the Team

Born at X, Google's Moonshot Factory, Taara is on a mission to connect billions of people who lack abundant and affordable internet by pioneering high-throughput, long-range free-space optical communication (FSOC). Our links use eye-safe lasers propagating between two terminals to transmit high-speed data wirelessly. Lead the charge in bringing our groundbreaking wireless optical communication to the world. Join us to light the way toward bridging the digital divide and illuminating the future.

About the Role

Taara is seeking a Senior High-Speed Photonic Design Engineer to work on next-generation photonic and electronic integrated modules as part of the R&D team developing cutting-edge wireless optical communication systems based on integrated optical phased arrays.

The successful candidate will own photonic transmitter and receiver architecture, high-speed photonic modulator and detector design, and RF/microwave transmission line design within the very-large-scale photonic integrated circuits (PICs) developed at Taara. The role requires deep expertise in 35-70 GHz RF and photonic design — including demonstrated design and layout ownership on commercial foundry tapeouts — as well as extensive experience with the intricacies of modulation formats and communication link budgets.

We are looking for a highly motivated individual who thrives in ambiguity, enjoys working in a small, dynamic team environment, and has a passion for solving challenging problems that lead to high-impact technological advances.

How you will make 10x impact:

 - Own and deliver record-breaking high-speed photonic integrated circuit designs.

 - Contribute to system-level optimization and product strategy.

 - Demonstrate a strong motivation to make the world a better place through technology and a desire to be part of the team making this happen.

What you should have:

 - Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering, Applied Physics, Materials Science, or a related field.

 - Five (5) or more years of relevant industry experience with demonstrated achievements in photonic circuit designs.

 - Extensive expertise in high-speed photonic modulator and detector design.

 - Extensive expertise in RF/microwave design.

 - Expertise in the intricacies of optical modulation formats and photonic link modeling.

 - Experience with RF/microwave design software (HFSS, ADS or equivalent).

 - Experience with photonic device simulation software (Lumerical or equivalent).

 - Experience with optical link simulation software (VPIphotonics, Lumerical Interconnect, or equivalent).

 - Hands-on experience with multiple tapeouts at commercial foundries.

It would be great if you also had these:

 - Experience in photonic spectral filter design.

 - Experience with Python, Git, and gdsfactory.

 - Experience with Design Rule Checks (DRC) and Layout Versus Schematic (LVS).

 - Experience with commercial layout verification software (Calibre or equivalent).

 - Excellent communication and presentation skills, with the ability to work effectively with senior external partners.

 - Hands-on experience in advancing a product from the prototype phase to the final production stage.

Job Location & Compensation: 

 - Hybrid/Onsite in Sunnyvale, CA is preferred. Remote can be considered as well.

 - Relocation can be provided.

jobs.title: Optics Intern
jobs.description:
ABOUT OVERVIEW ENERGY

Overview Energy is a mission-driven team committed to building a new layer of energy infrastructure: satellites in geosynchronous orbit that redirect solar energy to terrestrial solar projects via passively safe near-infrared  light. We're in the earliest phase, where the ground beacon our satellites will point to is aligned, characterized, and field-corrected end-to-end by a small, dedicated team. Headquartered in the Northern Virginia / Washington, DC area and backed by world-class investors, we are advancing the next generation of clean energy technology.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We're looking for an Optics Intern to help with the design and building of our ground beacon from the optical bench to a field test site. The beacon is the pointing reference the satellite system will depend on. If it isn't aligned and characterized correctly, nothing downstream works.



You'll work hands-on with the emitter and the observational telescope: aligning the laser, characterizing its output, and co-aligning the beacon with the telescope. Then you'll own a problem we haven't solved yet. Once the system is transported to the test site, alignment may shift. You'll design the procedure that brings it back.



This internship supports our program under a Department of War (DoW) energy investment program. You'll work alongside our optics and hardware engineers, and your alignment data will feed directly into hardware decisions we make.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Align the beacon laser within its emitter and verify pointing outside the emitter aperture

 - Characterize laser output - power, beam profile, divergence, and pointing stability - and document the results

 - Co-align the beacon laser with the observational telescope and verify boresight

 - Design a repeatable field alignment procedure that corrects misalignment introduced during transport and installation at the DoW site

 - Write that procedure so a non-optics operator can execute it, then validate it hands-on before delivery

 - Maintain clean alignment and characterization records, and feed findings back to the engineering team
   
   


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR FROM YOU

 - Currently enrolled in a bachelor's or master's program in optics, optical engineering, physics, or a closely related field

 - Coursework or lab experience with optical alignment: mounts, mirrors, lenses, and beam paths

 - Willingness to complete laser safety training and follow protocol without exception

 - Careful documentation habits - alignment work is only useful if it's repeatable by someone else

 - Able to commit approximately 10 hours per week from September 2026 through March 2027, on-site in Northern Virginia
   
   


WE HAVE A STRONG PREFERENCE FOR

 - Hands-on use of beam profilers, power meters, autocollimators, or shear plates

 - Telescope operation or astronomical instrumentation experience

 - Zemax OpticStudio, Quadoa, Code V, or comparable optical design and analysis software

 - Experience writing test or alignment procedures that other people have actually followed

 - Demonstrated interest in defense, space, or energy applications
   
   


INTERNSHIP DETAILS

This is a paid, part-time internship running September 2026 through March 2027 at approximately 10 hours per week, based on-site at our Northern Virginia headquarters. Hourly rate: $30-$40.

You'll be mentored directly by the engineers running the program, and your work is a funded DoW deliverable, not a side project. Interns are not eligible for the full-time benefits package.




ITAR REQUIREMENTS

This position is subject to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR). Candidates must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident, protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State.




EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER

Overview Energy is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are based on merit, competence, and qualifications, without regard to race, color, religion, gender, national origin, ethnicity, veteran status, disability, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, or any other legally protected status.



If you require a reasonable accommodation during the application process, please contact us at talent@overviewenergy.com.



Research shows that women and individuals from underrepresented groups often only apply for roles where they meet every listed qualification. If you believe you can succeed in this role, we encourage you to apply - even if you don't check every box.

jobs.description:
Heartflow is a medical technology company advancing the diagnosis and management of coronary artery disease, the #1 cause of death worldwide, using cutting-edge technology. The flagship product—an AI-driven, non-invasive cardiac test supported by the ACC/AHA Chest Pain Guidelines called the Heartflow FFRCT Analysis—provides a color-coded, 3D model of a patient’s coronary arteries indicating the impact blockages have on blood flow to the heart. Heartflow is the first AI-driven non-invasive integrated heart care solution across the CCTA pathway that helps clinicians identify stenoses in the coronary arteries (RoadMap™Analysis), assess coronary blood flow (FFRCT Analysis), and characterize and quantify coronary atherosclerosis (Plaque Analysis). Our pipeline of products is growing and so is our team; join us in helping to revolutionize precision heartcare.

Heartflow is a publicly traded company (HTFL) that has received international recognition for exceptional strides in healthcare innovation, is supported by medical societies around the world, cleared for use in the US, UK, Europe, Japan and Canada, and has been used for more than 750,000 patients worldwide.

The Clinical Field Specialist, CT is responsible for optimizing customers’ imaging programs and workflows by assisting with the proper use of Heartflow products (e.g. CT quality, systems, processes). This includes traveling to customer sites to deliver training and build relationships with Technologists, Radiologists, Cardiologists, and other customer representatives.

The Clinical Field Specialist, CT will have substantial experience in clinical and cardiac CT, will be able to express a deep understanding of Heartflow’s technology and products, and will be passionate about delivering the highest level of customer support.

• Identify areas of improvement and make recommendations to enhance quality acceptance rates during customer onboarding.

• Conduct virtual and/or live training of technologists using various delivery methods, including product demonstrations, one-on-one, and group training sessions, to transfer knowledge on the use of Heartflow products in assigned geography.

• Establish credibility and sustain strong working relationships with key stakeholders.

• Ensure proper records (e.g. customer contacts, CT volume, engagement logs, training records, etc.) and documentation are input and maintained in Heartflow systems.

• Capture customer feedback and participate in clinical discussions with customers and colleagues regarding Heartflow analysis on multiple products.

• Maintain knowledge of the latest CT and Workstation technology innovations, training delivery methodologies, and training materials for effective training.

• Build and execute on plans to proactively optimize customer performance and identify opportunities for improvement.

jobs.title: Staff/Senior Staff Supply Chain Manager
jobs.description:
WHAT TO EXPECT 

Heron Power is a startup company building cutting-edge power electronics for the 21st-century grid. We aim to debottleneck the growth of electricity generation and consumption with scalable, innovative, and less costly hardware solutions, accelerating the electrification of everything.

Our first goal is to build better converters (inverters & rectifiers) to connect large-scale renewables, storage, and loads to the grid. Heron Power’s leadership team is made up of seasoned veterans who have designed and shipped gigawatts of power conversion products over the past decade.

We understand that no one individual knows everything. We will all learn a lot together and from each other. We strive to build a collaborative, enriching environment conducive to personal, technical, and career growth. You can expect to work in a dynamic and collaborative environment, driven by first principles engineering, solving difficult problems.




JOB OVERVIEW

As a Staff/Senior Staff Supply Chain Manager, you’ll lead strategic sourcing for the critical components and assemblies that power Heron Link.  In this pivotal role, you’ll partner closely with the Head of Supply Chain and leaders across Finance, Design Engineering, NPI and Manufacturing to build a resilient supply base. You will ensure the commercial success of Heron’s supply chain, overseeing product cost and supplier performance. 




HOW YOU WILL CONTRIBUTE

 - Define and own the category strategies for key components and assemblies.

 - Achieve or exceed cost targets through data-driven should-cost modeling, market and commodity analysis, and disciplined negotiations.

 - Lead RFx processes and negotiate commercial agreements, including piece pricing, tooling/NRE, and key contractual terms.

 - Manage business risk through scenario assessment of capacity, geopolitics, logistics, and supplier technology / commercial roadmaps. Actively partner with the engineering team to identify/mitigate supply and demand challenges

 - Develop and execute the logistics and warehousing strategy associated with and in partnership with factory operations

 - Escalate key supply, cost, and/or quality issues with partner teams and collaboratively develop corrective action plans 




WHAT YOU WILL BRING

We’re open to early to mid-career candidates with or without leadership experience. Scope and responsibilities will scale with the right candidate.




MUST HAVE REQUIREMENTS 

 - 8+ years of experience in sourcing or procurement for high volume manufacturing

 - Degree in Supply Chain, Engineering, Business Administration, or equivalent experience

 - Deep category knowledge across mechanical, electrical (PCB/PCBA), and/or electro-mechanical components and assemblies

 - Strong negotiation and contract management skills

 - Experience leading cross-functional work-streams with engineering, operations, finance, legal and NPI teams to drive alignment and execute sourcing strategies

NICE TO HAVES

jobs.title: Total Rewards Manager
jobs.description:
Nestled in San Francisco's Excelsior neighborhood on a nine-acre campus, the San Francisco Campus for Jewish Living (SFCJL) is the leading senior services organization in Northern California. Our continuum of care includes: the Frank Residences assisted living and memory care; the Jewish Home and Rehabilitation Center, offering long-term skilled nursing, short-term rehabilitation, an acute geriatric psychiatric unit for adults over the age of 65; and our Foundation.

Founded in 1871 and formerly known as the Jewish Home, our legacy grounds us as our vision propels us forward. Today, we've evolved to support more than 2,500 older adults each year through innovative, comprehensive programs rooted in the Jewish values of compassion, community, and excellence. We are equally proud of our inclusive culture, where 950 team members of diverse faiths and backgrounds work together in shared purpose.

WHY WORK WITH US

• Mission-driven nonprofit organization

• Competitive compensation and comprehensive benefits

• Meaningful work that positively impacts the lives of older adults every day

• Inclusive community, welcoming to all (you do not need to be Jewish to live or work here)

• Supportive, team-oriented environment

• Opportunities for professional growth and development

• Collaborative leadership focused on enhancing the employee experience

Position Summary

The Total Rewards Manager is responsible for the hands-on day-to-day administration, delivery, and continuous improvement of compensation, benefits, and recognition programs that attract, retain, and engage employees across Skilled Nursing and Assisted Living operations. This is a highly hands-on, operational role that directly manages day-to-day Total Rewards activities, resolves employee and manager issues, maintains data and systems, and ensures programs are administered accurately, timely, and in compliance with applicable laws, regulations, and organizational policies.

The Total Rewards Manager partners closely with HR, Finance, Talent Acquisition, Payroll, and senior leaders to ensure compensation and benefits programs are competitive, cost-effective, compliant, and aligned with organizational strategy, with a strong emphasis on compensation administration, benefits operations, data accuracy, analytics, and employee support.

Key Responsibilities

Compensation

• Serve as the primary subject matter expert and day-to-day owner of compensation operations, providing hands-on support to HR Partners, Talent Acquisition, managers, and senior leaders.

• Review and process compensation changes, including promotions, transfers, market adjustments, equity adjustments, new hire offers, internal moves, and other salary actions.

• Analyze compensation data, internal equity, market trends, and external benchmarks to support compensation decisions and recommendations.

• Conduct job evaluations, salary reviews, market benchmarking, and internal equity analysis.

• Manage participation in compensation surveys and maintain accurate market pricing data.

• Lead and administer the annual compensation planning and review cycle in ADP, including system configuration, testing, manager support, reporting, and troubleshooting.

• Maintain salary structures, pay ranges, job classifications, compensation frameworks, policies, and related documentation.

• Partner with Talent Acquisition and HR to review offers and ensure proposed compensation is consistent with internal equity, market data, and established guidelines.

• Monitor compensation data for accuracy and identify and resolve discrepancies or inconsistencies.

• Prepare compensation reports, analyses, and recommendations for HR and leadership.

• Support union and non-union compensation administration, including interpretation and application of contractual pay provisions where applicable.

Benefits

• Own the day-to-day administration and operational management of employee benefit programs, serving as a hands-on resource for employees, managers, HR, and leadership.

• Process and oversee benefit eligibility, enrollment, qualifying life events, status changes, and benefit-related employee transactions.

• Troubleshoot and resolve complex benefits issues, working directly with employees, vendors, carriers, Payroll, and HR to ensure timely resolution.

• Manage annual benefits renewals, open enrollment, plan changes, system configuration, testing, communications, and implementation.

• Monitor benefit deductions and eligibility data between HRIS, payroll, benefits systems, and external vendors to identify and correct discrepancies.

• Serve as the primary point of contact for benefit vendors and carriers, managing day-to-day vendor relationships and issue resolution.

• Conduct benefits benchmarking, utilization analysis, cost analysis, and plan reviews to identify opportunities for improvement.

• Ensure benefits programs and processes comply with applicable federal, state, and local requirements.

• Maintain accurate benefits documentation, policies, procedures, employee communications, and process guides.

• Support audits, reconciliations, required filings, and compliance activities related to benefit programs.

• Partner with Finance and Payroll on benefit costs, deductions, invoices, reconciliations, and financial reporting.

• Provide hands-on employee education and support regarding medical, dental, vision, retirement, HSA/FSA, commuter, leave, and other benefit programs.

Total Rewards Operations & Analytics

• Manage the day-to-day operation of the Total Rewards function, ensuring employee requests, system transactions, vendor issues, and administrative tasks are completed accurately and within established timelines.

• Maintain the integrity and accuracy of Total Rewards data within ADP and other applicable HR systems.

• Develop and maintain recurring reports, dashboards, audits, and metrics related to compensation and benefits.

• Identify process gaps and implement improvements that increase efficiency, accuracy, compliance, and employee experience.

• Create and maintain Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), process documentation, and internal controls for Total Rewards activities.

• Partner with HRIS/HR Operations to test system changes, troubleshoot issues, and improve automated workflows.

• Provide responsive day-to-day consultation and problem-solving to employees, managers, HR leadership, Finance, Payroll, and other internal stakeholders.

• Maintain confidentiality and exercise sound judgment when handling sensitive compensation and employee benefits information.

Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Business, or a related field required; advanced degree preferred.

• 6–8+ years of experience in compensation and benefits, including at least 4 years in a leadership role.

• Deep knowledge of total rewards best practices, compensation design, compliance, and market trends.

• Advanced Excel skills (pivot tables, formulas, lookups; macros a plus).

• Experience with HRIS platforms; ADP Workforce Now preferred.

• Strong analytical, problem-solving, and stakeholder communication skills.

Why Join Us
At San Francisco Campus for Jewish Living, you’ll shape programs that support over 900 employees and directly impact the quality of care for our residents. Be part of a mission-driven team that values innovation, compassion, and excellence.

Salary: $130,000 – $160,000 | Full-time | Primarily on-site four days a week

OUR INVESTMENT IN YOU

Comprehensive benefits, including Medical, Dental, and Vision coverage; a 403(b) Retirement Plan; Paid Time Off (PTO); Tuition Reimbursement; Commuter Benefits; and Weekday Shuttle Service to and from Glen Park BART Station.

The San Francisco Campus for Jewish Living is committed to fostering a diverse, equitable, and inclusive workplace. We provide equal employment opportunities to all qualified individuals without regard to race, color, religion, gender, age, national origin, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity, veteran status, genetic information, disability, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

jobs.title: Public Affairs & Policy Intern
jobs.description:
ABOUT OVERVIEW ENERGY

Overview Energy is a mission-driven team committed to building a new layer of energy infrastructure: satellites in geosynchronous orbit that redirect solar energy to terrestrial solar projects via passively safe near-infrared light. We're in the earliest phase, where the operating concept and every warfighter conversation helps to define how this technology is used. Headquartered in the Northern Virginia / Washington, DC area and backed by world-class investors, we are advancing the next generation of clean energy technology.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We're looking for a Public Affairs & Policy Intern to answer a question nobody has answered yet: what rules govern space solar energy operations, and how does a warfighter actually operate the system?

In support of a Department of War (DoW) energy investment program, you'll research the policy landscape for space and beacon operations and turn it into concrete CONOPS language. You'll research DoW sites for present and future testing. And you'll build the material that makes this technology legible to the people who would use it to feed our broader space solar energy operational guide.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Research U.S. policy and regulation governing space operations and ground-based beacon operations, and translate it into CONOPS language the engineering team can design against

 - Identify and profile DoW sites for present and future testing, including access, airspace, and environmental considerations

 - Support warfighter engagement: prepare briefing material, capture feedback in the room, and route it back into CONOPS and design

 - Draft an operator manual written for the warfighter, not the engineer

 - Create warfighter and DoW engagement materials that make an unfamiliar technology easy to understand quickly

 - Track DoW expectations against what we're producing, and flag gaps early
   
   


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR FROM YOU

 - Currently enrolled in a bachelor's or master's program in public policy, government, international affairs, communications, or a closely related field

 - Demonstrated interest in defense, space, or energy policy - coursework, clubs, writing, or prior internships all count

 - Clear, fast writing for non-expert audiences: you can turn a dense directive into a paragraph an operator will actually read

 - Comfortable with primary source research - statute, DoW directives, and federal regulatory frameworks 

 - Able to commit 3-5 hours per week from September 2026 through March 2027 with potential extended work time based on the needs of the program; schedule is flexible
   
   


WE HAVE A STRONG PREFERENCE FOR

 - ROTC participation, prior military service, or coursework in military operations and doctrine

 - Internship or fellowship experience on Capitol Hill, in the Executive Branch, or with DoW

 - Experience producing briefing-grade materials: one-pagers, decks, manuals, or visual explainers

 - Familiarity with laser safety, space systems, and/or airspace coordination

 - Interest in a longer-term career in the Executive Branch or the military
   
   


INTERNSHIP DETAILS

jobs.title: Federal Account Executive
jobs.description:
What we’re building

The marine industry supports recreation, global commerce, and national defense. And yet it runs on technology that hasn't meaningfully changed in fifty years. Until now.

Arc is on a mission to electrify the marine industry. We're rethinking powertrains, software, and vessel designs from first principles. And we're already executing. We started with consumers to develop and harden our core technology. We’re now scaling production of our flagship model with new models and sectors on the horizon. Now we’re extending our platform to commercial applications, starting with tugs, ferries, and defense, with years worth of signed contracts and a pipeline that spans every vessel type on the water.

The technology is proven, the momentum is building, and the opportunity is enormous. The marine industry is going electric and Arc is building the platform that powers it

Who we’re looking for

As Arc's Defense Federal Account Executive, you will own a set of accounts and carry them from first conversation to signed business. You will find and open new opportunities, grow the ones already in motion, and bring in partners when it helps us win.

We're looking for someone fired up by the mission and ready to build. You'll thrive here if you move fast, take ownership, and care about the details.

This is a full-time, on-site role at our Los Angeles headquarters.

What You'll Do

• Owning a portfolio of U.S. Navy accounts. Build and run account plans, prospect for new opportunities, and expand the relationships Arc Boats already has.

• Developing trusted relationships across the customer and its partners, from program leaders to prime contractors, and represent Arc Boats with credibility and clarity.

• Understanding each customer's mission and priorities, then position Arc Boat’s technology to solve real problems and open the door with the easiest first step.

• Qualifying opportunities carefully and run them through to a win with a disciplined, repeatable sales and capture process.

• Partnering with prime contractors, teammates, and Arc Boats engineering to build compelling proposals and teaming arrangements.

• Forecasting accurately, keep your records current, and report progress and pipeline health on a regular cadence.

Minimum Qualifications

• Familiarity with government contracting or defense acquisition.

• Field sales, business development, or capture experience, ideally selling to the U.S. Navy, the Department of War, or the federal government.

• A proven track record of managing full sales cycles and consistently exceeding targets.

• Comfort building relationships inside large, complex organizations and guiding group buying decisions to a close.

• Strong discovery, presentation, and storytelling skills that connect a technical product to a customer's mission.

• The ability to manage many opportunities at once while staying focused on the accounts that matter most.

• This position requires access to information controlled under U.S. export control laws and regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR). Applicants must be a 'U.S. person' as defined by ITAR (22 CFR §120.62) — i.e., a U.S. citizen, U.S. national, lawful permanent resident, or protected individual (asylee or refugee).

Bonus Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in business, engineering, or a related field.

• Background in maritime, power and propulsion, unmanned systems, or a related technical field.

• Training in a modern sales or capture methodology (e.g., Challenger, SPIN, or Shipley), and an active or recent security clearance.

At Arc, we encourage diversity and consider all qualified applicants equally for employment, regardless of background, identity, or status. You’re always welcome to reach out even if you don’t meet many of these qualifications. Passion and aptitude make up for a lot.

What we offer

The base salary for this role is $140,000 annually

Highly competitive equity grants are included with full time offers. As well as semi-annual bonuses tied to your impact, not just your tenure.

Additionally, Arc offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:

• Healthcare benefits — 99% employer-paid medical, dental, and vision

• Parental leave — 14 weeks fully paid for birthing and non-birthing parents

• Generous time off — Highly competitive PTO with an opportunity to earn more time with tenure

• Income protection — Life and disability insurance for all employees

• Retirement savings — Traditional and Roth 401(k) access

• Water fund — $500 for you to spend each year to get out on the water, however you choose

• Professional development — $500 annual reimbursement for professional development and a monthly AI stipend

• Safety Support- Annual reimbursement for PPE, ergonomic equipment and anything that ensures we keep our crew safe

• Captain training — Training and access to take Arc boats out with friends and family

• Office perks — Daily lunches, snacks, and good coffee while onsite

• Relocation assistance — Available depending on role eligibility.

Our values

We move with urgency and build with care. We value these five things above all else:

• Ownership over both your work and the company’s success

• Empathy for colleagues and for customers

• Humility in problem solving and collaboration

• Pragmatism for navigating ambiguity quickly and sensibly

• Inclusion of different backgrounds, opinions, cultures, and perspectives.

We want people who share and embody these values. It is vital that our values align - we’d be happy to elaborate on any or all of these during the interview process.
